results.title: Structural characterization of newt tendon regeneration after complete transection: In vivo two‐photon imaging and transmission electron microscopy
results.author: Tomoka Kamiya
results.takeaway: Newt tendon regeneration after complete transection can be divided into two phases, with the early phase involving initial response to transection and the late phase focusing on maturation of regenerated collagenous tissue into new tendon.

results.title: Regeneration of Bone, Cartilage, and Tooth Following Lower Jaw Amputation in Newts.
results.author: Kento Tsubosaki
results.takeaway: Adult newts can regenerate their lower jaws, restoring bone, cartilage, and teeth after substantial loss, potentially benefiting human jaw reconstruction strategies.

results.title: Biomechanical analysis of tendon regeneration capacity of Iberian ribbed newts following transection injury: Comparison to a mouse model
results.author: F. Sato
results.takeaway: Iberian ribbed newts show remarkable tendon regeneration capacity after injury, making them a suitable model for studying tendon regeneration in adult vertebrates.

results.title: NEUROTROPHIC CONTROL OF LIMB REGENERATION IN THE NEWT *
results.author: M. Singer
results.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
results.takeaway: Neurotrophic control of limb regeneration in amphibians, particularly newts and salamanders, is crucial for restoring structure and function after amputation.

results.title: Deer antler renewal gives insights into mammalian epimorphic regeneration
results.author: Chunyi Li
results.takeaway: Deer antler renewal provides insights into mammalian epimorphic regeneration, suggesting that human epimorphic regeneration may follow a similar path to that of lower vertebrates like newt limbs.

results.title: The fine structure of tissues in the amputated‐regenerating limb of the adult newt, Diemictylus viridescens
results.author: Wesley P. Norman
results.takeaway: The adult newt's amputated forelimbs show a complex and detailed fine structure of wound epithelium, nerves, striated muscle, regeneration blastema, connective tissues, and cartilage.

results.title: Skin Wound Healing of the Adult Newt, Cynops pyrrhogaster: A Unique Re-Epithelialization and Scarless Model
results.author: Tatsuyuki Ishii
results.takeaway: Adult newts' skin regenerated exceptionally well and scarless, making them an ideal model for studying perfect skin wound healing and regeneration in postnatal humans.

results.title: Tail regeneration and other phenomena of wound healing and tissue restoration in lizards
results.author: Kathy Jacyniak
results.takeaway: Lizards exhibit unique wound healing and regeneration abilities, including the ability to regrow their entire tails and other tissues after injury, offering potential for biomedical sciences and regenerative medicine.

results.title: Chromosome-scale genome assembly reveals how repeat elements shape non-coding RNA landscapes active during newt limb regeneration
results.author: Thomas Brown
results.takeaway: Intronic repeat elements in newt genomes drive non-coding RNA biogenesis and regeneration-specific expression, providing insights into adult regeneration and developmental principles.

results.title: Spatio-temporal neural stem cell behavior leads to both perfect and imperfect structural brain regeneration in adult newts
results.author: Yuko Urata
results.takeaway: Adult newts can regenerate large parts of their brains from adult neural stem cells, with perfect regeneration taking over 1 year and regeneration phenotypes depending on wound closing.

results.title: Actin mesh in Re-epithelialization during skin regeneration in adult newt (Cynops pyrrhogaster)
results.author: Yu Liou

results.title: Regeneration of Soft Tissues Is Promoted by MMP1 Treatment after Digit Amputation in Mice
results.author: Xiaodong Mu
results.takeaway: MMP1 treatment significantly improves wound healing and regeneration of soft tissues in amputated digits of adult mice, without significantly affecting skeletal tissue elongation.

results.title: Initiation of limb regeneration: The critical steps for regenerative capacity
results.author: H. Yokoyama
results.takeaway: The early steps of wound healing and limb regeneration are crucial for determining the extent of regenerative response after limb amputation, with signaling molecules like FGF, Wnt, and BMP playing key roles.

results.title: The Regenerative Capability of the Urodele Amphibians and Its Potential for Plastic Surgery
results.author: B. Gesslbauer
results.takeaway: Newts and salamanders exhibit tremendous regenerative potential, offering new perspectives for plastic surgery and tissue regeneration improvements.

results.title: Reintegration of the regenerated and the remaining tissues during joint regeneration in the newt Cynops pyrrhogaster
results.author: Rio Tsutsumi
results.takeaway: Newt joint regeneration involves structural integration between opposing skeletal elements, resulting in a functional joint structure after amputation.

results.title: Immunohistochemical Analysis of Histone H3 Modification in Newt Tail Tissue Cells following Amputation
results.author: Jiwen Wu
results.takeaway: Newt tail regeneration involves epigenetic regulation, with increased stem cells and proliferating cells in the stump after amputation.

results.title: FGF‐stimulated tendon cells embrace a chondrogenic fate with BMP7 in newt tissue culture
results.author: Nao Sugiura
results.takeaway: FGF-stimulated tendon cells can aid in joint cartilage regeneration during functional elbow joint regeneration in newts.

results.title: Macrophages modulate fibrosis during newt lens regeneration
results.author: Georgios Tsissios
results.takeaway: Macrophages play a crucial role in newt lens regeneration by regulating fibrosis, modulating inflammation, and maintaining a proper balance of early proliferation and late apoptosis in iris pigment epithelial cells.

results.title: Comparative analysis of ear-hole closure identifies epimorphic regeneration as a discrete trait in mammals
results.author: Thomas R. Gawriluk
results.takeaway: Spiny mice and Oryctolagus cuniculus can completely regenerate tissue after injury, uniting blastema-mediated regeneration with regeneration in other vertebrates like salamanders, newts, and zebrafish.

results.title: Insights regarding skin regeneration in non-amniote vertebrates: Skin regeneration without scar formation and potential step-up to a higher level of regeneration.
results.author: Gembu Abe
results.takeaway: Fish, anurans, and urodeles can regenerate skin without scar formation, and their models can help study how skin regeneration can be stepped up to organ regeneration.

results.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Plant Regeneration.
results.author: Momoko Ikeuchi

results.title: Plant regeneration: cellular origins and molecular mechanisms
results.author: Momoko Ikeuchi

results.title: Cellular, Molecular, and Physiological Aspects of In Vitro Plant Regeneration
results.author: S. S. Bidabadi

results.title: New Insights Into Tissue Culture Plant-Regeneration Mechanisms
results.author: Y. Long

results.title: Cellular and molecular mechanisms of development and regeneration.

results.title: Assay of cyclic 3′‐5′‐monophosphate in the regenerating forelimb of the newt, Triturus
results.author: J. Jabaily
results.takeaway: Cyclic AMP concentrations in the regenerating forelimb of Triturus viridescens newt show a peak in early regeneration stages, followed by a sharp drop and a rise to a plateau similar to the unamputated limb.

results.author: Can Aztekin

results.title: Regeneration and defense: unveiling the molecular interplay in plants
results.author: Dawei Xu
results.takeaway: Plant regeneration and defense are influenced by aging, microbial interactions, and environmental cues, with microbes playing a key role in guiding these molecular decisions.

results.title: An insight into planarian regeneration
results.author: Xin-Yang Ge

results.title: Cellular and Molecular Triggers of Retinal Regeneration in Amphibians
results.author: Yuliya V Markitantova
results.takeaway: Amphibian retinal regeneration is triggered by specific signaling pathways, transcription factors, and the epigenome, potentially offering potential treatments for human retina diseases.

results.title: Cellular and Molecular Responses Unique to Major Injury Are Dispensable for Planarian Regeneration
results.author: Aneesha G Tewari
results.takeaway: Major cellular and molecular programs induced by large injuries accelerate regeneration but are not essential for regeneration itself.

results.title: The engine initiating tissue regeneration: does a common mechanism exist during evolution?
results.author: Yanmei Liu

results.title: The Molecular and Cellular Choreography of Appendage Regeneration.

results.author: A. Fehér

results.title: A Molecular Framework for Plant Regeneration
results.author: Jian Xu
results.takeaway: Laser-induced wounding in Arabidopsis roots leads to cell-fate changes, requiring PLETHORA, SHORTROOT, and SCARECROW transcription factors to stabilize new hormone distribution and promote regeneration.

results.title: Hallmarks of Regeneration
results.author: K. Poss
results.takeaway: Regeneration in various animal species involves activation of a cell source, initiation of regenerative programs, interplay with supporting cells, and control of tissue size and function.

results.title: Regeneration in Stentor coeruleus
results.author: W. Marshall
results.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
results.takeaway: Single cells can regenerate missing structures, resembling animal development and regeneration processes, and may have evolved by exploiting pre-existing subcellular developmental strategies from unicellular ancestors.

results.title: Integrated Multi-Omics Reveals Mechanism of Adventitious Buds Regeneration in In Vitro Cultures of Cinnamomum parthenoxylon
results.author: Chenglin Luo
results.takeaway: This study reveals that pluripotent callus formation in Cinnamomum parthenoxylon plants is regulated by a complex network of genes, offering valuable germplasm resources for efficient and stable genetic transformation through tissue culture.

results.title: Plant genetic transformation: achievements, current status and future prospects
results.author: Peilin Wang
results.takeaway: Plant genetic transformation technologies have advanced, advancing plant regeneration and ensuring global agricultural sustainability.

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: Hydra
results.author: M. Vogg
results.takeaway: Freshwater polyps serve as a powerful model system for studying regeneration, with recent results questioning the classical self-enhancement and long-range inhibition model and highlighting the need for integrative explanations incorporating biochemical and mechanical signaling.

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: Arabidopsis

results.takeaway: Arabidopsis serves as a model plant for studying cellular and molecular mechanisms of regeneration, providing insights into plant multi-scale regenerative potential.

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: planarians
results.author: Mario Ivanković
results.takeaway: Planarians, a group of flatworms, serve as a powerful model system for understanding the molecular and evolutionary underpinnings of regeneration.

results.title: Extraordinary model systems for regeneration.

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: Xenopus
results.author: Lauren S. Phipps
results.takeaway: Xenopus is a key model organism for regeneration research, as it can achieve scar-free healing and tissue regeneration during larval stages, offering insights into the mechanisms governing regeneration.

results.title: It Cuts Both Ways: An Annelid Model System for the Study of Regeneration in the Laboratory and in the Classroom
results.author: Veronica G. Martinez Acosta
results.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
results.takeaway: An annelid model system can effectively study regeneration, providing insights for regenerative medicine and providing a primer for biology for researchers and educators.

results.title: Establishment of an efficient Agrobacterium tumefaciens-mediated genetic transformation and regeneration system for Polygonum cuspidatum
results.author: Fan Lin

results.title: Gene regulatory programs of tissue regeneration
results.author: J. A. Goldman
results.takeaway: Understanding gene regulatory networks in tissue regeneration pathways could potentially enable targeted reactivation for treating human injuries and degenerative diseases.

results.title: Planarian Regeneration as a Model of Anatomical Homeostasis: Recent Progress in Biophysical and Computational Approaches

results.takeaway: Planarian regeneration offers valuable insights into anatomical homeostasis and regenerative medicine, with recent advances in understanding its physiological control and computational approaches.

results.author: Daniel Lobo

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: zebrafish

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: Drosophila
results.author: Donald T. Fox

results.title: A linear-encoding model explains the variability of the target morphology in regeneration
results.author: Daniel Lobo
results.journal: Journal of The Royal Society Interface

results.title: Evaluation of In Vitro Morphogenic Response of Triticum urartu, a Donor of Au Genome of Modern Wheat
results.author: D. Miroshnichenko
results.takeaway: In vitro regeneration of Triticum urartu, a donor of the Au genome of modern wheat, is possible using synthetic auxins, with Dicamba showing the highest frequency of regenerable callus production and 2,4-D allowing more plants per callus.

results.title: Regeneration or Scarring Derive from Specific Evolutionary Environmental Adaptations of the Life Cycles in Different Animals
results.author: L. Alibardi

results.title: Growth Factors in Regeneration and Regenerative Medicine: “the Cure and the Cause”
results.author: K. Kulebyakin
results.takeaway: Growth factors play a crucial role in regeneration and regenerative medicine, but their application in human tissue regeneration faces potential bottlenecks and epigenetic landscape influences.

results.title: Evolution of Regeneration in Animals: A Tangled Story
results.author: A. Elchaninov
results.takeaway: The evolution of regenerative capacity in animals is complex and not always beneficial, driven by signaling pathways and adaptive immunity advances.

results.title: Beyond Casual Resemblances: Rigorous Frameworks for Comparing Regeneration Across Species.
results.author: M. Srivastava
results.journal: Annual review of cell and developmental biology
results.takeaway: This review provides a framework for comparing regeneration across animals, focusing on gene regulatory networks, to identify unifying principles of regeneration biology across animals, benefiting evolutionary studies and human regenerative medicine.

results.title: Perspective: Appendage regeneration in amphibians and some reptiles derived from specific evolutionary histories.
results.author: L. Alibardi
results.journal: Journal of experimental zoology. Part B, Molecular and developmental evolution
results.takeaway: Amphibian regeneration and lizard regeneration are derived from specific evolutionary histories, and regenerative medicine could potentially induce limb regeneration in humans by creating soft, hyaluronate-rich blastemas.

results.title: Complex tissue regeneration in Lophuromys reveals a phylogenetic signal for enhanced regenerative ability in deomyine rodents
results.author: Brennan Riddell
results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
results.takeaway: Deomyine rodents show enhanced regenerative ability, with brush-furred mice showing musculoskeletal regeneration, while nondeomyine rodents heal ear pinna injuries via fibrotic repair with scar tissue.

results.title: Animal regeneration: ancestral character or evolutionary novelty?
results.author: J. Slack

results.title: A cross-species analysis of systemic mediators of repair and complex tissue regeneration
results.author: Julia Losner
results.takeaway: Systemic cues and circulating factors play a crucial role in tissue regeneration, and understanding their role could lead to new therapeutic avenues.

results.title: Evolutionary constraints impose multiple checkpoints that block mammalian sensory hair cell regeneration
results.author: Xiaoyi Zhang
results.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology

results.title: Conserved Genes in Highly Regenerative Metazoans Are Associated with Planarian Regeneration
results.author: S. C. Chereddy
results.takeaway: Cnidaria and Bilaterian regeneration genes play a major role in regeneration across highly regenerative Cnidaria and Bilateria species, suggesting a common molecular mechanism.

results.title: Changes in regeneration-responsive enhancers shape regenerative capacities in vertebrates
results.author: Wei Wang
results.takeaway: Changes in AP-1-enriched regeneration-responsive enhancers are a crucial source of loss of regenerative capacities in vertebrates, with caudal fin regeneration and cardiac regeneration being affected in teleost fish.

results.title: Reconsidering regeneration in metazoans: an evo-devo approach
results.author: S. Tiozzo
results.takeaway: Regeneration in metazoans may be an ancestral trait rather than independently evolved mechanisms, and understanding the conserved chronological steps can help test evolutionary hypotheses.

results.title: Childhood abuse accelerates inflammaging.
results.author: S. Entringer
results.takeaway: Childhood abuse accelerates inflammaging, with regenerative ability varying across different animal groups and an inverse relationship between immune system robustness and regeneration ability.

results.title: Evolutionary dynamics of whole-body regeneration across planarian flatworms
results.author: Miquel Vila‐Farré
results.takeaway: Planarian flatworms show multiple transitions between robust whole-body regeneration and restricted regeneration, with the Wnt pathway linked to regeneration defects and diverse roles in their reproductive systems.

results.title: Investigating the evolution and features of regeneration using cnidarians
results.author: Aide Macias-Muñoz
results.takeaway: Cnidarians provide insights into the evolution of regeneration and can be used to identify conserved cellular and molecular features that underlie differences in regeneration potential between animals.

results.title: Restoration of anterior regeneration in a planarian with limited regenerative ability
results.author: James M. Sikes
results.takeaway: Downregulation of canonical Wnt signaling in regeneration-deficient regions can restore regenerative abilities in a planarian with limited regenerative ability.

results.author: D. Stocum
results.takeaway: The complete circle rule may need modification for regenerating symmetrical hindlimbs in larval salamanders, as it fails to predict regeneration of anterior-posterior halves of thighs and posterior-posterior halves of shanks.

results.title: Regeneration of mirror symmetrical limbs in the axolotl.

results.title: Pattern regulation in a regenerating jellyfish
results.author: C. Sinigaglia

results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

results.author: Lital Shani-Zerbib

results.title: Allometry in limb regeneration and scale-invariant patterning as the basis of normal morphogenesis from different sizes of blastemas
results.author: Saya Furukawa

results.title: Pattern regulation during regeneration of embryonically produced symmetrical forelimbs in the axolotl, ambystoma mexicanum.
results.author: P. Tank

results.author: M. Casco-Robles

results.author: H. Bohn
results.journal: Journal of embryology and experimental morphology
results.takeaway: Cockroach larval legs regenerate from the medial region of the trochantin, with sclerites alone determining symmetry and polarity, and regeneration can occur at both anterior and posterior cut surfaces.

results.title: A Wnt11 and Dishevelled signaling pathway acts prior to injury to control wound polarization for the onset of planarian regeneration
results.author: David I. Gittin
results.takeaway: A Wnt11 and Dishevelled signaling pathway acts prior to injury to control wound polarization and muscle orientation in planarian regeneration, using pre-existing tissue information to determine the outcome of wound-induced signals.

results.title: Dorsoventral-mediated Shh induction is required for axolotl limb regeneration
results.author: Sakiya Yamamoto
results.takeaway: Dorsoventral contact within a blastema is crucial for limb formation in axolotls, with WNT10B and FGF2 playing key roles in inducing expression.

results.title: Live cell-lineage tracing and machine learning reveal patterns of organ regeneration
results.author: Oriol Viader-Llargués
results.takeaway: Live cell-lineage tracing and machine learning reveal how sensory organs regenerate to maintain function, with mediolateral position being the best predictor of cell-fate acquisition.

results.title: Physical forces in regeneration of cells and tissues
results.author: S. Tang
results.journal: Cold Spring Harbor perspectives in biology
results.takeaway: Physical forces play a role in wound healing and regeneration, with potential applications at both tissue and cell scales.

results.title: In preprints: retinoic acid degradation and tissue stiffness coordinate axolotl limb regeneration.
results.author: W. Masselink

results.title: On regeneration after the amputation of abnormal structures. II. Supernumerary induced limbs.
results.author: D. Newth
results.journal: Journal of embryology and experimental morphology
results.takeaway: Regenerative processes can replace abnormal structures with normal ones, but the ability to replace abnormal structures with normal ones is limited by the reversal of their original asymmetry.

results.author: L. Otsuki

results.author: Warren A. Vieira

results.author: Eugen Nacu
results.takeaway: Connective tissue cells, but not muscle cells, play a crucial role in limb regeneration and guide muscle patterning, with muscle patterning influenced by -catenin signaling.

results.title: Allometric growth in the Praying mantis Stagmatoptera biocellata
results.author: Ernesto Rodriguez

results.title: Postembryonic development of the predatory strike mechanics in a praying mantis (Insecta: Mantodea)
results.author: Thies H. Büscher

results.title: Allometric growth in two species of Ectobius (Dictyoptera: Blattidae)
results.author: V. Brown
results.takeaway: Allometric growth in Ectobius species shows significant variations, with few structures growing by simple allometry, and the choice of reference dimension and statistical model affects growth data estimates.

results.title: Manual of praying mantis morphology, nomenclature, and practices (Insecta, Mantodea)
results.author: Sydney K. Brannoch
results.takeaway: This study proposes new standards for praying mantis morphology, standardized foreleg femoral and tibial spine presentation, and provides guidelines for proper specimen preservation and research methods.

results.title: Allometry of Ingestion Among Habitat Mimicking Praying Mantises
results.author: C. Oufiero
results.takeaway: Large praying mantises can ingest more resources than needed based on their metabolic rate, potentially impacting their role in the ecosystem.

results.title: A multivariate analysis of postembryonic growth in two species of Ectobius (Dictyoptera: Blattidae)
results.author: R. G. Davies
results.takeaway: Postembryonic growth in Ectobius species shows four or five orthogonal patterns, with the major component being a set of independently definable allometric growth ratios.

results.title: Allometric growth in reef-building corals
results.author: M. Dornelas
results.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences
results.takeaway: Coral growth rates can be best predicted from colony size and morphology, rather than species, simplifying the task of projecting community responses to disturbance and climate change.

results.title: Comparative Mitogenomic Analyses of Praying Mantises (Dictyoptera, Mantodea): Origin and Evolution of Unusual Intergenic Gaps
results.author: Hong-li Zhang

results.title: Complete mitochondrial genomes of four species of praying mantises (Dictyoptera, Mantidae) with ribosomal second structure, evolutionary and phylogenetic analyses
results.author: Yan Shi

results.title: Allometric scaling laws linking biomass and rooting depth vary across ontogeny and functional groups in tropical dry forest lianas and trees.

results.title: Allometric Scaling of Metabolism, Growth, and Activity in Whole Colonies of the Seed‐Harvester Ant Pogonomyrmex californicus

results.author: A. Chtioui

results.author: Hangwei Liu

results.author: C. Polidori

results.title: Size and shape: the developmental regulation of static allometry in insects

results.title: Exploring the role of insulin signaling in relative growth: a case study on wing-body scaling in Lepidoptera.

results.title: Utilizing geometric morphometrics to investigate gene function during organ growth: Insights through the study of beetle horn shape allometry
results.author: P. Rohner
results.takeaway: Geometric morphometry can help distinguish between genes primarily affecting relative trait growth and those primarily affecting alternative developmental processes.

results.title: Structure and molecular basis of spermatid elongation in the Drosophila testis
results.author: Qiuru Huang
results.takeaway: Spermatid elongation in the testis involves microtubule-based axoneme assembly, individualization complex formation, and mitochondria maintenance, which are crucial for male fertility.

results.title: A muscle-epidermis-glia signaling axis sustains synaptic specificity during allometric growth in Caenorhabditis elegans
results.author: Jiale Fan
results.takeaway: A muscle-epidermis-glia signaling axis maintains synaptic specificity during allometric growth in Caenorhabditis elegans, preserving the synaptic pattern established during embryogenesis.

results.title: Developmental model of static allometry in holometabolous insects
results.author: A. Shingleton
results.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences
results.takeaway: The slope of nutritional static allometries in Drosophila melanogaster is controlled by the relative sensitivity of an organ's growth rate to changes in nutrition, and the relative duration of development when nutrition affects an organ's final size.

results.title: The worldwide allometric relationship in anatomical structures for plant roots
results.author: Yue Zhang
results.takeaway: Root allometry, where cortex thickness increases faster than stele radius with increasing root diameter, is common in plants and varies greatly across species, with implications for understanding plant ecology and physiology.

results.title: Single particle tracking-based reaction progress kinetic analysis reveals a series of molecular mechanisms of cetuximab-induced EGFR processes in a single living cell
results.author: Do-Hyeon Kim
results.takeaway: Using single particle tracking-based reaction progress kinetic analysis (sptRPKA), researchers identified a previously unknown intermediate state responsible for the selective targeting of cetuximab-induced EGFR endocytosis to cancer cells.

results.title: Streptomyces morphogenetics: dissecting differentiation in a filamentous bacterium
results.author: K. Flärdh
results.takeaway: Morphological differentiation in Streptomyces is closely integrated with growth, cell-cycle processes, and multicellular behavior, involving hormone-like extracellular signaling and diverse secondary metabolism.

results.title: Cellular Allometry of Mitochondrial Functionality Establishes the Optimal Cell Size
results.author: Teemu P. Miettinen
results.takeaway: Optimal cell size is determined by uncoupling mitochondrial content and functional scaling, resulting in maximized cellular fitness and proliferative capacity.

results.title: Growth polarity and cell division in Streptomyces.
results.author: K. Flärdh
results.takeaway: Streptomyces DivIVA protein and nucleoid migration contribute to bacterial growth polarity and cell division, leading to single-chromosome spores.

results.title: Bioelectric-calcineurin signaling module regulates allometric growth and size of the zebrafish fin
results.author: Jacob M. Daane
results.takeaway: The potassium channel kcnk5b plays a key role in regulating allometric growth and size of zebrafish fins, integrating calcineurin's growth effects and maintaining proper proportionality during development.

results.title: Allometries and the morphogenesis of the molluscan shell: a quantitative and theoretical model.
results.author: Séverine Urdy
results.journal: Journal of experimental zoology. Part B, Molecular and developmental evolution
results.takeaway: Growth rate has a significant impact on shell shape and the relationship between growth increment size and spiral geometry.

results.title: Allometry and size control: what can studies of body size regulation teach us about the evolution of morphological scaling relationships?
results.author: C. Mirth
results.takeaway: Insects regulate organ and body sizes in response to environmental conditions, such as nutritional availability, and combining developmental insights with population genetics can help understand the evolution of morphological allometry.

results.title: A Hyperspace Model to Decipher the Genetic Architecture of Developmental Processes: Allometry Meets Ontogeny
results.author: R. Wu
results.takeaway: This study presents a high-dimensional statistical model for studying the genetic regulation of ontogenetic growth and shape, integrating growth curves and developmental allometry into genetic mapping.

results.title: Integration and the Developmental Genetics of Allometry.
results.author: B. Hallgrímsson
results.takeaway: Allometric variation in craniofacial shape is highly polygenic, with distinct but overlapping patterns convergent on a common genetic basis, challenging the view of allometry as a distinct phenomenon from morphological integration.

results.title: Computational identification of genes modulating stem height–diameter allometry
results.author: Libo Jiang
results.takeaway: Functional mapping can effectively identify genes that control stem height-diameter allometry in trees, potentially improving our understanding of genetic control mechanisms in trade-offs between assimilate allocation to different growth parts.

results.title: Developmental origin of limb size variation in lizards
results.author: R. Andrews
results.takeaway: Species-specific differences in limb and tail length emerge abruptly during embryonic development, with genetic mechanisms influencing adaptive variation in limb size in squamate reptiles.

results.title: A highly conserved ontogenetic limb allometry and its evolutionary significance in the adaptive radiation of Anolis lizards
results.author: Nathalie Feiner
results.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences
results.takeaway: The remarkable diversification of locomotor specialists in lizards is accessible through changes independent from ontogenetic growth trajectories, likely due to modifications in early stages of limb development.

results.title: A Computational Model for Inferring QTL Control Networks Underlying Developmental Covariation
results.author: Libo Jiang
results.takeaway: This study identifies "pioneering" and "maintaining" QTLs in a tree species, mei, to better understand developmental covariation and its genetic architecture.

results.title: Why does allometry evolve so slowly?
results.author: D. Houle
results.takeaway: Natural selection acts to maintain allometric relationships, but the slow evolution of morphological allometry may be due to selection on multiple pleiotropic effects.

results.title: A Conceptual Framework for Mapping Quantitative Trait Loci Regulating Ontogenetic Allometry
results.author: Hongying Li
results.takeaway: This study developed a framework model for unraveling the genetic machinery for ontogenetic changes of allometry, enabling better insights into developmental patterns and processes in organisms.

results.title: The growth factor BMP11 is required for the development and evolution of a male exaggerated weapon and its associated fighting behavior in a water strider
results.author: William Toubiana
results.takeaway: BMP11 plays a crucial role in the development and evolution of male exaggerated weapons and intense fighting behavior in the water strider Microvelia longipes.

results.title: Insect Flight Energetics and the Evolution of Size, Form, and Function
results.author: Charles-A. Darveau
results.takeaway: Insect flight energetics are influenced by body size, wing proportions, and metabolic properties, with larger insects having slower wingbeat frequencies and wing proportions affecting energy requirements.

results.title: Macroevolution of Steep Interspecific Metabolic Allometry in an Old Insect Order
results.author: D. Schönberger
results.takeaway: Metabolic allometries in Odonata (dragonflies and damselflies) can and do evolve, challenging traditional allometric theories and suggesting that body size evolution is influenced by aerobic demands rather than cell size.

results.title: The morphological allometry of four closely related and coexisting insect species reveals adaptation to the mean and variability of the resource size
results.author: E. Fleurot
results.takeaway: Morphological allometry in four insect species reveals adaptation to the mean and variability of resource size, with the smallest species showing the most variable rostrum length to match resource variability over time.

results.title: Can multitrophic interactions shape morphometry, allometry, and fluctuating asymmetry of seed-feeding insects?
results.author: T. Oliveira
results.takeaway: Multitrophic interactions in food webs can shape the development of seed-feeding insects, with variations in allometric slopes and morphological structure changes depending on factors tested.

results.title: Static and evolutionary allometry in the Italian endemic ant species Cataglyphis italica (Emery 1906)
results.author: M. Centorame
results.takeaway: Longer legs relative to body size in Cataglyphis italica ants may be an adaptation to more arid environmental conditions, enhancing foraging efficiency.

results.title: Thermodynamics Constrains Allometric Scaling of Optimal Development Time in Insects
results.author: M. Dillon
results.takeaway: Insect development time scales with body mass to the quarter power, with warm-adapted species developing more quickly regardless of body size, supporting the "hotter is better" hypothesis.

results.title: The scaling and allometry of organ size associated with miniaturization in insects: A case study for Coleoptera and Hymenoptera
results.author: A. Polilov
results.takeaway: Most insect organs can scale and maintain their organization, but reproductive and nervous systems increase in volume as body size decreases, limiting miniaturization in insects.

results.title: Allometric relationships shape foreleg evolution of long‐legged oil bees (Melittidae: Rediviva)
results.author: A. Melin
results.takeaway: Oil-collecting bee foreleg evolution is influenced by the variability of the allometric intercept and adaptation to host plants, with forelegs not tracking spur length perfectly.

results.title: The origin and maintenance of metabolic allometry in animals
results.author: C. R. White
results.takeaway: The genetic correlation between mass and metabolic rate is strong and positive in insects, birds, and mammals, suggesting persistent multivariate selection over long periods of time.

results.title: Ontogenetic and static allometry of hind femur length in the cricket Gryllus bimaculatus (Orthoptera: Gryllidae) with implications for evo-devo of morphological scaling
results.author: Jakke Neiro
results.takeaway: The cricket Gryllus bimaculatus has a slightly positive ontogenetic allometry for hind femur length, supporting the size-grain hypothesis in Orthoptera, but ontogenetic allometries may not predict evolutionary allometries.

results.title: Exploring the role of insulin signaling in relative growth: a case study on wing-body scaling in Lepidoptera.
results.author: Kenneth Z McKenna
results.takeaway: Insulin signaling plays a role in wing-body scaling in Lepidoptera, influencing the development and evolution of organismal forms.

results.title: Evolution and Regulation of Decoupled Dimorphic Scaling Patterns in Ants
results.author: Erica Vong
results.takeaway: Ants in the genus Pheidole exhibit an unexpected scaling pattern, with antennal sizing being identical between worker and soldier, and its regulation influenced by social environment, developmental hormones, and interorgan signaling.

results.title: Evolution of multivariate wing allometry in schizophoran flies (Diptera: Schizophora)
results.author: P. Rohner
results.takeaway: Wing shape variation in Schizophora flies is primarily driven by size-related changes, suggesting a shared developmental program underlying size-dependent phenotypic plasticity across species.

facets.q: What is the molecular basis of positional memory in amphibian limb regeneration?

6.state: Positional memory is central to limb-regeneration research: axolotl studies show it is stabilized by a positive-feedback loop, reprogrammable by retinoic acid, and encoded in segment-specific H3K27me3. Why an edge-restricted defect yields a heteromorphic structure is exactly this positional-information problem.

results.title: Molecular basis of positional memory in limb regeneration
results.author: L. Otsuki
results.takeaway: Positional memory in limb regeneration in axolotls is stabilized by a positive-feedback loop, and can be reprogrammed more easily from anterior to posterior direction, impacting tissue engineering.

results.title: Positional Memory in Vertebrate Regeneration: A Century's Insights from the Salamander Limb.
results.author: L. Otsuki
results.journal: Cold Spring Harbor perspectives in biology
results.takeaway: Positional memory in vertebrate regeneration, as demonstrated in the salamander limb model, could lead to improved tissue repair and tissue engineering for therapeutic purposes.

results.title: Molecular basis for positional memory and its reprogrammability in limb regeneration
results.author: L. Otsuki
results.takeaway: A positive feedback mechanism in limb regeneration allows for the reprogramming of positional memory, allowing for more easily altered limb identities in tissue engineering.

results.title: Use of retinoids to analyze the cellular basis of positional memory in regenerating amphibian limbs.
results.author: D. Stocum
results.journal: Biochemistry and cell biology = Biochimie et biologie cellulaire
results.takeaway: Retinoids, such as retinoic acid, can modify positional memory in amphibian limb regeneration, potentially through a cellular RA-binding protein.

results.title: A chromatin code for limb segment identity in axolotl limb regeneration.
results.author: Akane Kawaguchi
results.takeaway: Axolotl limb connective tissue cells use segment-specific levels of histone H3K27me3 as an intrinsic segment information code, supporting an ancient, conserved regeneration program.

results.title: Hierarchical pattern formation during amphibian limb regeneration
results.author: Warren A. Vieira
results.takeaway: Hierarchical pattern formation in amphibian limb regeneration involves four basic steps: cell memory, communication, induction of molecular signaling centers, and specialized cell types interpreting signals to restore the limb.

results.title: Lmx1b activation in axolotl limb regeneration
results.author: Sakiya Yamamoto
results.takeaway: Lmx1b activation in axolotl limb regeneration is triggered by nerve presence, enabling positional memory to be reactivated and triggering limb regeneration.

results.title: Stability and plasticity of positional memory during limb regeneration in Ambystoma mexicanum
results.author: R. Iwata
results.takeaway: Positional memories on anteroposterior and dorsoventral axes are relatively stable during limb regeneration in Ambystoma mexicanum, even though cellular differentiation is reprogrammed.

results.title: The Use of Retinoids to Explore the Cellular and Molecular Basis of Positional Memory in Regenerating Amphibian Limbs
results.author: D. Stocum
results.takeaway: Retinoids can help explore the cellular and molecular basis of positional memory in amphibian limb regeneration, potentially revealing intrinsic or extrinsic mechanisms.

results.title: ECM-mediated positional cues are able to induce pattern, but not new positional information, during axolotl limb regeneration
results.author: Warren A. Vieira
results.takeaway: ECM-mediated positional cues play a role in Type-2 communication during axolotl limb regeneration, influencing cell arrangement without new positional information.

results.title: Genetic reprogramming of positional memory in a regenerating appendage
results.author: Ying-Ting Wang
results.takeaway: Positional information in regenerating tissues is malleable, with zebrafish tailfins retaining memory of their new size when disrupted during a 48-hour window of regeneration.

results.title: In preprints: cellular memory - the tension between old and new identities in the blastema.
results.author: Benjamin Tajer
results.takeaway: Hand2 expression in the posterior limb of axolotl salamanders serves as a seat of memory for posteriorizing activity during limb development and regeneration, potentially enforcing a fixed posterior identity during regeneration.

results.title: Transcriptional Correlates of Proximal-Distal Identity and Regeneration Timing in Axolotl Limbs
results.author: S. R. Voss

results.takeaway: Positional memory in axolotl limbs is linked to gene expression patterns, which explain the similar regeneration time for proximal and distal amputations.

results.title: Positional information in axolotl and mouse limb extracellular matrix is mediated via heparan sulfate and fibroblast growth factor during limb regeneration in the axolotl (Ambystoma mexicanum)

results.title: Limb blastema cell: A stem cell for morphological regeneration
results.author: K. Tamura
results.takeaway: Limb blastema cells play a crucial role in morphological regeneration, providing insights into creating three-dimensional morphology during regeneration processes.

results.title: The regeneration of positional information in the amphibian limb.
results.author: M. Maden
results.takeaway: The amphibian limb regeneration process follows five simple rules, with the cell surface playing a crucial role in positional information regeneration and development.

results.title: Transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic landscape of positional memory in the caudal fin of zebrafish
results.author: Jeremy S. Rabinowitz
results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
results.takeaway: Positional memory in zebrafish caudal fins relies on complex overlapping expression patterns for hundreds of molecules involved in diverse cellular functions, aiding future studies on regeneration.

results.author: M. Kragl

results.title: Modeling proximalisation in axolotl limb regeneration
results.author: Hernan Arce

results.title: [Regulation of the spatial organization of the regenerating extremity in amphibians].

results.author: Bana Abolibdeh
results.takeaway: Centronuclear myopathy (CNM) is a disorder involving impaired organelle communication and structural crosstalk, requiring a comprehensive, multi-target approach for full phenotypic rescue across affected tissues.

results.author: Yilan Zhang

results.author: K. Kraft

results.author: Steven J. Foltz

results.author: Marie Goret

results.author: É. Vincent

results.title: Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type R2 manifesting as fetal growth restriction in a woman with two pregnancies: a case report
results.author: Kaiyu Fu

results.title: Morphological patterns in limb deficiencies and duplications.

results.title: Plant genetic transformation: achievements, current status and future prospects

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: Hydra

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: Arabidopsis
results.author: Mabel Maria Mathew
results.takeaway: Arabidopsis serves as a model plant for studying cellular and molecular mechanisms of regeneration, providing insights into plant multi-scale regenerative potential.

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: planarians
results.author: Mario Ivanković
results.takeaway: Planarians, a group of flatworms, serve as a powerful model system for understanding the molecular and evolutionary underpinnings of regeneration.

results.title: Extraordinary model systems for regeneration.

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: Xenopus
results.author: Lauren S. Phipps
results.takeaway: Xenopus is a key model organism for regeneration research, as it can achieve scar-free healing and tissue regeneration during larval stages, offering insights into the mechanisms governing regeneration.

results.title: It Cuts Both Ways: An Annelid Model System for the Study of Regeneration in the Laboratory and in the Classroom
results.author: Veronica G. Martinez Acosta
results.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
results.takeaway: An annelid model system can effectively study regeneration, providing insights for regenerative medicine and providing a primer for biology for researchers and educators.

results.title: Establishment of an efficient Agrobacterium tumefaciens-mediated genetic transformation and regeneration system for Polygonum cuspidatum
results.author: Fan Lin
results.takeaway: Our efficient Agrobacterium tumefaciens-mediated genetic transformation and regeneration system for Polygonum cuspidatum, a valuable medicinal plant, effectively regenerates and genetically transforms it.

results.title: An insight into planarian regeneration
results.author: Xin-Yang Ge
results.takeaway: Planarian regeneration is regulated by diverse molecular factors and cellular signaling pathways, with neoblasts playing a crucial role in tissue regeneration and morphology maintenance.

results.title: Gene regulatory programs of tissue regeneration
results.author: J. A. Goldman
results.takeaway: Understanding gene regulatory networks in tissue regeneration pathways could potentially enable targeted reactivation for treating human injuries and degenerative diseases.

results.title: Animal regeneration in the era of transcriptomics
results.author: Loïc Bideau
results.takeaway: Recent data on animal regeneration models has identified key shared mechanisms, shedding light on the evolution of regeneration and its control mechanisms.

results.title: Planarian Regeneration as a Model of Anatomical Homeostasis: Recent Progress in Biophysical and Computational Approaches
results.author: M. Levin
results.takeaway: Planarian regeneration offers valuable insights into anatomical homeostasis and regenerative medicine, with recent advances in understanding its physiological control and computational approaches.

results.title: Modeling Planarian Regeneration: A Primer for Reverse-Engineering the Worm
results.author: Daniel Lobo
results.takeaway: This paper presents a review of planarian regeneration, focusing on key patterning properties and signal exchanges, to facilitate collaborations between biology and the information sciences.

results.title: Establishment of a leaf regeneration system and its molecular basis in Poplar 741
results.author: Lingyun Liu

results.title: New Insights Into Tissue Culture Plant-Regeneration Mechanisms
results.author: Y. Long
results.takeaway: Tissue culture plant regeneration can be influenced by environmental factors, such as explant sources, basal culture medium, growth regulators, and light/dark treatment, enhancing plant micropropagation and genetic modification.

results.title: Molecular and Cellular Basis of Regeneration and Tissue Repair
results.author: J. Slack

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: zebrafish

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: Drosophila

results.author: D. Miroshnichenko

results.title: Regeneration or Scarring Derive from Specific Evolutionary Environmental Adaptations of the Life Cycles in Different Animals
results.author: L. Alibardi

results.title: Growth Factors in Regeneration and Regenerative Medicine: “the Cure and the Cause”
results.author: K. Kulebyakin
results.takeaway: Growth factors play a crucial role in regeneration and regenerative medicine, but their application in human tissue regeneration faces potential bottlenecks and epigenetic landscape influences.

results.title: Evolution of Regeneration in Animals: A Tangled Story
results.author: A. Elchaninov
results.takeaway: The evolution of regenerative capacity in animals is complex and not always beneficial, driven by signaling pathways and adaptive immunity advances.

results.title: Beyond Casual Resemblances: Rigorous Frameworks for Comparing Regeneration Across Species.
results.author: M. Srivastava
results.journal: Annual review of cell and developmental biology
results.takeaway: This review provides a framework for comparing regeneration across animals, focusing on gene regulatory networks, to identify unifying principles of regeneration biology across animals, benefiting evolutionary studies and human regenerative medicine.

results.title: Perspective: Appendage regeneration in amphibians and some reptiles derived from specific evolutionary histories.
results.author: L. Alibardi
results.journal: Journal of experimental zoology. Part B, Molecular and developmental evolution
results.takeaway: Amphibian regeneration and lizard regeneration are derived from specific evolutionary histories, and regenerative medicine could potentially induce limb regeneration in humans by creating soft, hyaluronate-rich blastemas.

results.title: Complex tissue regeneration in Lophuromys reveals a phylogenetic signal for enhanced regenerative ability in deomyine rodents

results.title: Animal regeneration: ancestral character or evolutionary novelty?

results.title: Hallmarks of Regeneration

results.title: A cross-species analysis of systemic mediators of repair and complex tissue regeneration
results.author: Julia Losner

results.title: Evolutionary constraints impose multiple checkpoints that block mammalian sensory hair cell regeneration

results.title: Conserved Genes in Highly Regenerative Metazoans Are Associated with Planarian Regeneration

results.author: Wei Wang

results.title: Reconsidering regeneration in metazoans: an evo-devo approach
results.author: S. Tiozzo
results.takeaway: Regeneration in metazoans may be an ancestral trait rather than independently evolved mechanisms, and understanding the conserved chronological steps can help test evolutionary hypotheses.

results.title: Childhood abuse accelerates inflammaging.

results.title: SnoRNAs may accelerate protein synthesis for the rapid growth of the regenerating tail blastema in the lizard Podarcis muralis

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: planarians

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: Hydra

results.title: Extraordinary model systems for regeneration.

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: Arabidopsis

results.title: Gene regulatory programs of tissue regeneration
results.author: J. A. Goldman
results.takeaway: Understanding gene regulatory networks in tissue regeneration pathways could potentially enable targeted reactivation for treating human injuries and degenerative diseases.

results.title: It Cuts Both Ways: An Annelid Model System for the Study of Regeneration in the Laboratory and in the Classroom
results.author: Veronica G. Martinez Acosta

results.title: An insight into planarian regeneration

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: Xenopus

results.title: Modeling Planarian Regeneration: A Primer for Reverse-Engineering the Worm

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: salamanders
results.author: A. Joven

results.title: Molecular Determinants of in vitro Plant Regeneration: Prospects for Enhanced Manipulation of Lettuce (Lactuca sativa L.)

results.title: The cellular and molecular basis for planarian regeneration
results.author: P. Reddien

results.title: Planarian Regeneration as a Model of Anatomical Homeostasis: Recent Progress in Biophysical and Computational Approaches
results.author: M. Levin
results.takeaway: Planarian regeneration offers valuable insights into anatomical homeostasis and regenerative medicine, with recent advances in understanding its physiological control and computational approaches.

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: zebrafish
results.author: Ines J. Marques
results.takeaway: Zebrafish are an accessible model organism for studying regeneration, providing insights into tissue recovery strategies for species with poor regenerative capacity.

results.title: Establishment of an efficient Agrobacterium tumefaciens-mediated genetic transformation and regeneration system for Polygonum cuspidatum
results.author: Fan Lin
results.takeaway: Our efficient Agrobacterium tumefaciens-mediated genetic transformation and regeneration system for Polygonum cuspidatum, a valuable medicinal plant, effectively regenerates and genetically transforms it.

results.title: A linear-encoding model explains the variability of the target morphology in regeneration
results.author: Daniel Lobo
results.journal: Journal of The Royal Society Interface

results.title: Cellular and Molecular Basis of Liver Regeneration
results.author: Sushant Bangru

results.title: Unraveling Tissue Regeneration Pathways Using Chemical Genetics*

results.title: A cross-species analysis of systemic mediators of repair and complex tissue regeneration
results.author: Julia Losner
results.takeaway: Systemic cues and circulating factors play a crucial role in tissue regeneration, and understanding their role could lead to new therapeutic avenues.

results.title: Establishment of a leaf regeneration system and its molecular basis in Poplar 741

results.title: Regeneration or Scarring Derive from Specific Evolutionary Environmental Adaptations of the Life Cycles in Different Animals
results.author: L. Alibardi

results.title: Growth Factors in Regeneration and Regenerative Medicine: “the Cure and the Cause”
results.author: K. Kulebyakin

results.title: Animal regeneration in the era of transcriptomics

results.author: A. Elchaninov
results.takeaway: The evolution of regenerative capacity in animals is complex and not always beneficial, driven by signaling pathways and adaptive immunity advances.

results.title: Animal regeneration: ancestral character or evolutionary novelty?
results.author: J. Slack

results.title: Complex tissue regeneration in Lophuromys reveals a phylogenetic signal for enhanced regenerative ability in deomyine rodents

results.title: Evolution, comparative biology and ontogeny of vertebrate heart regeneration
results.author: Céline J. Vivien

results.title: Enduring questions in regenerative biology and the search for answers
results.author: A. Seifert

results.title: Regenerative medicine, organ bioengineering and transplantation
results.author: Lauren Edgar

results.title: Reconsidering regeneration in metazoans: an evo-devo approach
results.author: S. Tiozzo
results.takeaway: Regeneration in metazoans may be an ancestral trait rather than independently evolved mechanisms, and understanding the conserved chronological steps can help test evolutionary hypotheses.

results.title: The loss of regeneration competency in the animal kingdom at the expense of immunity: A journey in retrospect.
results.author: Satadal Adhikary
results.takeaway: The robustness of immune systems in animals is generally linked to a decrease in regenerative ability, with some species having a limited capacity for regeneration.

results.title: Evolutionary constraints impose multiple checkpoints that block mammalian sensory hair cell regeneration
results.author: Xiaoyi Zhang

results.title: Regeneration in anamniotes was replaced by regengrow and scarring in amniotes after land colonization and the evolution of terrestrial biological cycles
results.author: L. Alibardi
results.takeaway: Vertebrates evolved terrestrial lifecycles, limiting regeneration, and regenerative medicine should consider diverse developmental pathways before introducing "anamniote regenerative genes" in amniotes.

results.title: Changes in regeneration-responsive enhancers shape regenerative capacities in vertebrates
results.author: Wei Wang
results.takeaway: Changes in AP-1-enriched regeneration-responsive enhancers are a crucial source of loss of regenerative capacities in vertebrates, with caudal fin regeneration and cardiac regeneration being affected in teleost fish.

results.title: Evolutionary dynamics of whole-body regeneration across planarian flatworms
results.author: Miquel Vila‐Farré
results.takeaway: Planarian flatworms show multiple transitions between robust whole-body regeneration and restricted regeneration, with the Wnt pathway linked to regeneration defects and diverse roles in their reproductive systems.

results.title: Understanding Liver Regeneration: From Mechanisms to Regenerative Medicine.
results.author: H. Gilgenkrantz
results.takeaway: Understanding liver regeneration mechanisms may help patients with chronic liver diseases and inform novel approaches for regenerative medicine.

results.title: Mechanisms of Regeneration and Fibrosis in the Endometrium
results.author: Claire J. Ang

results.takeaway: The endometrium serves as a powerful model for regeneration in mammals, but some assaults can lead to scarring, potentially contributing to infertility.

results.title: Regulation and phylogeny of skeletal muscle regeneration.
results.author: Meryem B. Baghdadi
results.takeaway: Skeletal muscle regeneration involves a complex interaction between stem cells, progeny, and stromal cells, which is crucial for successful repair and re-establishing homeostasis after injury.

results.title: Liver Regeneration
results.author: G. Michalopoulos
results.takeaway: Liver regeneration restores hepatic mass and preserves normal liver histology in adult animals, utilizing specific stimuli and feedback loops to maintain metabolic support.

results.title: Comparative regenerative mechanisms across different mammalian tissues
results.author: S. Iismaa
results.takeaway: Recent insights into molecular mechanisms of regeneration in various mammalian tissues show potential for future regenerative therapies, despite constraints like immune responses, extracellular matrix composition, age, injury type, and physiological adaptations.

results.title: PPARβ/δ: Linking Metabolism to Regeneration
results.author: Ajit Magadum
results.takeaway: PPAR/ plays a crucial role in wound healing and regeneration in mammals, including skin, bone, and liver, and may be a promising target for promoting human organ repair.

results.title: Regeneration in Stentor coeruleus
results.author: W. Marshall
results.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
results.takeaway: Single cells can regenerate missing structures, resembling animal development and regeneration processes, and may have evolved by exploiting pre-existing subcellular developmental strategies from unicellular ancestors.

results.title: Comparative aspects of animal regeneration.
results.author: J. Brockes
results.journal: Annual review of cell and developmental biology
results.takeaway: Animal regeneration involves wound epithelium formation, regenerative progenitor cells, and morphogenesis, with common mechanisms in both vertebrates and invertebrates, and potential evolutionary origins.

results.title: Advances in signaling in vertebrate regeneration as a prelude to regenerative medicine.
results.author: Cristi L. Stoick-Cooper
results.takeaway: Understanding shared signaling pathways in vertebrate regeneration can accelerate the development of regenerative medicine therapies for organ and appendage regeneration in humans.

results.title: The Diversity of Muscles and Their Regenerative Potential across Animals
results.author: L. Zullo
results.takeaway: Muscle regeneration in metazoans reveals conserved and divergent cellular and molecular mechanisms, highlighting the importance of using non-canonical animal models for molecular studies.

results.title: Bridging the regeneration gap: genetic insights from diverse animal models
results.author: A. S. Alvarado
results.takeaway: Genetic tools in diverse animal models have significantly improved our understanding of animal regenerative biology, revealing similarities and differences among various species, with implications for regenerative medicine and stem-cell biology.

results.title: Molecular and Cellular Basis of Regeneration and Tissue Repair
results.author: J. Slack
results.takeaway: The Xenopus tadpole is a suitable model organism for regeneration research due to its suitability for micromanipulative procedures and transgenic methods, enabling precise gene activation or inhibition in specific tissue types.

results.title: Insights into regeneration tool box: An animal model approach.
results.author: A. Mehta
results.takeaway: Advancements in genetic engineering and tissue engineering can potentially enhance regeneration capabilities in animals with limited regeneration properties, potentially benefiting regenerative medicine and stem cell biology.

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: Hydra
results.author: M. Vogg
results.takeaway: Freshwater polyps serve as a powerful model system for studying regeneration, with recent results questioning the classical self-enhancement and long-range inhibition model and highlighting the need for integrative explanations incorporating biochemical and mechanical signaling.

results.title: Distinct patterns of gene expression during regeneration and asexual reproduction in the annelid Pristina leidyi
results.author: Irene del Olmo
results.journal: Journal of Experimental Zoology. Part B, Molecular and Developmental Evolution
results.takeaway: The molecular mechanisms underlying anterior regeneration and asexual reproduction in annelids are conserved across metazoans, with 291 genes upregulated during regeneration and 130 genes upregulated during asexual reproduction.

results.title: It Cuts Both Ways: An Annelid Model System for the Study of Regeneration in the Laboratory and in the Classroom
results.author: Veronica G. Martinez Acosta
results.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
results.takeaway: An annelid model system can effectively study regeneration, providing insights for regenerative medicine and providing a primer for biology for researchers and educators.

results.title: The zebrafish as a model for complex tissue regeneration
results.author: M. Gemberling
results.takeaway: Zebrafish serve as a valuable model system for understanding tissue regeneration mechanisms and providing guidance for potential regenerative strategies in mammals.

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: Xenopus
results.author: Lauren S. Phipps
results.takeaway: Xenopus is a key model organism for regeneration research, as it can achieve scar-free healing and tissue regeneration during larval stages, offering insights into the mechanisms governing regeneration.

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: zebrafish
results.author: Ines J. Marques
results.takeaway: Zebrafish are an accessible model organism for studying regeneration, providing insights into tissue recovery strategies for species with poor regenerative capacity.

results.title: Regeneration Genetics
results.author: Chen-Hui Chen
results.takeaway: Genetic approaches are revolutionizing our understanding of regeneration mechanisms in animals, potentially revolutionizing regenerative medicine.

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: Drosophila
results.author: Donald T. Fox
results.takeaway: Drosophila models have become a powerful tool for studying regeneration in damaged tissues and organs, with precision approaches accelerating progress in this field.

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: salamanders
results.author: A. Joven
results.takeaway: Salamanders are key models for regeneration, demonstrating remarkable abilities to regrow tissues, organs, and even whole body parts, providing insights into cell, tissue, and organ regeneration mechanisms.

results.title: Molecular genetic system for regenerative studies using newts
results.author: Toshinori Hayashi
results.takeaway: The Iberian ribbed newt (Pleurodeles waltl) is a suitable model animal for studying regeneration using molecular genetics, with comparable abilities to Japanese common newts and a method for efficient transgenesis.

results.title: Cellular and molecular processes of regeneration, with special emphasis on fish fins
results.author: Y. Nakatani
results.takeaway: Understanding the regeneration mechanisms in teleost fish, particularly fish fins, can help rationalize tissue and organ regeneration approaches in mammals.

results.title: The cell biology of regeneration
results.author: Ryan S. King
results.takeaway: Regeneration of complex structures after injury involves diverse cellular processes, including wound healing, cell death, dedifferentiation, and stem cell proliferation, and integrating polarity and positional identity cues with preexisting body structures.

results.title: Regeneration or Scarring Derive from Specific Evolutionary Environmental Adaptations of the Life Cycles in Different Animals
results.author: L. Alibardi
results.takeaway: Regeneration in aquatic animals is influenced by the evolution of larval and intense metamorphic transformations, while terrestrial species have lost most of their regeneration ability due to modified genetic networks.

results.title: EvoRegen in animals: Time to uncover deep conservation or convergence of adult stem cell evolution and regenerative processes.
results.author: Alvina G. Lai
results.takeaway: Regenerative ability in animals evolves through changes in the maintenance of embryogenic stem cells into adult life, with some highly regenerative animals harboring adult stem cells that overlap with germline stem cells.

results.title: Growth Factors in Regeneration and Regenerative Medicine: “the Cure and the Cause”
results.author: K. Kulebyakin
results.takeaway: Growth factors play a crucial role in regeneration and regenerative medicine, but their application in human tissue regeneration faces potential bottlenecks and epigenetic landscape influences.

results.title: Perspective: Appendage regeneration in amphibians and some reptiles derived from specific evolutionary histories.
results.author: L. Alibardi
results.journal: Journal of experimental zoology. Part B, Molecular and developmental evolution
results.takeaway: Amphibian regeneration and lizard regeneration are derived from specific evolutionary histories, and regenerative medicine could potentially induce limb regeneration in humans by creating soft, hyaluronate-rich blastemas.

results.title: Evolution, comparative biology and ontogeny of vertebrate heart regeneration
results.author: Céline J. Vivien
results.takeaway: Cardiac regeneration in adult mammals is limited due to adaptations during aquatic to terrestrial life and birth, and correlates with low metabolic state, inability to regulate body temperature, low heart pressure, hypoxia, immature cardiomyocyte structure, and immature immune system.

results.title: Regeneration in anamniotes was replaced by regengrow and scarring in amniotes after land colonization and the evolution of terrestrial biological cycles
results.author: L. Alibardi
results.takeaway: Vertebrates evolved terrestrial lifecycles, limiting regeneration, and regenerative medicine should consider diverse developmental pathways before introducing "anamniote regenerative genes" in amniotes.

results.title: Comparative Study in Zebrafish and Medaka Unravels the Mechanisms of Tissue Regeneration
results.author: K. Chowdhury
results.takeaway: Comparing zebrafish and medaka fish models can reveal insights into tissue regeneration mechanisms and potential therapeutic strategies for human diseases.

results.title: Complex tissue regeneration in Lophuromys reveals a phylogenetic signal for enhanced regenerative ability in deomyine rodents
results.author: Brennan Riddell
results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
results.takeaway: Deomyine rodents show enhanced regenerative ability, with brush-furred mice showing musculoskeletal regeneration, while nondeomyine rodents heal ear pinna injuries via fibrotic repair with scar tissue.

results.title: The blastema and epimorphic regeneration in mammals
results.author: A. Seifert
results.takeaway: Regenerative failure in mammals is likely influenced by the cellular response to the microenvironment after traumatic injury, providing a roadmap for advancing human regeneration.

results.title: Skin shedding and tissue regeneration in African spiny mice (Acomys)
results.author: A. Seifert
results.takeaway: African spiny mice (Acomys) exhibit skin autotomy and tissue regeneration, including complete regeneration of hair follicles, sebaceous glands, dermis, and cartilage, suggesting a higher capacity for regeneration than previously believed.

results.title: Zebra-Fishing for Regenerative Awakening in Mammals
results.author: Laura Massoz
results.takeaway: Zebrafish research has identified conserved regenerative molecular events that could potentially be used to restore damaged organs and tissues in mammals, with potential clinical translation potential.

results.title: Animal regeneration: ancestral character or evolutionary novelty?
results.author: J. Slack
results.takeaway: Whole-body regeneration is an ancestral character, while appendage regeneration is more likely a derived character resulting from specific adaptations.

results.title: Evolution of animal regeneration: re-emergence of a field.
results.author: Alexandra E. Bely
results.takeaway: Animal regeneration's origin, maintenance, and loss are driven by distinct factors, offering exciting progress in understanding the underlying mechanisms of regeneration evolution.

results.title: Regenerative Potential Across Species: An Eco-Evo-Devo Perspective
results.author: J. Coffman
results.takeaway: Regenerative medicine can target key constraints in mammalian development, ecology, epigenetics, and metabolism to improve tissue repair and regeneration.

facets.q: The cabbage-white pupa matches its colour to the surrounding light and background.

What is the ecological and evolutionary role of light effects on pigmentation in Pieris?
