results.title: The control of melanin-incorporation into the pupal color-pattern of the cabbage white pieris brassicae L.
results.author: Alert Oltmer
results.takeaway: The pigmentation of cabbage white pupae is influenced by light conditions, temperature, and a melanization inhibitoring factor distributed from the anterior part of the body during a critical period.

results.title: Pigments in the pupal integuments of two colour types of cabbage white butterfly, Pieris rapae crucivora
results.author: T. Ohtaki
results.takeaway: Cabbage white butterfly pupae can be green or greyish brown depending on light conditions, with green color due to yellow cuticle and bluish green epidermis, and brown color due to black spots and reddish-brown pigment in the epidermis.

results.title: Die Steuerung des Melanineinbaus in das Farbmuster der KohlweißlingspuppePieris brassicae L.
results.author: Alert Oltmer
results.journal: Wilhelm Roux' Archiv für Entwicklungsmechanik der Organismen
results.takeaway: The pigmentation of Cabbage White caterpillar pupae is influenced by light conditions, temperature, and a melanization inhibitoring factor distributed from the anterior part of the body.

results.title: [The course of melanization and its inhibition in pupae of the cabbage whitePieris brassicae L.]
results.author: D. Bückmann
results.journal: Wilhelm Roux' Archiv fur Entwicklungsmechanik der Organismen
results.takeaway: Cabbage White pupae melanize in response to light conditions and are controlled by gradual inhibition, with melanization varying in size and shape, and a melanization inhibitor secreted by a thoracic center.

results.title: Cabbage whites have a unique take on polarized light
results.author: K. Knight
results.takeaway: Cabbage white butterflies are in their natural habitat, they're not influenced by the presence of polarized light, making it easier for them to find suitable locations for laying their eggs.

results.title: Pupal colour plasticity in the butterfly Catopsilia pomona (Lepidoptera: Pieridae)
results.author: Tarunkishwor Yumnam
results.journal: Biological Journal of the Linnean Society
results.takeaway: Pupal color plasticity in the butterfly Catopsilia pomona helps pupae match their substrate colors, with leaf-borne pupae tending to be greener and off-leaf pupae browner, influenced by leaf position, midrib thickness, and leaf length.

results.title: Lack of response to background colour in Pieris brassicae pupae reared on carotenoid-free diet
results.author: M. Rothschild
results.takeaway: Pieris brassicae pupae show heterochromy (background contrasting) rather than homochromy (background matching) when fed a carotenoid-free diet, likely due to toxic effects of the toxic plant.

results.title: Carotenoids of the pupae of the Large White butterfly (Pieris brassicae) and the Small White butterfly (Pieris rapae)
results.author: M. Rothschild
results.takeaway: Diapausing pupae of the Large White and Small White butterflies contain more than double the concentration of carotenoids in their epidermis than non-diapausing pupae, and their green color can be modified by switching to long day regimes after feeding ceases.

results.title: Biology of Cabbage Butterfly Pieris brassicae Linn. (Lepidoptera: Pieridae)
results.author: M. Bhowmik
results.journal: International Journal of Current Microbiology and Applied Sciences
results.takeaway: Cabbage butterfly Pieris brassicae Linn. is a major insect pest that significantly reduces cabbage yield in India, affecting various vegetable crops.

results.title: White cabbage (Brassica oleracea var. capitata f. alba): botanical, phytochemical and pharmacological overview
results.author: Dunja Šamec
results.takeaway: White cabbage is a significant source of phytonutrients and health-promoting phytochemicals, with potential health benefits.

results.title: Molecular Mechanisms Underlying Pupal Protective Color Switch in Papilio polytes Butterflies
results.author: S. Yoda
results.takeaway: Papilio polytes butterflies' pupal colors are regulated by melanin synthesis genes, tyrosine hydroxylase, and laccase 2, with green coloration mainly influenced by multiple bilin binding protein and juvenile hormone binding protein genes.

results.title: Establishment of pupal color as a screening marker and activity analysis of six U6 promoters in Zeugodacus cucurbitae using the white pupae gene
results.author: Zizhen Fan
results.takeaway: This study successfully used piggyBac transgenic technology to create a screening marker for transgenic strains, enabling genetic control of tephritid species using CRISPR technology.

results.title: Blue-green light treatment enhances the quality and nutritional value in postharvest Chinese cabbage (Brassica rapa L. ssp. pekinensis)
results.author: Ruixing Zhang
results.takeaway: Blue-green light treatment effectively enhances the nutritional value and prolongs the shelf life of Chinese cabbage by increasing soluble protein, flavonoids, total phenols, and carotene.

results.title: Companion planting of flowering annuals enhances the colonization of natural enemies in white cabbage fields
results.author: G. Hithesh
results.journal: Journal of Plant Diseases and Protection
results.takeaway: Planting white cabbage with flowering annuals, such as chenopodium and calendula, can reduce insect pests and increase the colonization of natural enemies, potentially yielding higher returns for farmers.

results.title: Background matching and disruptive coloration as habitat-specific strategies for camouflage
results.author: Natasha Price
results.takeaway: Shore crabs exhibit habitat-specific camouflage strategies, with disruptive coloration dominating in complex rock pools and background matching in uniform mudflats, depending on the visual environment.

results.title: Pupal colour dimorphism in a desert swallowtail (Lepidoptera: Papilionidae) is driven by changes in food availability, not photoperiod
results.author: Daniel Piñones‐Tapia
results.takeaway: Pupal coloration in desert swallowtail butterflies is driven by food availability, not photoperiod, with matching pupation site coloration potentially aiding in field survival.

results.title: Effects of Different LED Spectra on the Antioxidant Capacity and Nitrogen Metabolism of Chinese Cabbage (Brassica rapa L. ssp. Pekinensis)
results.author: Jie Li
results.takeaway: Adding purple light to red-blue light effectively improves the nutritional value and antioxidant capacity of Chinese cabbage, making it a cost-effective supplemental lighting strategy for leafy vegetables.

results.title: Pupal colour–pupation substrate correlation in butterflies
results.author: H. Mayekar
results.takeaway: Pupal color plasticity in butterflies is strongly correlated with pupation substrate choice, potentially protecting them against predation by matching their background.

results.title: Effect of Biostimulants on the Productivity and Nutritional Value of White Cabbage (Brassica oleracea L. var. capitata)
results.author: D. Juškevičienė
results.takeaway: Biostimulants, such as amino acids and humic acids, can enhance white cabbage productivity and nutritional value, with the highest productivity achieved when applying a combination of humic and amino acids.

results.title: Phenotypic, transcriptomic, and metabolic comparison between white cabbage (Brassica oleracea var. capitata) and savoy cabbage (Brassica oleracea var. sabauda)
results.author: Hyunjoon Kim
results.takeaway: Savoy cabbage has a unique, bumpy leaf surface and higher amounts of functional secondary metabolites compared to white cabbage, with KNOX family genes playing a role in this development.

results.title: Action spectra for light-controlled pupal pigmentation in Pieris brassicae: melanization and level of bile pigment.
results.author: H. Kayser
results.takeaway: Light-controlled pupal pigmentation in Pieris brassicae is influenced by central nervous system mechanisms, with melanization and bile pigment levels correlated positively for 500 nm and negatively for >500 nm.

results.title: Ppbbx24-del mutant positively regulates light-induced anthocyanin accumulation in the ‘Red Zaosu’ pear (Pyrus pyrifolia White Pear Group)
results.author: Shuran Li
results.takeaway: The mutant Ppbbx24-del positively regulates anthocyanin accumulation in pear fruit peels, potentially enabling the creation of red pear cultivars.

results.title: Evolution and Mechanism of Spectral Tuning of Blue-Absorbing Visual Pigments in Butterflies
results.author: M. Wakakuwa
results.takeaway: Two amino acid substitutions at positions 116 and 177 in butterfly opsins are crucial for spectral tuning, which is specific to invertebrates and partially shared by other pierid and lycaenid butterfly species.

results.title: Untersuchungen zur photobiologie und endokrinologie der Farbmodifikationen bei der Kohlweisslingspuppe Pieris brassicae: Zeitverlauf der sensiblen und Kritischen Phasen☆
results.author: Inge Kayser-Wegmann
results.takeaway: Pieris brassicae pupae are sensitive to all light conditions and darkness only during two short phases, with sensitivity to yellow and blue light and darkness affecting bile pigment content differently.

results.title: Light-Induced Basic/Helix-Loop-Helix64 Enhances Anthocyanin Biosynthesis and Undergoes CONSTITUTIVELY PHOTOMORPHOGENIC1-Mediated Degradation in Pear1
results.author: Ruiyan Tao
results.takeaway: Light-induced PpbHLH64 positively regulates anthocyanin biosynthesis in red pear, with its degradation by CONSTITUTIVE PHOTOMORPHOGENIC1 being crucial for this process.

results.title: Light-responsive transcription factor PpWRKY44 induces anthocyanin accumulation by regulating PpMYB10 expression in pear
results.author: A. Alabd
results.takeaway: PpWRKY44 promotes anthocyanin accumulation in red pears by regulating PpMYB10 expression, potentially impacting fruit peel coloration in red pears.

results.title: Pterin pigment granules are responsible for both broadband light scattering and wavelength selective absorption in the wing scales of pierid butterflies
results.author: N. Morehouse
results.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences
results.takeaway: Pterin pigment granules in pierid butterflies' wing scales contribute to their bright colors and increase light reflection, potentially explaining sexual dichromatism and color signal evolution.

results.title: Melanocytes Sense Blue Light and Regulate Pigmentation through Opsin-3.
results.author: Claire Regazzetti
results.takeaway: OPN3 is the key sensor in melanocytes responsible for regulating pigmentation in skin type III and higher, offering potential targets for regulating melanogenesis and protecting dark skins against blue light exposure.

results.title: Ultrastructure and migration of screening pigments in the retina of Pieris rapae L. (Lepidoptera, Pieridae)
results.author: W. Ribi
results.takeaway: Pieris rapae's retina shows a complex morphology and migration of screening pigments, with two UV-receptors and four green receptors identified.

results.title: A unique visual pigment expressed in green, red and deep-red receptors in the eye of the small white butterfly, Pieris rapae crucivora
results.author: M. Wakakuwa
results.takeaway: The novel visual pigment PrL is expressed in green, red, and deep-red receptors in the eye of the small white butterfly Pieris rapae crucivora, with a maximum absorption at 563 nm.

results.title: Understanding the Mechanism of Light-Induced Age-Related Decrease in Melanin Concentration in Retinal Pigment Epithelium Cells
results.author: A. Dontsov
results.takeaway: The decrease in melanin concentration in retinal pigment epithelium cells with age is due to oxidative degradation by reactive oxygen species generated by lipofuscin in melanolipofuscin granules.

results.title: Colors and pterin pigmentation of pierid butterfly wings.
results.author: B. Wijnen
results.takeaway: Pierid butterfly wings' reflectance is primarily determined by pterin pigments in the scale structures, with ultraviolet-absorbing leucopterin in white Pieris species and violet-absorbing xanthopterin and blue-absorbing erythropterin in yellow- and orange-colored Coliadinae

results.title: The Emerging Role of Visible Light in Melanocyte Biology and Skin Pigmentary Disorders: Friend or Foe?
results.author: Xuanxuan He
results.takeaway: Visible light has complex effects on melanocyte biology and skin pigmentary disorders, with different wavelengths potentially having positive or negative effects depending on interactions with specific chromophores, photoaging, and other photon-mediated reactions.

results.title: NNT mediates redox-dependent pigmentation via a UVB- and MITF-independent mechanism
results.author: J. Allouche
results.takeaway: NNT-modifying topical drugs can target a redox-dependent pigmentation mechanism in skin, potentially benefiting medical and cosmetic purposes.

results.title: Opsin3—A Link to Visible Light-Induced Skin Pigmentation
results.author: Subba Rao Gangi Setty
results.takeaway: Visible light stimulates opsin3-regulated calcium-dependent microphthalmia-associated transcription factor activation, potentially contributing to long-lasting skin pigmentation in melanocompetent skins.

results.title: The Aqueous Extract of Polypodium leucotomos (Fernblock®) Regulates Opsin 3 and Prevents Photooxidation of Melanin Precursors on Skin Cells Exposed to Blue Light Emitted from Digital Devices
results.author: Mikel Portillo
results.takeaway: Fernblock protects skin cells from blue light damage and early photoaging by regulating Opsin-3 and preventing melanin photooxidation.

results.title: Skin Pigmentation and its Control: From Ultraviolet Radiation to Stem Cells
results.author: J. M. Yardman-Frank
results.takeaway: This review highlights the complex mechanisms of skin pigmentation, including the role of UV radiation, melanocyte stem cells, and potential interventions for pigmentation disorders.

results.title: Fish pigmentation and coloration: Molecular mechanisms and aquaculture perspectives
results.author: Mingkun Luo
results.takeaway: This review highlights the importance of understanding cellular and molecular mechanisms in fish coloration, which can be used to enhance body color in aquaculture through single-sex control and molecular marker-assisted breeding.

results.title: Extreme Refractive Index Wing Scale Beads Containing Dense Pterin Pigments Cause the Bright Colors of Pierid Butterflies
results.author: B. Wilts
results.takeaway: Extreme pterin pigment concentrations in wing scale beads create one of the most highly light scattering media in the animal kingdom, contributing to the bright colors of Pierid butterflies.

results.title: Melanin’s Journey from Melanocytes to Keratinocytes: Uncovering the Molecular Mechanisms of Melanin Transfer and Processing
results.author: Liliana Bento-Lopes
results.takeaway: Understanding the molecular mechanisms regulating skin pigmentation can lead to novel therapeutic strategies for treating hypo- or hyper-pigmentation disorders and cosmetic applications.

results.title: Analysis of the genetic loci of pigment pattern evolution in vertebrates
results.author: J. Elkin
results.takeaway: Cis-regulatory mutations contribute more to vertebrate pigmentation patterns, with carotenoid-based pigmentation and pattern boundaries being more affected, and genes involved in developmental processes being more affected.

results.title: Piebaldism and chromatophore development in reptiles are linked to the tfec gene
results.author: Alan García-Elfring
results.takeaway: The tfec gene is linked to the recessive piebald phenotype in ball pythons and is required for chromatophore development in reptiles, highlighting its importance as a model species for understanding vertebrate coloration.

results.title: Genome-wide association study reveals genetic architecture and evolution of human retinal pigmentation
results.author: Jian Yuan
results.takeaway: Deep learning-based deep learning framework DeepGRP identifies 42 genetic signals in retinal pigmentation, revealing polygenic adaptation in Europeans driven by snow-reflected light at high latitudes and a polygenic risk score for myopia.

results.title: The genetic basis of wing spots in Pieris canidia butterflies
results.author: Jocelyn Liang Qi Wee
results.takeaway: Pieris canidia butterflies' wing spots and nymphalid butterflies' eyespots share common regulatory modules, suggesting their likely independent origins.

results.title: Adaptive Variation in Beach Mice Produced by Two Interacting Pigmentation Genes
results.author: C. Steiner
results.takeaway: Two interacting genes, melanocortin-1 receptor and Agouti signaling protein, contribute to adaptive coloration in beach mice, with the latter having a lighter coat for camouflage on coastal sand dunes.

results.title: ADAPTIVE SIGNIFICANCE OF PIGMENT POLYMORPHISMS IN COLIAS BUTTERFLIES. I. VARIATION OF MELANIN PIGMENT IN RELATION TO THERMOREGULATION
results.author: W. B. Watt
results.takeaway: Temperature influences the variation in melanin pigmentation in Colias butterflies, suggesting that thermal regulation may play a role in adaptive significance of pigment polymorphism.

results.title: Effects of Light on the Fruiting Body Color and Differentially Expressed Genes in Flammulina velutipes
results.author: J-H Im
results.takeaway: Exposure to green and blue light intensifies the color of fruiting bodies in Flammulina velutipes, with 103 differentially expressed genes identified, potentially affecting light-mediated regulatory pathways.

results.title: The thermal dependence and molecular basis of physiological color change in Takydromus septentrionalis (Lacertidae)
results.author: Kun Guo
results.takeaway: Physiological color change in lizards, like Takydromus septentrionalis, helps regulate body temperature by altering pigment arrangement and solar radiation absorption/reflection.

results.title: Vertebrate pigmentation: from underlying genes to adaptive function.
results.author: J. K. Hubbard
results.takeaway: Pigment gene function is largely conserved across diverse vertebrate taxa and influences adaptive coloration in predictable ways, raising questions about selection shaping phenotypic and genetic variation.

results.title: Genetics, development and evolution of adaptive pigmentation in vertebrates
results.author: H. Hoekstra
results.takeaway: Pigmentation studies in vertebrates provide insights into the genetic basis of adaptive traits and the evolutionary process, offering insights into organismal diversity and adaptation.

results.title: Reproductive toxicology. Pesticide/fertilizer mix III (Iowa).
results.author: C. Steiner
results.takeaway: Two genes, melanocortin-1 receptor and Agouti signaling protein, are responsible for most of the color variation in oldfield mice subspecies, with a derived mutation in Mc1r and an increase in Agouti mRNA expression contributing to beach mice's lighter coat.

results.title: The genetics of pigmentation: from fancy genes to complex traits.
results.author: G. Barsh
results.takeaway: Recent developments in genetics of pigmentation reveal that homologous genes in humans are responsible for both rare diseases and common phenotypic variations, such as red hair and fair skin.

results.title: Microscopic basis of reaction center modulation in PsbA variants of photosystem II
results.author: Sinjini Bhattacharjee
results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
results.takeaway: Genetic variations in photosystem II's D1 protein can alter primary charge separation and electron transfer processes, potentially impacting photosynthesis under different environmental conditions.

results.title: Compound eyes of the small white butterfly Pieris rapae have three distinct classes of red photoreceptors
results.author: A. Blake
results.takeaway: The compound eyes of the small white butterfly Pieris rapae have three distinct classes of red photoreceptors, with no significant differences in sensitivity between the two subspecies.

results.title: Environmental factors influencing pupal colour determination in Lepidoptera. II. Experiments with Pieris rapae, Pieris napi and Pieris brassicae
results.author: A. Smith
results.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society of London. Series B. Biological Sciences
results.takeaway: Light stimuli, particularly yellow and blue spectral wavelengths, play a crucial role in determining pupal coloration in Lepidoptera species.

results.title: Induced Changes in the Pigmentation of the Pupoe of the Butterfly Pieris Napi L., and their Inheritance
results.author: J. Harrison
results.journal: Proceedings of The Royal Society B: Biological Sciences
results.takeaway: Exposure to orange light before pupation in Pieris Napi L. butterfly larvae leads to inherited green pupal pigmentation, affecting the appearance of the chrysalids.

results.title: Pigmentation and colour changing mechanism in fishes
results.author: Mintumoni Pegu
results.takeaway: Fish pigmentation is influenced by genetic, morphological, physiological, and environmental factors, with genes and nutritional contents playing crucial roles in pigment production and color change.

results.title: Seeing the light to change colour: An evolutionary perspective on the role of melanopsin in neuroendocrine circuits regulating light‐mediated skin pigmentation
results.author: G. Bertolesi
results.takeaway: Melanopsins play a crucial role in regulating light-mediated skin pigmentation, with their evolutionary selection influenced by thermoregulation, ultraviolet protection, background adaptation, and the loss of a photosensitive pineal gland in mammals.

results.title: Sexual dichroism and pigment localization in the wing scales of Pieris rapae butterflies
results.author: M. Giraldo
results.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences
results.takeaway: Beads in Pieris rapae butterflies' wing scales play a crucial role in wing coloration, allowing for strong color contrasts and sexual dichroism in the Japanese subspecies.

results.title: A transition to white LED increases ecological impacts of nocturnal illumination on aquatic primary producers in a lowland agricultural drainage ditch.
results.author: M. Grubisic
results.takeaway: The transition to white LED nocturnal illumination decreases aquatic primary producer biomass by up to 62%, potentially impacting ecosystem functions.

results.title: The effect of juvenile hormone on pupal pigmentation of Pieris brassicae L.
results.author: W. Ressin
results.takeaway: Juvenile hormone (JH) plays a role in the pigmentation of pupae of Pieris brassicae, with blue light producing the strongest pigmentation and FME inhibiting black spot formation in the cuticle.

results.title: Evolutionary Recycling of Light Signaling Components in Fleshy Fruits: New Insights on the Role of Pigments to Monitor Ripening
results.author: Briardo Llorente
results.takeaway: Evolutionary recycling of light-signaling components in fleshy fruits, such as tomatoes, has allowed plants to finely adjust pigmentation to the actual ripening stage, potentially providing a selective advantage before the extinction of dinosaurs.

results.title: The Genetics and Evolution of Human Pigmentation
results.author: Dorra Guermazi
results.takeaway: Human skin pigmentation is shaped by natural selection in response to ultraviolet radiation, with genetic variations influencing skin cancer risk, vitamin-D metabolism, and pigmentary disorders.

results.title: Molecular ecology and adaptation of visual photopigments in craniates
results.author: Wayne I. L. Davies
results.takeaway: Molecular adaptations in visual photopigments in craniates have evolved to survive in diverse light environments, including brightly lit aquatic surroundings, the deep sea, and light-restricted fossorial settings.

results.title: Diversified Mammalian Visual Adaptations to Bright- or Dim-Light Environments
results.author: Yulin Gai
results.takeaway: Mammalian visual adaptations to bright- and dim-light environments are influenced by different evolutionary patterns in visual pigments, indicating ecological adaptations.

results.title: Thermobiological effects of temperature‐induced color variations in Aglais urticae (Lepidoptera, Nymphalidae)
results.author: G. Markl
results.takeaway: Temperature-induced color variations in adult butterflies provide thermobiological benefits, with lower temperatures leading to darker coloration and higher temperatures leading to lighter individuals.

results.title: Evolutionary loss of shell pigmentation, pattern, and eye structure in deep‐sea snails in the dysphotic zone
results.author: Suzanne T. Williams
results.takeaway: Loss of shell pigmentation, pattern, and eye structure in deep-sea snails (Solariellidae) occurs without reversal, with pigmentation and pattern being important for camouflage from visual predators, and low-resolution vision requiring high light intensity for basic visual tasks.

15.state: How light wavelength acts on pigment-pattern formation is partly addressed — visual input regulates melanophore differentiation and specific wavelengths change melanin in juveniles — but a direct account of light shaping amphibian pattern is still open. The specific question is alive only at the edges.

results.title: Individual colour patches as multicomponent signals
results.author: G. Grether
results.takeaway: Multiple trait evolution theory can be applied to individual color patch components, allowing for a more comprehensive understanding of animal coloration.

results.title: Light-specific wavelengths differentially affect the exploration rate, opercular beat, skin color change, opsin transcripts, and the oxi-redox system of the longsnout seahorse Hippocampus reidi.
results.author: J. A. Souto-Neto
results.journal: Comparative biochemistry and physiology. Part A, Molecular & integrative physiology
results.takeaway: Yellow light increases melanin levels in juvenile seahorses, while blue and yellow wavelengths increase juvenile mortality rates, impacting their color change, growth, and survival rates.

results.title: Colouration matters in dull toads: ultraviolet adornment for ladies and agrochemicals fading effects
results.author: S. Tartu
results.takeaway: Spiny toads exhibit sexual dichromatism, with females reflecting more ultraviolet light than males, and agrochemical exposure can alter throat coloration, potentially impacting mate attractiveness.

results.title: Salamanders and other amphibians are aglow with biofluorescence
results.author: Jennifer Y. Lamb
results.takeaway: Biofluorescence is widespread in amphibians, with variations in patterning and primary wavelengths within the green light spectrum, potentially impacting their ecology and evolution.

results.title: Evolutionary analyses of visual opsin genes in frogs and toads: Diversity, duplication, and positive selection
results.author: Ryan K. Schott
results.takeaway: Anurans exhibit diverse visual systems with ecological factors and behavior driving changes in their visual systems, including visual opsin duplication in the African bullfrog.

results.title: Adaptive colouration in amphibians.
results.author: Andreas Rudh
results.takeaway: Adaptive coloration in amphibians plays a role in thermoregulation, UV protection, predator avoidance, and sexual signaling, but many functions remain unexplored and few genes influencing pigmentation or patterning have been identified.

results.title: A transcriptome analysis revealing the molecular mechanism of light intensity-driven color variation in the skin of Chinese giant salamander (Andrias davidianus)
results.author: Zhizhi Jing

results.title: Colour Confusion: Reviewing Ambiguities in the Identification and Classification of Chromatophore Deficiencies Among Amphibians
results.author: John Gould
results.takeaway: This review clarifies terminology and establishes standards for identifying and classifying color abnormalities in amphibians, addressing ambiguity and confusion in the literature.

results.title: The diversity of opsins in Lake Baikal amphipods (Amphipoda: Gammaridae)
results.author: P. Drozdova
results.takeaway: Lake Baikal amphipods have evolved a unique visual system, with middle and long wavelength-sensitive opsins, suggesting common triggers during periods of darkness during Lake Baikal's ice cover and melting.

results.title: Naturally occurring fluorescence in frogs
results.author: C. Taboada
results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
results.takeaway: Fluorescence in tree frogs contributes to 18-29% of total emerging light in twilight and nocturnal scenarios, enhancing brightness and matching night vision in amphibians.

results.title: Developmental changes in the cone visual pigments of black bream Acanthopagrus butcheri.
results.author: J. Shand
results.takeaway: Black bream develop a sensitivity to longer wavelengths in their visual pigments, potentially adapting to a changing light environment in estuarine waters.

results.title: Anion sensitivity and spectral tuning of cone visual pigments in situ.
results.author: J. Kleinschmidt
results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
results.takeaway: Long-wavelength-absorbing vertebrate visual pigments are anion sensitive, with Cl- and Br- anions redshifting their absorbance spectrum, and Lyotropic anions causing blue shifts.

results.title: THE EFFECT OF WAVELENGTH AND INTENSITY OF LIGHT ON THE PROPORTION OF PIGMENTS IN PORPHYRIDIUM CRUENTUM
results.author: M. Brody
results.takeaway: Controlling light intensity and wavelength can alter the concentrations of chlorophyll and phycoerythrin in Porphyridium cruentum, allowing for varying red and green pigment proportions.

results.title: Adaptive evolutionary paths from UV reception to sensing violet light by epistatic interactions
results.author: S. Yokoyama
results.takeaway: Epistatic interactions in short wavelength-sensitive pigments can enable animals to evolve from UV reception to violet light reception, improving visual resolution and subtle contrast detection.

results.title: Editorial: Evo-Devo of Color Pattern Formation
results.author: R. Mallarino
results.takeaway: Advances in genomic, molecular, and imaging approaches reveal the mechanistic basis of color pattern formation in animal species, providing insights into evolutionary developmental biology and phenotypic diversity.

results.title: Biofluorescent sexual dimorphism revealed in a southern Appalachian endemic salamander, Plethodon metcalfi
results.author: J. Cox
results.takeaway: Southern Gray-Cheeked Salamanders exhibit biofluorescent sexual dimorphism, potentially related to ventral modified granular glands used in plethodontid chemosensory communication.

results.title: Larval Pigmentation Reveals Environmental and Genetic Influences in Hybridizing Ambystoma Salamanders
results.author: Alfredo Ascanio
results.takeaway: Hybrid Ambystoma salamander larvae show intermediate UVR responses, with greater similarity to their maternal phenotype, suggesting potential performance reduction if intermediate pigmentation is suboptimal.

results.title: Genetic Basis of Spectral Tuning in the Violet-Sensitive Visual Pigment of African Clawed Frog, Xenopus laevis
results.author: Yusuke Takahashi
results.takeaway: The spectral tuning of African clawed frog violet-sensitive visual pigment is influenced by 13 critical amino acid sites, increasing the total number of critical sites in vertebrate SWS1 pigments.

results.title: Zebrafish Pigment Pattern Formation: Insights into the Development and Evolution of Adult Form.
results.author: Larissa B. Patterson
results.takeaway: Zebrafish pigment patterns are shaped by precise coordination of pigment cell lineage specification, differentiation, and cellular interactions, providing insights into pattern diversification in vertebrates.

results.title: Changes in the visual environment affect colour signal brightness and shoaling behaviour in a freshwater fish
results.author: J. Kelley
results.takeaway: Western rainbowfish exhibit increased brightness of red color patterns in environments rich in organic matter, potentially enhancing communication in altered visual environments.

results.title: Visual input regulates melanophore differentiation
results.author: K. Atkinson‐Leadbeater
results.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
results.takeaway: Reduced visual input in stage 40 larvae leads to rapid melanophore differentiation, with extra-pineal melatonin signaling promoting this process.

results.title: Genetics and evolution of pigment patterns in fish.
results.author: R. Kelsh
results.takeaway: Fish pigment patterns are shaped by local cues, chromatophore interactions, and cell-cell interactions, with potential for evolution through developmental genetics and theoretical modeling.

results.title: Interplay of Light, Melatonin, and Circadian Genes in Skin Pigmentation Regulation
results.author: G. Bertolesi
results.takeaway: Circadian cycle regulation, rather than proliferative capacity, alters melanization of melanophores, with melatonin playing a key role in this process.

results.title: Role of eyes and pineal gland in melanophore response in the green frog. Rana esculenta.
results.author: P. K. Saxena
results.takeaway: The green frog's melanophore response is influenced by the eyes and pineal gland, with the latter potentially playing a role in photic cues and melanin aggregating substance release.

results.title: In vitro analysis suggests that difference in cell movement during direct interaction can generate various pigment patterns in vivo
results.author: Hiroaki Yamanaka
results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
results.takeaway: Different cell movements during direct interaction between melanophores and xanthophores in zebrafish can generate various pigment patterns, highlighting the importance of cell movements in pattern formation.

results.title: Rhabdomeric phototransduction initiated by the vertebrate photopigment melanopsin.
results.author: M. C. Isoldi
results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
results.takeaway: Melanopsin in vertebrates initiates a similar light-activated signaling cascade to invertebrates, resulting in increased intracellular inositol triphosphate and melanosome dispersion.

results.title: Iridophores as a source of robustness in zebrafish stripes and variability in Danio patterns
results.author: A. Volkening
results.takeaway: Iridophores play a key role in zebrafish stripes and Danio patterns, enabling robust patterning and variability within the fish species.

results.title: How fish color their skin: A paradigm for development and evolution of adult patterns
results.author: C. Nüsslein-Volhard
results.takeaway: Fish color their skin through species-specific interactions among pigment cell types, influenced by direct cell contact and tissue environment cues.

results.title: Pigment Pattern Formation by Contact-Dependent Depolarization
results.author: Masafumi Inaba
results.takeaway: Contact-dependent depolarization of melanophores and xanthophores in zebrafish skin leads to migration, potentially explaining the stripe pattern in zebrafish.

results.title: Interactions with Iridophores and the Tissue Environment Required for Patterning Melanophores and Xanthophores during Zebrafish Adult Pigment Stripe Formation
results.author: Larissa B. Patterson
results.takeaway: Iridophores play a crucial role in organizing melanophores and xanthophores during the development of stripes and interstripes in zebrafish.

results.title: Pigment patterns of larval salamanders (Ambystomatidae, Salamandridae): the role of the lateral line sensory system and the evolution of pattern-forming mechanisms.
results.author: D. Parichy
results.takeaway: Larval salamanders' horizontal stripe patterns are influenced by the development of the trunk lateral line sensory system, with similar mechanisms being common and ancestral in both Ambystomatidae and Salamandridae families.

results.title: Agouti and BMP signaling drive a naturally occurring fate conversion of melanophores to leucophores in zebrafish
results.author: Delai Huang
results.takeaway: Local signals in zebrafish's fins drive the transformation of black pigment cells into white ones, resulting in white highlights and ornamentation.

results.title: Bar, stripe and spot development in sand-dwelling cichlids from Lake Malawi
results.author: Laura A. Hendrick
results.takeaway: Stripes in sand-dwelling cichlids develop through differentiation of melanophores along horizontal myosepta, while bars are supported by extensive migration of undifferentiated melanophores in the skin during metamorphosis.

results.title: Iridophore apoptosis mediates socially-regulated developmental color pattern plasticity in an anemonefish
results.author: Laurie J. Mitchell
results.takeaway: Social environment influences developmental color pattern plasticity in anemonefish, with iridophore apoptosis playing a key role in regulating color changes and potentially aiding in conflict avoidance during recruitment.

results.title: Homotypic cell competition regulates proliferation and tiling of zebrafish pigment cells during colour pattern formation
results.author: B. Walderich
results.takeaway: Homotypic cell competition plays a key role in regulating the proliferation and tiling of zebrafish pigment cells during color pattern formation.

results.title: The dynamic behavior of chromatophores marks the transition from bands to spots in leopard geckos
results.author: Asier Ullate-Agote
results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
results.takeaway: Leopard geckos' skin coloration is influenced by melanophores-iridophores interactions, with melanophores autonomously forming black spots in adulthood, and a genetic mutation in the transcription factor plays a key role in skin pattern formation.

results.title: Formation of the adult pigment pattern in zebrafish requires leopard and obelix dependent cell interactions
results.author: Florian Maderspacher
results.takeaway: Leopard and obelix-dependent cell interactions drive the formation of the adult pigment pattern in zebrafish, with leopard regulating homotypic interaction within melanophores and xanthophores and obelix controlling boundary shape.

results.title: Testis development in the Japanese eel is affected by photic signals through melatonin secretion
results.author: Ji-Yeon Hyeon
results.takeaway: Japanese eels' testis development is influenced by photic signals through melatonin secretion, with new moon exposure leading to higher eye and plasma melatonin levels.

results.title: Effect of monochromatic light on melanophore arrangement in spotted snakehead fish Channa punctata (Bloch, 1793).
results.author: Bulbul Ali
results.takeaway: Monochromatic light significantly influences melanophore arrangement in spotted snakehead fish Channa punctata, with blue light being appropriate for overall species color and continuous black or white light causing severe damage.

results.title: Functional colour genes and signals of selection in colour‐polymorphic salamanders
results.author: J. Burgon
results.takeaway: European fire salamanders show functional associations between color morphs and genes, suggesting that current ecological and evolutionary hypotheses may need revision.

results.title: Coordinated microRNA/mRNA Expression Profiles Reveal Unique Skin Color Regulatory Mechanisms in Chinese Giant Salamander (Andrias davidianus)
results.author: Yanjie Guo
results.journal: Animals : an Open Access Journal from MDPI
results.takeaway: Chinese giant salamanders with albino skin have unique skin color regulatory mechanisms, which could help accelerate the acquisition of specific body colors through genetic means.

results.title: Analysis of the genetic loci of pigment pattern evolution in vertebrates
results.author: J. Elkin
results.takeaway: Cis-regulatory mutations contribute more to vertebrate pigmentation patterns, with carotenoid-based pigmentation and pattern boundaries being more affected, and genes involved in developmental processes being more affected.

results.title: Evolutionary and genomic associations of colour and pattern in fire and Alpine salamanders (Salamandra Spp.)
results.author: J. Burgon
results.takeaway: This study provides greater phylogenetic resolution for the genus Salamandra and confirms the convergent evolution of reproductive and color phenotypes, highlighting the need for taxonomic revisions and understanding of amphibian coloration.

results.title: Skin Colour in Salamanders Is Modulated by Both Epitranscriptomic Methylation and Gene Expression
results.author: Nicholas Strowbridge
results.takeaway: Multiple molecular mechanisms, including gene expression and RNA methylation, contribute to salamander color diversity, with a positive correlation and significant overlap in transcripts.

results.title: ADAPTIVE COLORATION AND GENE FLOW AS A CONSTRAINT TO LOCAL ADAPTATION IN THE STREAMSIDE SALAMANDER, AMBYSTOMA BARBOURI
results.author: Andrew Storfer
results.takeaway: Larvae of the streamside salamander, Ambystoma barbouri, tend to be lighter in permanent streams, less conspicuous to fish, and have higher survival, while those in ephemeral streams are darker and more conspicuous to predators.

results.title: Effects of Light on the Fruiting Body Color and Differentially Expressed Genes in Flammulina velutipes
results.author: J-H Im
results.takeaway: Exposure to green and blue light intensifies the color of fruiting bodies in Flammulina velutipes, with 103 differentially expressed genes identified, potentially affecting light-mediated regulatory pathways.

results.title: Transcriptomics reveals the molecular processes of light-induced rapid darkening of the non-obligate cave dweller Oreolalax rhodostigmatus (Megophryidae, Anura) and their genetic basis of pigmentation strategy
results.author: Wei Zhu
results.takeaway: Rapid morphological color change plays a key role in the light-induced rapid darkening of Oreolalax rhodostigmatus tadpoles, with genetic mutations in MC1R coordinating pigment regression and robust melanogenesis in darkness and light.

results.title: Genetic manipulation of structural color in bacterial colonies
results.author: V. Johansen
results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
results.takeaway: Genetic modifications in bacterial colonies can alter their optical appearance, paving the way for the creation of on-demand living optical materials for use as paints and sensors.

results.title: The conspicuous postmetamorphic coloration of fire salamanders, but not their toxicity, is affected by larval background albedo.
results.author: Eugenia Sanchez
results.journal: Journal of experimental zoology. Part B, Molecular and developmental evolution
results.takeaway: Fire salamanders' black-and-yellow coloration is conspicuous to predators at night, but not their toxicity, as larval background albedo does not affect their alkaloid profile.

results.title: The Adaptive Role of Carotenoids and Anthocyanins in Solanum lycopersicum Pigment Mutants under High Irradiance
results.author: A. Ashikhmin
results.takeaway: High-pigment tomato mutants show enhanced adaptability to high-intensity light, with increased flavonoid and carotenoid contents leading to enhanced expression of key genes related to pigment synthesis and light regulation.

results.title: Investigating the Physiological and Molecular Responses of Solanum lycopersicum hp Mutants to Light of Different Quality for Biotechnological Applications
results.author: M. Vereshchagin
results.takeaway: The 3005mutant shows the highest nonenzymatic antioxidant activity under blue light, suggesting potential for biotechnology applications to enhance nutritional value by enhancing flavonoid content.

results.title: The thermal dependence and molecular basis of physiological color change in Takydromus septentrionalis (Lacertidae)
results.author: Kun Guo
results.takeaway: Physiological color change in lizards, like Takydromus septentrionalis, helps regulate body temperature by altering pigment arrangement and solar radiation absorption/reflection.

results.title: Fish pigmentation and coloration: Molecular mechanisms and aquaculture perspectives
results.author: Mingkun Luo
results.takeaway: This review highlights the importance of understanding cellular and molecular mechanisms in fish coloration, which can be used to enhance body color in aquaculture through single-sex control and molecular marker-assisted breeding.

results.title: A methodological workflow for quantitative colouration and colour pattern comparison reveals taxonomic and habitat‐level differences in the polymorphic fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra)
results.author: L. Alarcón‐Ríos
results.takeaway: This study effectively detects differences in color patterns in the polymorphic fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra) at both taxonomic and habitat levels, revealing an increased prevalence of melanistic coloration and less homogeneous color pattern in urban settings.

results.title: Colour polymorphism in Salamandra salamandra (Amphibia: Urodela), revealed by a lack of genetic and environmental differentiation between distinct phenotypes
results.author: W. Beukema
results.journal: Journal of Zoological Systematics and Evolutionary Research
results.takeaway: Colour polymorphism exists in Salamandra salamandra, but the subspecies S. s. alfredschmidti should be reclassified as a junior synonym of S. s. bernardezi due to lack of genetic and environmental differentiation between distinct phenotypes.

results.title: Monkeyflowers (Mimulus): new model for plant developmental genetics and evo-devo.
results.author: Yao-wu Yuan
results.takeaway: Monkeyflowers (Mimulus) offer a new model for studying plant developmental genetics and evolution, offering opportunities for exciting discoveries in areas such as carotenoid biosynthesis, pigmentation patterns, and pollinator shift.

results.title: Changing color can have health benefits
results.author: Jin Zhou
results.journal: Frontiers in Ecology and the Environment
results.takeaway: Chinese giant salamanders' changing skin color is an adaptive strategy for living in different light levels, with dark skin pigment acting as an antioxidant, anti-ultraviolet light, and antimicrobial property.

results.title: Circadian Rhythm of Body Color Change in the Juvenile Chinese Giant Salamander (Andrias davidianus) Under Different Photoperiods
results.author: Yifang Zhang
results.journal: Animals : an Open Access Journal from MDPI
results.takeaway: The circadian rhythm of body color change in juvenile Chinese giant salamanders is coordinatedly regulated by endogenous circadian rhythms and exogenous photoperiodic signals, affecting their survival and adaptation to the environment.

results.title: Color morphs of the fire salamander are discriminated at night by conspecifics and predators
results.author: P. Aguilar
results.takeaway: Fire salamander color morphs can be visually discriminated at night by conspecifics and predators, potentially representing different adaptive optima and influencing predation pressure.

results.title: Factors determining the dorsal coloration pattern of aposematic salamanders
results.author: Benedetta Barzaghi
results.takeaway: Environmental conditions and food availability are more important than local adaptations in determining differences in aposematic coloration patterns of salamanders.

results.title: Evolutionary Recycling of Light Signaling Components in Fleshy Fruits: New Insights on the Role of Pigments to Monitor Ripening
results.author: Briardo Llorente
results.takeaway: Evolutionary recycling of light-signaling components in fleshy fruits, such as tomatoes, has allowed plants to finely adjust pigmentation to the actual ripening stage, potentially providing a selective advantage before the extinction of dinosaurs.

results.title: Seeing the light to change colour: An evolutionary perspective on the role of melanopsin in neuroendocrine circuits regulating light‐mediated skin pigmentation
results.author: G. Bertolesi
results.takeaway: Melanopsins play a crucial role in regulating light-mediated skin pigmentation, with their evolutionary selection influenced by thermoregulation, ultraviolet protection, background adaptation, and the loss of a photosensitive pineal gland in mammals.

results.author: Bernat Burriel-Carranza

results.title: A role for ecology in the evolution of colour variation and sexual dimorphism in Hawaiian damselflies
results.author: I. Cooper
results.takeaway: Exposure to solar radiation significantly predicts body color variation in Hawaiian damselflies, with redder coloration associated with more exposure to solar radiation.

results.title: Light adaptation in cone photoreceptors of the salamander: a role for cytoplasmic calcium.
results.author: H. Matthews
results.takeaway: Cytoplasmic calcium concentration plays a primary role in light adaptation in salamander cone photoreceptors, with pigment bleaching potentially significant at high intensities.

results.title: Evolutionary loss of shell pigmentation, pattern, and eye structure in deep‐sea snails in the dysphotic zone
results.author: Suzanne T. Williams
results.takeaway: Loss of shell pigmentation, pattern, and eye structure in deep-sea snails (Solariellidae) occurs without reversal, with pigmentation and pattern being important for camouflage from visual predators, and low-resolution vision requiring high light intensity for basic visual tasks.

results.title: A transition to white LED increases ecological impacts of nocturnal illumination on aquatic primary producers in a lowland agricultural drainage ditch.
results.author: M. Grubisic
results.takeaway: The transition to white LED nocturnal illumination decreases aquatic primary producer biomass by up to 62%, potentially impacting ecosystem functions.

16.state: Whether an environmentally induced pattern can be inherited is today's transgenerational-plasticity debate: modern work shows non-genetic inheritance of induced morphologies (Daphnia) but stresses that Kammerer's specific claim is unconfirmed and that coloration is often strongly genetic. The core question is open and actively argued.

results.title: The Midwife Toad Challenge After (Half) a Century
results.author: J. Arntzen
results.takeaway: Paul Kammerer's claim that environmentally induced character states are carried over to the next generation remains unconfirmed, but his experiment on fire salamander color pattern change has been confirmed.

results.title: Genetic and environmental drivers of colour and pattern in the Australian jacky dragon (Amphibolurus muricatus)
results.author: Rebecca S Raynal
results.takeaway: Heritable genetic factors and hatchling age are key drivers of coloration in the Australian jacky dragon, while thermal environment does not significantly contribute to variation in coloration.

results.title: The Genetic Basis of Adaptation following Plastic Changes in Coloration in a Novel Environment.
results.author: Ammon Corl
results.takeaway: Ancient plasticity in coloration facilitated initial survival in a lava environment, followed by genetic changes that modified the phenotype and aided adaptation to the new environment.

results.title:
Non-genetic inheritance of induced defense morphologies across multiple unexposed generations of
 Daphnia lumholtzi
results.author: Shannon N Snyder
results.takeaway: Non-genetic inheritance of predator-induced morphologies in Daphnia lumholtzi water fleas persists through multiple generations, highlighting the ecological significance of non-genetic inheritance in natural populations.

results.title: Family resemblance in color‐patch size is not affected by stress experience in a cichlid fish
results.author: Angelika Ziegelbecker
results.takeaway: The size of a yellow bar on a cichlid fish's body is strongly determined by genetic factors or shared maternal and brood environments, with limited environmental influences later in life.

results.title: Background matching through fast and reversible melanin-based pigmentation plasticity in tadpoles comes with morphological and antioxidant changes
results.author: H. C. Liedtke
results.takeaway: Tadpoles can rapidly and reversibly adjust their pigmentation to match environmental changes, leading to larger tail fins and improved redox status.

results.title: Fish and dragonfly nymph predators induce opposite shifts in color and morphology of tadpoles
results.author: Justin C. Touchon
results.takeaway: Tadpoles can shift both color and morphology in opposite, predator-specific directions in response to fish and dragonfly nymph predators, potentially resulting in genetic variation for developmental plasticity.

results.title: Predator-induced transgenerational plasticity in animals: a meta-analysis
results.author: Kirsty J Macleod
results.takeaway: Predator-induced transgenerational plasticity is strong in animals, but no clear evidence supports specific hypotheses about its strength, direction, or waning over ontogeny.

results.title: Plasticity across Generations
results.author: R. Bonduriansky
results.takeaway: Transgenerational plasticity can contribute to adaptive evolution, with both adaptive and non-adaptive forms, but caution is needed when inferring adaptive function.

results.title: MORPHOLOGY AND PHYSIOLOGY OF LARVAL COLOR VARIATION IN THE WHITE-LINED SPHINX MOTH, HYLES LINEATA
results.author: C. Francois
results.takeaway: The yellow and green coloration in larvae of the whitelined sphinx moth, Hyles lineata, is primarily controlled by one gene, with modifier genes interacting with it, and may provide an ecological advantage in changing environments.

results.title: Plastic background colour matching in the springbok mantis
results.author: N. Burke
results.takeaway: The springbok mantis exhibits strong developmental plasticity in coloration, with green backgrounds promoting all-green phenotypes and brown backgrounds producing mixed phenotypes, likely due to habitat diversity and sedentary lifestyle.

results.title: Adaptive colouration in amphibians.
results.author: Andreas Rudh
results.takeaway: Adaptive coloration in amphibians plays a role in thermoregulation, UV protection, predator avoidance, and sexual signaling, but many functions remain unexplored and few genes influencing pigmentation or patterning have been identified.

results.title: Transgenerational Plasticity in Human-Altered Environments
results.author: S. Donelan
results.takeaway: Human-induced rapid environmental change may negatively impact transgenerational plasticity, potentially leading to negative fitness outcomes for species.

results.title: Transgenerational Plasticity in Flower Color Induced by Caterpillars
results.author: M. Sobral
results.takeaway: Herbivory on wild radish plants leads to transgenerational effects on flower color, partly related to chromatin modifications.

results.title: Developmental Plasticity in Anurans: Meta-analysis Reveals Effects of Larval Environments on Size at Metamorphosis And Timing of Metamorphosis.
results.author: Molly A. Albecker
results.takeaway: Developmental plasticity in anurans is partly influenced by larval environments, with higher temperatures and lower water levels reducing mass at metamorphosis and less food and higher densities increasing the duration of the larval period.

results.title: Experimental Tests for Heritable Morphological Color Plasticity in Non-Native Brown Trout (Salmo trutta) Populations
results.author: Peter A. H. Westley
results.takeaway: Photypic plasticity, rather than heritable variation, is the most likely explanation for the variation in color intensity observed among non-native brown trout populations in nature.

results.title: Transgenerational Plasticity in the Context of Predator-Prey Interactions
results.author: J. Tariel
results.takeaway: Predator-induced transgenerational plasticity in metazoans allows prey to fine-tune their phenotype to the current risk of predation, with potential adaptive value and underlying mechanisms.

results.title: What coloration brings: Implications of background adaptation to oxidative stress in anurans
results.author: Tijana B. Radovanović
results.takeaway: Background color adaptation in amphibians can increase oxidative stress, but if the background color changes, defense systems decline and lipid peroxidation occurs.

results.title: Pigmentation plasticity enhances crypsis in larval newts: associated metabolic cost and background choice behaviour
results.author: Nuria Polo-Cavia
results.takeaway: Newt larvae exhibit considerable pigmentation plasticity, enhancing their concealment against predators regardless of perceived predation risk, but metabolic costs may constrain their camouflage in dim habitats.

results.title: Transgenerational plasticity research: Challenges and opportunities
results.author: C. McAndry
results.takeaway: Transgenerational plasticity research can advance our understanding of organismal evolution and climate change responses by clarifying terminology and integrating parallel processes.

results.title: The conspicuous postmetamorphic coloration of fire salamanders, but not their toxicity, is affected by larval background albedo.
results.author: Eugenia Sanchez
results.journal: Journal of experimental zoology. Part B, Molecular and developmental evolution
results.takeaway: Fire salamanders' black-and-yellow coloration is conspicuous to predators at night, but not their toxicity, as larval background albedo does not affect their alkaloid profile.

results.title: Factors determining the dorsal coloration pattern of aposematic salamanders
results.author: Benedetta Barzaghi
results.takeaway: Environmental conditions and food availability are more important than local adaptations in determining differences in aposematic coloration patterns of salamanders.

results.title: Pigmentation enhancement techniques during ornamental fish production
results.author: Cher Chien Lau
results.journal: Reviews in Fish Biology and Fisheries
results.takeaway: Feed additives and tank color and light are key factors in enhancing ornamental fish body pigmentation and patterns, offering valuable insights for boosting the breeding industry.

results.title: ADAPTIVE COLORATION AND GENE FLOW AS A CONSTRAINT TO LOCAL ADAPTATION IN THE STREAMSIDE SALAMANDER, AMBYSTOMA BARBOURI
results.author: Andrew Storfer
results.takeaway: Larvae of the streamside salamander, Ambystoma barbouri, tend to be lighter in permanent streams, less conspicuous to fish, and have higher survival, while those in ephemeral streams are darker and more conspicuous to predators.

results.title: Developmental costs of yellow colouration in fire salamanders and experiments to test the efficiency of yellow as a warning colouration
results.author: B. Caspers
results.takeaway: Yellow coloration in fire salamanders reduces predation risk, but its development is condition-dependent and potentially costly.

results.title: Fish skin pigmentation in aquaculture: the influence of rearing conditions and its neuroendocrine regulation.
results.author: P. Vissio
results.takeaway: Fish skin pigmentation in aquaculture is influenced by neuroendocrine regulation and rearing conditions, which impact its market value and welfare.

results.title: Does tank background colour influence the growth, survival, and carotenoid content in fishes? An illustration in filament barb, Dawkinsia filamentosa (Valenciennes, 1844)
results.author: N. Padhi
results.takeaway: Black background color is the best tank color for rearing and production of filament barb, with higher growth rate, survival rate, and carotenoid content compared to other tank colors.

results.title: Which pigment appears first in the corolla—patterned or background?
results.author: Eapsa Berry
results.takeaway: In 28 out of 35 studied species, pigment pattern appears in the corolla earlier than background color, with a tendency towards earlier appearance in the corolla.

results.title: Functional colour genes and signals of selection in colour‐polymorphic salamanders
results.author: J. Burgon
results.takeaway: European fire salamanders show functional associations between color morphs and genes, suggesting that current ecological and evolutionary hypotheses may need revision.

results.title: The Effect of Background Color on Skin Color Variation of Juvenile Plectropomus leopardus
results.author: Feibiao Song
results.journal: Animals : an Open Access Journal from MDPI
results.takeaway: A white background is more conducive to maintaining red skin color in juvenile Plectropomus leopardus, while black and red backgrounds cause darkening in response to other colors.

results.title: Editorial: Evo-Devo of Color Pattern Formation
results.author: R. Mallarino
results.takeaway: Advances in genomic, molecular, and imaging approaches reveal the mechanistic basis of color pattern formation in animal species, providing insights into evolutionary developmental biology and phenotypic diversity.

results.title: A methodological workflow for quantitative colouration and colour pattern comparison reveals taxonomic and habitat‐level differences in the polymorphic fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra)
results.author: L. Alarcón‐Ríos
results.takeaway: This study effectively detects differences in color patterns in the polymorphic fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra) at both taxonomic and habitat levels, revealing an increased prevalence of melanistic coloration and less homogeneous color pattern in urban settings.

results.title: Larval Pigmentation Reveals Environmental and Genetic Influences in Hybridizing Ambystoma Salamanders
results.author: Alfredo Ascanio
results.takeaway: Hybrid Ambystoma salamander larvae show intermediate UVR responses, with greater similarity to their maternal phenotype, suggesting potential performance reduction if intermediate pigmentation is suboptimal.

results.title: Blue, Black, and Stripes: Evolution and Development of Color Production and Pattern Formation in Lizards and Snakes
results.author: Takeo Kuriyama
results.takeaway: Lizards and snakes' color patterns are influenced by pigment cells and genetic factors during embryogenesis, improving our understanding of reptilian color pattern evolution.

results.title: Skin Colour in Salamanders Is Modulated by Both Epitranscriptomic Methylation and Gene Expression
results.author: Nicholas Strowbridge
results.takeaway: Multiple molecular mechanisms, including gene expression and RNA methylation, contribute to salamander color diversity, with a positive correlation and significant overlap in transcripts.

results.title: Effects of background color on pigmentation, morphological traits, and behavior in the European tree frog (Hyla arborea, Hylidae, Anura) tadpoles
results.author: Marko Mirc
results.takeaway: European tree frog tadpoles can rapidly change body pigmentation to achieve crypsis, with reversible color changes, and can actively choose an appropriate background for maximum crypsis.

results.title: Zebrafish Pigment Pattern Formation: Insights into the Development and Evolution of Adult Form.
results.author: Larissa B. Patterson
results.takeaway: Zebrafish pigment patterns are shaped by precise coordination of pigment cell lineage specification, differentiation, and cellular interactions, providing insights into pattern diversification in vertebrates.

results.title: EffEcts of background color and prEdation risk on color changE in firE salamandEr larvaE
results.author: O. Segev
results.takeaway: Fire salamander larvae rapidly change color to become less conspicuous against contrasting backgrounds, with predator presence further enhancing this response.

results.title: Evolutionary and genomic associations of colour and pattern in fire and Alpine salamanders (Salamandra Spp.)
results.author: J. Burgon
results.takeaway: This study provides greater phylogenetic resolution for the genus Salamandra and confirms the convergent evolution of reproductive and color phenotypes, highlighting the need for taxonomic revisions and understanding of amphibian coloration.

results.title: The inbred newt genome unveils molecular mechanisms of behavior, development, and regeneration in urodele amphibians
results.author: Yuki Kimura
results.takeaway: The inbred newt genome provides insights into amphibian evolution, behavior, development, and regeneration, offering a valuable model organism for studying vertebrate development and regeneration.

results.title: Homeostatic and regenerative neurogenesis in salamanders
results.author: A. Joven
results.takeaway: Salamanders exhibit large-scale regeneration in the adult central nervous system, enabling functional recovery in retina, brain, and spinal cord, with recent technological advances aiding in understanding regenerative processes.

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: salamanders
results.author: A. Joven
results.takeaway: Salamanders are key models for regeneration, demonstrating remarkable abilities to regrow tissues, organs, and even whole body parts, providing insights into cell, tissue, and organ regeneration mechanisms.

results.title: Evolutionary Insights into the Relationship of Frogs, Salamanders, and Caecilians and Their Adaptive Traits, with an Emphasis on Salamander Regeneration and Longevity
results.author: Bin Lu
results.journal: Animals : an Open Access Journal from MDPI
results.takeaway: Salamander genomes have undergone accelerated adaptive evolution, with genes like and potentially linked to regeneration and longevity, potentially benefiting human well-being.

results.title: Hybridization and extensive mitochondrial introgression among fire salamanders in peninsular Italy
results.author: Roberta Bisconti
results.takeaway: Fire salamanders in peninsular Italy show extensive mitochondrial introgression, triggering mitonuclear discordance and highlighting the complexity of mechanisms triggering mitonuclear discordance in animals.

results.title: Genetic and morphological data demonstrate hybridization and backcrossing in a pair of salamanders at the far end of the speciation continuum
results.author: J. Arntzen
results.takeaway: Hybridization and backcrossing occur in deep diverged salamander species, with fluctuating range boundaries, ecological segregation, and cytonuclear incompatibilities contributing to species integrity despite incomplete isolation during secondary contact.

results.title: Developmental Basis and Consequences of a Key Innovation in Lungless Salamanders
results.author: J. Hanken
results.takeaway: Lungless salamanders' evolutionary success may be linked to novel developmental mechanisms and a novel gene paralog that expresses surfactant-associated protein C outside the lung.

results.title: Heterochrony, cannibalism, and the evolution of viviparity in Salamandra salamandra
results.author: D. Buckley
results.takeaway: Heterochrony and intrauterine cannibalism contribute to the evolution of viviparity in the fire salamander, a unique model system for studying evolutionary developmental research at the population level.

results.title: Genetic drift and rapid evolution of viviparity in insular fire salamanders (Salamandra salamandra)
results.author: G. Velo‐Antón
results.takeaway: Rising sea levels caused the isolation of island fire salamander populations 9000 years ago, leading to rapid genetic differentiation and rapid evolution of viviparity.

results.title: Colour polymorphism in Salamandra salamandra (Amphibia: Urodela), revealed by a lack of genetic and environmental differentiation between distinct phenotypes
results.author: W. Beukema
results.journal: Journal of Zoological Systematics and Evolutionary Research
results.takeaway: Colour polymorphism exists in Salamandra salamandra, but the subspecies S. s. alfredschmidti should be reclassified as a junior synonym of S. s. bernardezi due to lack of genetic and environmental differentiation between distinct phenotypes.

results.title: ‘Mainland-island’ population structure of a terrestrial salamander in a forest-bocage landscape with little evidence for in situ ecological speciation
results.author: J. Arntzen
results.takeaway: The fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra) shows a'mainland-island' population structure in a forest-bocage landscape, with no evidence of adaptive genetic divergence in pond versus stream larval habitats, suggesting a hybrid zone rather than speciation in

results.title: DISPERSAL OF VIVIPARITY ACROSS CONTACT ZONES IN IBERIAN POPULATIONS OF FIRE SALAMANDERS (SALAMANDRA) INFERRED FROM DISCORDANCE OF GENETIC AND MORPHOLOGICAL TRAITS
results.author: Mario García-París
results.takeaway: Viviparity likely arose only once within Salamandra salamandra, with genetic and molecular traits discordant across contact zones in Iberian populations.

results.title: Variability of colour pattern and genetic diversity of Salamandra salamandra (Caudata: Salamandridae) in the Czech Republic
results.author: Jindřich Brejcha
results.takeaway: The striped phenotype of fire salamanders in the Czech Republic is not associated with the S. s. terrestris lineage, but is found more frequently in the northwest than in the rest of the country.

results.title: Tracing the first step to speciation: ecological and genetic differentiation of a salamander population in a small forest
results.author: S. Steinfartz
results.takeaway: The fire salamander, Salamandra salamandra, has evolved specific adaptations to different ecological conditions and genetic differentiation, suggesting a co-evolution of habitat adaptations and mating signals.

results.title: A molecular phylogeny of ‘true’ salamanders (family Salamandridae) and the evolution of terrestriality of reproductive modes
results.author: M. Veith
results.journal: Journal of Zoological Systematics and Evolutionary Research
results.takeaway: The phylogeny of 'true' salamanders suggests that terrestrial reproductive modes evolved independently, with some species showing convergent evolution of adaptations.

results.title: Ecological, Biological and Genetic Adaptation to Xeric Habitats of Salamandra infraimmaculata on the Southern Border of Its Distribution
results.author: G. Degani
results.takeaway: Salamandra infraimmaculata adapts to semi-arid habitats mainly through terrestrial phases, with little aquatic phase involvement, and shows molecular genetic variation among different areas.

results.title: Mitochondrial sequence analysis of Salamandra taxa suggests old splits of major lineages and postglacial recolonizations of Central Europe from distinct source populations of Salamandra salamandra
results.author: S. Steinfartz
results.takeaway: Salamandra salamandra has recolonized Central Europe from distinct source populations, suggesting it was the only species to do so after the last glaciation.

results.title: Repeated ecological and life cycle transitions make salamanders an ideal model for evolution and development
results.author: Ronald M. Bonett
results.takeaway: Salamanders serve as a model for understanding how developmental patterns evolve and lead to phenotypic diversification after shifts to new adaptive zones.

results.title: Hybridizing salamanders experience accelerated diversification
results.author: Austin H. Patton
results.takeaway: Hybridizing salamander lineages experience significantly greater net-diversification rates than non-hybridizing lineages, driven by increased speciation rates and decreased extinction rates.

results.title: Independent evolutionary transitions to pueriparity across multiple timescales in the viviparous genus Salamandra.
results.author: Kevin P. Mulder
results.takeaway: Five independent transitions to pueriparity have occurred in the viviparous genus Salamandra, spanning multiple timescales and highlighting the need for taxonomic revisions in the genus.

results.title: Metamorphosis shapes cranial diversity and rate of evolution in salamanders
results.author: Anne‐Claire Fabre
results.takeaway: Metamorphosis promotes cranial evolution in salamanders, requiring greater autonomy of cranial elements and facilitating rapid evolution of regions remodelled through ontogeny.

results.title: Allopatric diversification and evolutionary melting pot in a North African Palearctic relict: The biogeographic history of Salamandra algira.
results.author: M. Dinis
results.takeaway: Climate-driven refugia in North Africa play a crucial role in promoting allopatric diversification and persistence of the North African fire salamander, Salamandra algira.

results.title: The evolution of viviparity in holocene islands: ecological adaptation versus phylogenetic descent along the transition from aquatic to terrestrial environments
results.author: G. Velo‐Antón
results.journal: Journal of Zoological Systematics and Evolutionary Research
results.takeaway: Viviparity in Salamandra salamandra island populations is an evolutionary novelty, and considering these populations as an evolutionary unit for conservation purposes is crucial.

results.title: A biogeographic and ecological perspective to the evolution of reproductive behaviour in the family Salamandridae.
results.author: Sarah Kieren
results.takeaway: The family Salamandridae has a diverse reproductive behavior, but no significant changes in habitat type have significantly influenced mating behavior.

results.title: Urban Life Affects Differentiation and Phenotypic Variation but not Asymmetry in a Fully Terrestrial Salamander
results.author: L. Alarcón‐Ríos
results.takeaway: Urban life affects differentiation and phenotypic variation in fully terrestrial salamander populations, but does not significantly impact morphological asymmetry or developmental stability.

results.title: Cast away: drift as the main determinant for larval survival in western fire salamanders (Salamandra salamandra) in headwater streams
results.author: T. Reinhardt
results.takeaway: High summer precipitation is the main cause of mortality for western fire salamander larvae in headwater streams, with drift potentially influencing their evolutionary processes and ecological prevalence.

results.title: The Dry‐Climate Hypothesis: Identifying the Environmental Drivers of Terrestrial Viviparous Salamanders
results.author: M. Dinis
results.takeaway: The dry-climate hypothesis suggests that the transition from larviparous to pueriparous reproduction in viviparous salamanders is driven by the absence of water for larval deposition.

results.title: Comparative landscape genetics reveals the evolution of viviparity reduces genetic connectivity in fire salamanders
results.author: A. Lourenço
results.takeaway: The evolution of viviparity in fire salamanders leads to greater differentiation and reduced genetic connectivity compared to larviparous populations, possibly due to water courses and agricultural areas.

results.title: Landscape resistance constrains hybridization across contact zones in a reproductively and morphologically polymorphic salamander
results.author: G. Velo‐Antón
results.takeaway: Landscape resistance constrains hybridization across contact zones in a polymorphic salamander, with high levels of introgression between subspecies and distinct phenotypes, but environmental heterogeneity plays a crucial role in evolutionary dynamics.

results.title: Microenvironment, reproductive tactics and morphology in Mediterranean Salamandra
results.author: D. Escoriza
results.takeaway: High humidity in Mediterranean Salamandra habitats may facilitate shifts into new environmental niches and the emergence of novel adaptive phenotypes, but is not the sole factor driving these divergences.

results.title: Coincident transitions across elevation and origins of functional innovations drove the phenotypic and ecological diversity of lungless salamanders.
results.author: E. Burress
results.journal: Evolution; international journal of organic evolution
results.takeaway: Elevation and functional innovations significantly shape the ecological and phenotypic diversity of lungless salamanders, with lower elevations leading to rapid phenotypic evolution and higher elevations reducing it.

results.title: Hybridization during altitudinal range shifts: nuclear introgression leads to extensive cyto‐nuclear discordance in the fire salamander
results.author: R. Pereira
results.takeaway: Hybridization between ecomorphs of the fire salamander can lead to alternative evolutionary outcomes, such as genetic merger or gene flow, rather than extinction and replacement in response to climate change.
