results.title: The biology ofApanteles medicaginisMuesebeck (hymenoptera: Braconidae)
results.author: W. Allen
results.journal: University of California, Agriculture and Natural Resources
results.takeaway: Apanteles medicaginis Muesebeck effectively prevents alfalfa damage by killing host caterpillars before they can feed heavily, making it a crucial parasite for the genus Apanteles.

results.title: Mmp-induced fat body cell dissociation promotes pupal development and moderately averts pupal diapause by activating lipid metabolism
results.author: Qiangqiang Jia
results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
results.takeaway: Mmp-induced fat body cell dissociation promotes pupal development and moderately averts pupal diapause in insects, with its inhibition increasing diapause risk.

results.title: Record of Lema pectoralis Baly, 1865 (Coleoptera: Chrysomelidae) on the beaked micropera orchid Micropera rostrata (Roxb.) N. P. Balakr., 1970, Philippine ground orchid Spathoglottis plicata Blume, 1825 and Papilionanthe teres (Roxb.) Schltr. (Orchidaceae: Epidendroideae)
results.author: G. Ragesh
results.takeaway: Red palm weevil larvae can be successfully reared on pineapple, making it a simple, efficient, and cost-effective method compared to sugar cane, date palm bolts, and artificial diet.

results.title: Eating Caterpillars
results.author: M. Samston

results.title: Neonicotinoids can cause arrested pupal ecdysis in Lepidoptera
results.author: Niranjana Krishnan
results.takeaway: Neonicotinoids can cause arrested pupal ecdysis in Lepidoptera larvae, potentially disrupting crustacean cardioactive peptide neurons and causing delayed development.

results.title: Caterpillar-Induced Volatile Emissions in Cotton: The Relative Importance of Damage and Insect-Derived Factors
results.author: C. C. Arce
results.takeaway: Cotton plants release volatile compounds in response to caterpillar attack, with damage-associated molecular patterns and insect-associated molecular patterns playing a role, but other factors must be involved for enhanced resistance.

results.title: A dynamical model of growth and maturation in Drosophila
results.author: J. Tyson
results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
results.takeaway: The size-sensing mechanism that initiates metamorphosis in Drosophila larvae occurs before reaching a critical weight, and involves interactions between body size, ecdysone, and nutritional signaling.

results.title: Caterpillars of the marsh fritillary butterfly Euphydryas aurinia can extend their life-cycle in Scotland
results.author: N. Ravenscroft
results.takeaway: Caterpillars of the marsh fritillary butterfly Euphydryas aurinia can extend their life-cycle in Scotland, potentially contributing to its persistence in mild climates.

results.title: Salivary surprise: Symmerista caterpillars anoint petioles with red saliva after clipping leaves
results.author: D. E. Dussourd
results.takeaway: Leaf clipping by Symmerista caterpillars is primarily to introduce salivary constituents into the plant, preventing defenses from mobilizing in nearby leaves where the caterpillar feeds next.

results.title: The sensory ecology of caterpillars
results.author: Sam J. England
results.journal: Journal of Comparative Physiology. A, Neuroethology, Sensory, Neural, and Behavioral Physiology
results.takeaway: Caterpillar sensory ecology provides valuable insights into ecology, evolution, conservation, and management, but more comparative studies and knowledge gaps are needed.

results.title: Juvenile responses to immune challenges are not carried through to subsequent life stages in an insect
results.author: F. W. S. Silva
results.takeaway: High population density and immune challenges during larval stages of the moth Anticarsia gemmatalis trigger increased lytic activity, but this effect is transient and does not persist into later stages.

results.title: The steroid hormone 20-hydroxyecdysone binds to dopamine receptor to repress lepidopteran insect feeding and promote pupation
results.author: Xin-Le Kang
results.takeaway: 20-hydroxyecdysone (20E) binds to the dopamine receptor (DopEcR) to stop larval feeding and promote pupation in lepidopteran insects, such as the agricultural pest Helicoverpa armigera.

results.title: Regulatory Mechanisms of Vitellogenesis in Insects
results.author: Zhongxia Wu
results.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
results.takeaway: Insect vitellogenesis is regulated by hormones, microRNA, and nutritional pathways, aiding in understanding insect reproduction and developing new strategies for pest control.

results.title: Physiological and Molecular Mechanisms of Lepidopteran Insects: Genomic Insights and Applications of Genome Editing for Future Research
results.author: Dongsheng Niu
results.takeaway: Integrating genomic data into pest control strategies can help reduce reliance on chemical insecticides and promote environmentally friendly integrated pest management approaches.

results.title: Molecular mechanisms of sex determination in Lepidoptera: current status and perspectives
results.author: F. Marec
results.takeaway: The molecular mechanisms of sex determination in Lepidoptera show considerable diversity, with Masc playing a conserved role in male sex determination and dosage compensation in most species.

results.title: Gustatory receptors in Lepidoptera: chemosensation and beyond
results.author: A. Agnihotri
results.takeaway: Lepidopteran gustatory receptors play a crucial role in chemosensation, host selection, and adaptation, and could be targets for effective insect control strategies.

results.title: Egg Formation in Lepidoptera
results.author: W. Telfer
results.takeaway: Lepidopteran egg formation has unique traits, contributing to our understanding of egg formation in insects generally.

results.title: Mutation of a lepidopteran-specific PMP-like protein, BmLSPMP-like, induces a stick body shape in silkworm, Bombyx mori.
results.author: D. Tan
results.takeaway: BmLSPMP-like dysfunction in silkworms leads to a stick-like body shape, potentially offering eco-friendly targets for lepidopteran pest management.

results.title: IMMUNITY IN LEPIDOPTERAN INSECTS
results.author: Haobo Jiang
results.journal: Advances in experimental medicine and biology
results.takeaway: Lepidopteran insects exhibit innate immunity, recognizing infectious microorganisms and triggering phagocytic responses, which can be applied to combat agricultural pests.

results.title: Convergent Molecular Evolution Associated With Repeated Transitions to Gregarious Larval Behavior in Heliconiini
results.author: F. Cicconardi
results.takeaway: Social living significantly alters selection pressures on physiological, immunological, and behavioral traits in Heliconiini butterflies, leading to repeated convergent shifts towards gregarious larvae.

results.title: The Circadian Clock in Lepidoptera
results.author: D. Brady
results.takeaway: The circadian clock in Lepidoptera plays a crucial role in controlling developmental, mating, and migration phenotypes, impacting both pest control and beneficial rearing of beneficial species.

results.title: Evolutionary Novelty of Apolipoprotein D Facilitates Metabolic Plasticity in Lepidopteran Wings
results.author: Shun-Ze Jia
results.takeaway: Duplicated Apolipoprotein D (ApoD) plays a crucial role in lipid and energy homeostasis in lepidopteran wings, shaping adaptive metabolic regulatory networks during wing phenotypic evolution.

results.title: Immune functions of pattern recognition receptors in Lepidoptera
results.author: Lin Zhao
results.takeaway: Pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) play a crucial role in recognizing pathogen-associated molecular patterns and initiating effective defense responses in Lepidoptera, with potential for wider recognition of signaling molecules.

results.title: Pattern recognition receptors from lepidopteran insects and their biological functions.
results.author: Zhe Lin
results.takeaway: Lepidopteran insects have potent innate immunity against pathogens, with pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) playing a crucial role in recognizing pathogen-associated molecular patterns and initiating immune responses.

results.title: How do moth and butterfly taste?—Molecular basis of gustatory receptors in Lepidoptera
results.author: W. Xu
results.takeaway: Advances in sequencing, cellular biology, and CRISPR technologies have revealed the molecular mechanisms of Lepidopteran gustatory receptors, guiding insect feeding behaviors and interactions with plants.

results.title: Molecular Mechanisms Underlying Resistance to Bacillus thuringiensis Cry Toxins in Lepidopteran Pests: An Updated Research Perspective
results.author: Deqin Hu
results.takeaway: Lepidopteran pest resistance to Bt crops is primarily due to mutations and alterations in midgut receptor genes, and innovative pest control strategies can address this issue.

results.title: Chemical, Physiological and Molecular Responses of Host Plants to Lepidopteran Egg-Laying
results.author: C. Bertea
results.takeaway: Plants respond to lepidopteran egg-laying with direct and indirect defenses, including necrosis, neoplasm formation, and production of ovicidal compounds, to protect against larval damage and attract natural enemies.

results.title: Transcriptomic analysis of the testicular fusion in Spodoptera litura
results.author: Yaqing Chen
results.takeaway: MMPs play a critical role in testicular fusion in Spodoptera litura, contributing to sperm production and the pest's widespread presence in Asia.

results.title: An Overview of Mechanisms of Cry Toxin Resistance in Lepidopteran Insects
results.author: Bianca Peterson
results.takeaway: Lepidopteran insect resistance to cry toxins is highly complex, with altered binding sites being the most common mechanism, and it is unclear if all these sites are regulated by an MAPK signaling pathway.

results.title: Molecular basis of circadian rhythm divergence between diurnal and nocturnal lepidoperans
results.author: Guiyun Li
results.takeaway: Metabolic differences and light sensitivity differences underpin the behavioral differences between diurnal and nocturnal Lepidoptera species, such as the black cutworm and monarch butterfly.

results.title: A Molecular View of Autophagy in Lepidoptera
results.author: D. Romanelli
results.takeaway: Autophagy plays a crucial role in larval organ remodeling and degeneration during metamorphosis in Lepidoptera, with potential applications in both basic research and practical applications.

results.title: Comparative genomics reveals the dynamics of chromosome evolution in Lepidoptera
results.author: C. Wright
results.takeaway: Lepidopteran chromosomes are largely intact, with only eight lineages undergoing extensive reorganization through fission or fusion events.

results.title: Genetic parallelism underpins convergent mimicry coloration in Lepidoptera across 120 million years of evolution
results.author: Yacine Ben Chehida
results.takeaway: Convergent color pattern evolution in Lepidoptera is highly constrained and predictable, with similar genetic variants influencing wing coloration across multiple lineages over 120 million years.

results.title: A major gene controls mimicry and crypsis in butterflies and moths
results.author: Nicola J. Nadeau
results.takeaway: Cortex gene controls mimicry and cryptis in butterflies and moths, suggesting it is a major target for natural selection in color and pattern variation in Lepidoptera.

results.title: A determining factor for insect feeding preference in the silkworm, Bombyx mori
results.author: Zhongjie Zhang
results.takeaway: The GR66 gene is responsible for the mulberry-specific feeding preference of the silkworm Bombyx mori, and its mutation can lead to a wider range of plant species being consumed.

results.title: A microRNA is the effector gene of a classic evolutionary hotspot locus
results.author: Shen Tian
results.takeaway: A microRNA plays a major role in regulating melanic wing color in butterflies, driving adaptive evolution by repressing multiple pigmentation genes across three diverged lineages.

results.title: Molecular biology and genetics of the Lepidoptera
results.author: M. Goldsmith
results.takeaway: Lepidoptera are important models for studying molecular biology and genetics, with potential applications in pest management and human pathogen research.

results.title: The Lepidoptera Odorant Binding Protein gene family: Gene gain and loss within the GOBP/PBP complex of moths and butterflies.
results.author: R. Vogt
results.takeaway: The Lepidoptera GOBP/PBP complex is a monophyletic lineage with origins deep within Lepidoptera phylogeny, and butterflies may have lost a PBP gene that plays an important role in moth pheromone detection, suggesting shared chemosensory-based

results.title: Phylogenomics reveals the evolutionary timing and pattern of butterflies and moths
results.author: A. Kawahara
results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
results.takeaway: Butterflies became day-flying in the Late Cretaceous, moth hearing organs evolved multiple times before the evolutionary arms race with bats, and Lepidoptera played a crucial role in terrestrial ecosystems.

results.title: Molecular Model Systems in the Lepidoptera
results.author: M. Goldsmith
results.takeaway: Lepidoptera serve as valuable model systems for studying hormone action on the central nervous system, immune response, and developmental biology.

results.title: Gene Family Evolution Suggests Correlated Dietary Adaptations in Butterflies and Moths
results.author: Yi-Ming Weng
results.takeaway: Butterflies and moths have evolved to adapt to and diversify on angiosperm hosts through horizontal gene transfer events, involving digestion, detoxification, and immunity gene families.

results.title: Molecular Evolution of the Odorant and Gustatory Receptor Genes in Lepidopteran Insects: Implications for Their Adaptation and Speciation
results.author: Patamarerk Engsontia
results.takeaway: Lepidopteran odorant and gustatory receptor genes have undergone strong purifying selection, with gene family expansion potentially aiding in their adaptation to plant hosts and pheromones.

results.title: Contrasting patterns of evolutionary constraint and novelty revealed by comparative sperm proteomic analysis in Lepidoptera
results.author: E. Whittington
results.takeaway: Sperm proteins in Lepidoptera exhibit significant genetic novelty, potentially linked to the origin and evolution of heteromorphic spermatogenesis and the evolution of this unique reproductive system.

results.title: Electrostatic pollination by butterflies and moths
results.author: Sam J. England
results.journal: Journal of the Royal Society Interface
results.takeaway: Butterflies and moths accumulate electrostatic charge while in flight, generating electric fields over 5 kVm, which can elicit contactless pollen transfer from flowers across air gaps, potentially reflecting evolutionary adaptations.

results.title: Gregariousness in lepidopteran larvae
results.author: Chenyu Qian
results.takeaway: Lepidopteran larvae's gregarious lifestyle is driven by ecological and evolutionary factors, leading to improved larval survival and accelerated development, but may diminish with development.

results.title: Long-range seasonal migration in insects: mechanisms, evolutionary drivers and ecological consequences.
results.author: J. Chapman
results.takeaway: Insect migration research has made significant advances, improving our understanding of navigation strategies, sun compass orientation, and disease interactions.

results.title: Predatory and parasitic Lepidoptera: carnivores living on plants.
results.author: N. Pierce
results.takeaway: Predatory and parasitic Lepidoptera offer insights into ecology and evolution, with the butterfly family Lycaenidae being particularly rich in these feeding habits.

results.title: Towards an integrative approach to understanding collective behaviour in caterpillars
results.author: Callum F. McLellan
results.journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences
results.takeaway: Lepidopteran larvae provide a valuable study system for investigating the integrative biology of collective behavior, highlighting the complex interactions between ecological, morphological, and behavioral traits.

results.title: Ecology and evolution of cycad-feeding lepidoptera.
results.author: Melissa R. L. Whitaker
results.takeaway: Cycad-feeding Lepidoptera has evolved independently, with defensive traits playing a key role in their diversification and providing a promising study system for plant-insect coevolution and multi-trophic significance.

results.title: Two genomes of highly polyphagous lepidopteran pests (Spodoptera frugiperda, Noctuidae) with different host-plant ranges
results.author: A. Gouin
results.takeaway: The noctuid moth Spodoptera frugiperda has evolved to be polyphagous, eating a variety of crops, with tandem duplication as a possible adaptation mechanism and genomic differentiation.

results.title: Evolution of sexual dimorphism in the Lepidoptera.
results.author: C. Allen
results.takeaway: Sexual selection and natural selection play a crucial role in the evolution of sexual dimorphism in Lepidoptera, with potential constraints and facilitators affecting the development of sexual differences.

results.title: Aposematism and mimicry in caterpillars
results.author: M. Berenbaum
results.takeaway: Larval mimicry in Lepidoptera is fewer than adult mimicry, possibly due to a lack of research and reliance on visual cues for species recognition.

results.title: Gene novelty and gene family expansion in the early evolution of Lepidoptera
results.author: Asia E. Hoile
results.takeaway: The early evolution of Lepidoptera was driven by gene duplication and horizontal gene transfer, with two new gene families showing potential importance in Lepidopteran biology.

results.title: Evolution of wing shape in geometrid moths: phylogenetic effects dominate over ecology.
results.author: Kadri Ude
results.takeaway: Wing shape in geometrid moths shows a phylogenetically conservative pattern, with weak associations to environmental pressures optimizing aerodynamic performance.

results.title: Opsin Gene Duplication in Lepidoptera: Retrotransposition, Sex Linkage, and Gene Expression
results.author: P. Mulhair
results.takeaway: High rates of opsin duplications and changes in expression patterns have been observed across Lepidoptera, suggesting changes in color vision and sensory functions.

results.title: Ecology and evolution of pathogens in natural populations of Lepidoptera
results.author: J. Myers
results.takeaway: Insect pathogens play a crucial role in regulating host populations and influencing disease ecology and evolution in Lepidoptera, with environmental factors and diet playing key roles in virulence, transmission, and host resistance.

results.title: Diversity and Significance of Lepidoptera: A Phylogenetic Perspective
results.author: P. Goldstein
results.takeaway: Lepidoptera, including moths, butterflies, and skippers, play a significant role in human society and conservation efforts, offering valuable tools for studying evolutionary and ecological phenomena.

results.title: Expanding the Menu: Are Polyphagy and Gene Family Expansions Linked across Lepidoptera?
results.author: T. Breeschoten
results.takeaway: Gene family expansions in Lepidoptera are linked to polyphagy, with a positive correlation found between gene counts of detoxification gene families and polyphagy levels across the studied taxa.

results.title: The evolution and genetics of lepidopteran egg and caterpillar coloration.
results.author: X. Tong
results.takeaway: Lepidopteran egg and caterpillar coloration is influenced by genetics, developmental mechanisms, ecology, and evolution, with colors varying in developmental stages or response to different environments.

results.title: Pupal colour plasticity in the butterfly Catopsilia pomona (Lepidoptera: Pieridae)
results.author: Tarunkishwor Yumnam
results.journal: Biological Journal of the Linnean Society
results.takeaway: Pupal color plasticity in the butterfly Catopsilia pomona helps pupae match their substrate colors, with leaf-borne pupae tending to be greener and off-leaf pupae browner, influenced by leaf position, midrib thickness, and leaf length.

results.title: Pupal colour–pupation substrate correlation in butterflies
results.author: H. Mayekar
results.takeaway: Pupal color plasticity in butterflies is strongly correlated with pupation substrate choice, potentially protecting them against predation by matching their background.

results.title: Partially coupled reaction norms of pupal colour and spot size in a butterfly
results.author: H. Mayekar
results.takeaway: Pupal spot size in the tropical satyrine butterfly Mycalesis mineus is partially coupled with pupal color and substrate, suggesting a developmental link and potential function against predation.

results.title: A long noncoding RNA at the cortex locus controls adaptive coloration in butterflies
results.author: L. Livraghi
results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
results.takeaway: A long noncoding RNA, cortex, plays a key role in adaptive diversification of wing patterns in butterflies.

results.title: Induced Changes in the Pigmentation of the Pupoe of the Butterfly Pieris Napi L., and their Inheritance
results.author: J. Harrison
results.journal: Proceedings of The Royal Society B: Biological Sciences
results.takeaway: Exposure to orange light before pupation in Pieris Napi L. butterfly larvae leads to inherited green pupal pigmentation, affecting the appearance of the chrysalids.

results.title: Thermobiological effects of temperature‐induced color variations in Aglais urticae (Lepidoptera, Nymphalidae)
results.author: G. Markl
results.takeaway: Temperature-induced color variations in adult butterflies provide thermobiological benefits, with lower temperatures leading to darker coloration and higher temperatures leading to lighter individuals.

results.title: Identifying the proximal cue(s) for pupal color variation in the bordered patch butterfly, Chlosyne lacinia (Lepidoptera: Nymphalidae)
results.author: Jamie M. Phelps
results.journal: Annals of the Entomological Society of America
results.takeaway: Chlosyne lacinia pupae with higher melanization on black backgrounds have longer developmental periods, suggesting a trade-off between defense and developmental time.

results.title: Molecular Mechanisms Underlying Pupal Protective Color Switch in Papilio polytes Butterflies
results.author: S. Yoda
results.takeaway: Papilio polytes butterflies' pupal colors are regulated by melanin synthesis genes, tyrosine hydroxylase, and laccase 2, with green coloration mainly influenced by multiple bilin binding protein and juvenile hormone binding protein genes.

results.title: Color-pattern Modifications and Speciation in Butterflies of the Genus Vanessa and its Related Genera Cynthia and Bassaris
results.author: J. M. Otaki
results.takeaway: Spontaneous mutations in genes in a hypothetical pathway may play a major role in creating new color-patterns and species in the Vanessa genus, but not in the Cynthia genus.

results.title: Two different sensory mechanisms for the control of pupal protective coloration in butterflies.
results.author: Sota Hiraga
results.takeaway: In Graphium sarpedon, pupal coloration is determined by the illuminant difference between dorsal and ventral light, while in Papilio xuthus, it is determined by tactile signals from a rough surfaced pupation site.

results.title: Seasonal change in pupation behaviour and pupal mortality in a swallowtail butterfly
results.author: C. Stefanescu
results.takeaway: Seasonal changes in swallowtail butterfly pupation behavior and mortality rates suggest that pupation sites in litter and above ground level evolved to avoid strong bird predation on hostplants and to protect against both visual and non-visual predators.

results.title: Developmental dynamics of butterfly wings: real-time in vivo whole-wing imaging of twelve butterfly species
results.author: Masaki Iwata
results.takeaway: Butterfly wing development involves four sequential stages, with dynamic changes in tissue transparency, size, and color, suggesting common processes across butterfly species.

results.title: Lack of response to background colour in Pieris brassicae pupae reared on carotenoid-free diet
results.author: M. Rothschild
results.takeaway: Pieris brassicae pupae show heterochromy (background contrasting) rather than homochromy (background matching) when fed a carotenoid-free diet, likely due to toxic effects of the toxic plant.

results.title: Pupal colour dimorphism in a desert swallowtail (Lepidoptera: Papilionidae) is driven by changes in food availability, not photoperiod
results.author: Daniel Piñones‐Tapia
results.takeaway: Pupal coloration in desert swallowtail butterflies is driven by food availability, not photoperiod, with matching pupation site coloration potentially aiding in field survival.

results.title: Presence, species delimitation and identification of the Southern Small White butterfly Pieris mannii (Mayer, 1851) (Lepidoptera: Pieridae) in the Caucasus region
results.author: V. Lukhtanov
results.takeaway: DNA barcoding can accurately identify the Southern Small White butterfly Pieris mannii in the Caucasus region, despite its morphological similarity to P. napi pseudorapae.

results.title: Foraging Small White Butterflies, Pieris rapae, Search Flowers Using Color Vision
results.author: K. Arikawa
results.takeaway: Pieris rapae butterflies have true color vision and innately prefer blue and yellow disks for foraging, matching their flower preference in the field.

results.title:
Effect of density on pupal colour plasticity in the butterfly
 Mycalesis mineus
 (Lepidoptera, Nymphalidae)
results.author: H. Mayekar
results.takeaway: High larval densities in the butterfly Mycalesis mineus lead to a higher proportion of brown pupae, but results differed between two experiments.

results.title: Genetic parallelism underpins convergent mimicry coloration across Lepidoptera
results.author: Yacine Ben Chehida
results.takeaway: Convergent color pattern evolution in Lepidoptera is highly constrained, with genetic parallelism underlying similar color patterns across multiple species.

results.title: Carotenoids of the pupae of the Large White butterfly (Pieris brassicae) and the Small White butterfly (Pieris rapae)
results.author: M. Rothschild
results.takeaway: Diapausing pupae of the Large White and Small White butterflies contain more than double the concentration of carotenoids in their epidermis than non-diapausing pupae, and their green color can be modified by switching to long day regimes after feeding ceases.

results.title: Frizzled2 receives WntA signaling during butterfly wing pattern formation
results.author: Joseph J. Hanly
results.takeaway: Frizzled2 plays a cell-autonomous role in butterfly color pattern formation, forming a signaling axis with WntA, revealing the functional diversity of insect Frizzled receptors.

results.title: Melanocytes Sense Blue Light and Regulate Pigmentation through Opsin-3.
results.author: Claire Regazzetti
results.takeaway: OPN3 is the key sensor in melanocytes responsible for regulating pigmentation in skin type III and higher, offering potential targets for regulating melanogenesis and protecting dark skins against blue light exposure.

results.title: Skin Pigmentation and its Control: From Ultraviolet Radiation to Stem Cells
results.author: J. M. Yardman-Frank
results.takeaway: This review highlights the complex mechanisms of skin pigmentation, including the role of UV radiation, melanocyte stem cells, and potential interventions for pigmentation disorders.

results.title: The Pigmentation of Blue Light is Mediated by Both Melanogenesis Activation and Autophagy Inhibition through OPN3-TRPV1.
results.author: Eunbi Yu

results.title: NNT mediates redox-dependent pigmentation via a UVB- and MITF-independent mechanism
results.author: J. Allouche
results.takeaway: NNT-modifying topical drugs can target a redox-dependent pigmentation mechanism in skin, potentially benefiting medical and cosmetic purposes.

results.title: The Emerging Role of Visible Light in Melanocyte Biology and Skin Pigmentary Disorders: Friend or Foe?
results.author: Xuanxuan He
results.takeaway: Visible light has complex effects on melanocyte biology and skin pigmentary disorders, with different wavelengths potentially having positive or negative effects depending on interactions with specific chromophores, photoaging, and other photon-mediated reactions.

results.title: Opsin3—A Link to Visible Light-Induced Skin Pigmentation
results.author: Subba Rao Gangi Setty
results.takeaway: Visible light stimulates opsin3-regulated calcium-dependent microphthalmia-associated transcription factor activation, potentially contributing to long-lasting skin pigmentation in melanocompetent skins.

results.title: Visible light and human skin pigmentation: The importance of skin phototype
results.author: H. Moreiras
results.takeaway: Blue and green visible light can stimulate melanin production in fair-skinned individuals without the harmful consequences of UVR-induced pigmentation.

results.title: Clinical and molecular change induced by repeated low‐dose visible light exposure in both light‐skinned and dark‐skinned individuals
results.author: Sooyoung Kim
results.takeaway: Repeated low-dose visible light exposure causes immediate pigment darkening and delayed tanning in dark-skinned individuals, while no pigmentation or erythema is observed in light-skinned individuals.

results.title: Melanin Photosensitization and the Effect of Visible Light on Epithelial Cells
results.author: Orlando Chiarelli-Neto
results.takeaway: Visible light can damage melanocytes and cause DNA damage, potentially leading to photoaging and skin cancer.

results.title: New data on hyperpigmentation disorders
results.author: S. Schalka
results.journal: Journal of the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology
results.takeaway: UV, visible, and infrared light contribute to skin pigmentation, and adequate sunscreens with iron oxides are effective in preventing it.

results.title: The Aqueous Extract of Polypodium leucotomos (Fernblock®) Regulates Opsin 3 and Prevents Photooxidation of Melanin Precursors on Skin Cells Exposed to Blue Light Emitted from Digital Devices
results.author: Mikel Portillo
results.takeaway: Fernblock protects skin cells from blue light damage and early photoaging by regulating Opsin-3 and preventing melanin photooxidation.

results.title: Mechanisms of Ultraviolet Light‐Induced Pigmentation
results.author: Barbara A. Gilchrest
results.takeaway: Ultraviolet light-induced melanogenesis in the skin may serve as a protective tan, offering potential for novel therapeutic approaches to minimize acute and chronic photodamage.

results.title: Melanin’s Journey from Melanocytes to Keratinocytes: Uncovering the Molecular Mechanisms of Melanin Transfer and Processing
results.author: Liliana Bento-Lopes
results.takeaway: Understanding the molecular mechanisms regulating skin pigmentation can lead to novel therapeutic strategies for treating hypo- or hyper-pigmentation disorders and cosmetic applications.

results.title: Visible Light Protection Strategies for Diverse Populations
results.author: Willie Visser
results.takeaway: Visible light protection strategies, including tinted sunscreens and antioxidants, are crucial for individuals with skin of color and visible-light-sensitive dermatoses, to reduce skin damage and improve clinical outcomes.

results.title: MITF and UV responses in skin: from pigmentation to addiction
results.author: Nhu Nguyen
results.takeaway: The pigmentation response to UVR, driven by MITF, provides protection against DNA damage and carcinogenesis, while the opioid response may promote sun-seeking behavior to prevent vitamin D deficiency.

results.title: Visible Light Induces Melanogenesis in Human Skin through a Photoadaptive Response
results.author: Manpreet Randhawa
results.takeaway: Multiple exposures to visible light can cause darker and sustained pigmentation in human skin, impacting management of photo-aggravated pigmentary disorders and sunscreen use.

results.title: UV light activates a Gαq/11-coupled phototransduction pathway in human melanocytes
results.author: Nicholas W. Bellono
results.takeaway: UV light activates a Gq/11-dependent phototransduction pathway in human melanocytes, causing increased skin pigmentation and potentially contributing to skin cancer and photoaging.

results.title: Two light‐activated neuroendocrine circuits arising in the eye trigger physiological and morphological pigmentation
results.author: G. Bertolesi
results.takeaway: Eye photoperception links physiological and morphological pigmentation by altering -MSH and melatonin production, respectively.

results.title: Pigmentation effects of blue light irradiation on skin and how to protect against them
results.author: R. Campiche
results.takeaway: Blue light irradiation can cause visible skin pigmentation, but both microalga Scenedesmus rubescens extract and niacinamide can protect against this effect.

results.title: Clinical and Biological Characterization of Skin Pigmentation Diversity and Its Consequences on UV Impact
results.author: S. Del Bino
results.takeaway: Skin pigmentation diversity influences skin sensitivity to UV exposure, with lighter or darker skin types being more prone to sun-related issues.

results.title: Analysis of the genetic loci of pigment pattern evolution in vertebrates
results.author: J. Elkin
results.takeaway: Cis-regulatory mutations contribute more to vertebrate pigmentation patterns, with carotenoid-based pigmentation and pattern boundaries being more affected, and genes involved in developmental processes being more affected.

results.title: Deciphering the molecular basis of skin color variation through transcriptomics and machine learning

results.title: Muscle and neuronal guidepost-like cells facilitate planarian visual system regeneration
results.author: M. L. Scimone
results.takeaway: Muscle and neuronal guidepost-like cells in the planarian visual system promote de novo assembly of the visual system after injury or eye transplantation, providing a mechanism for axon pattern restoration in regeneration.

results.title: Regenerating Eye Tissues to Preserve and Restore Vision
results.author: J. Stern
results.takeaway: Ocular regenerative therapies show promise in treating various blinding disorders, with potential for a deep portfolio of sight-restoring stem cell-based medicine.

results.title: Photoreceptor transplantation: anatomic, electrophysiologic, and behavioral evidence for the functional reconstruction of retinas lacking photoreceptors.
results.author: Martin S. Silverman
results.takeaway: Photoreceptor transplantation can potentially reconstruct retinas lacking photoreceptors, potentially restoring visual activity and behavioral responses to sensory stimulation.

results.title: Technical Feasibility of Whole-eye Vascular Composite Allotransplantation: A Systematic Review
results.author: Matteo Laspro
results.journal: Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery Global Open
results.takeaway: Whole-eye transplantation (WET) appears feasible with potential for functional restoration, but optic nerve regeneration remains undetermined.

results.title: The Effect of Replantation, Lens Removal, and Optic Nerve Section of the Eye of the Salamander (Triturus Viridescens)
results.author: R. R. Chace
results.journal: The Yale Journal of Biology and Medicine
results.takeaway: Replantation and transplantation of eyes in salamanders can return vision, while animals higher than amphibia do not show vision return after eyeball transplantation.

results.title: Regenerating Eye Tissues to Preserve and Restore Vision.
results.author: J. Stern
results.takeaway: Regenerating eye tissues using stem cells could preserve and restore vision in patients with eye diseases.

results.title: Cell replacement and visual restoration by retinal sheet transplants
results.author: M. Seiler
results.journal: Progress in retinal and eye research
results.takeaway: Retinal sheet transplantation using fetal-derived retinal progenitor cells and retinal pigment epithelium can effectively repair and restore function in degenerating retinas, potentially setting a standard for optimal cell replacement therapies.

results.title: Serotonergic stimulation induces nerve growth and promotes visual learning via posterior eye grafts in a vertebrate model of induced sensory plasticity
results.author: Douglas Blackiston
results.takeaway: Using a serotonergic drug, 5-HTagonist, can enhance innervation and integration of transplanted organs in regenerative medicine.

results.title: Principles of regeneration revealed by the planarian eye
results.author: P. Reddien
results.takeaway: Planarian eyes can regenerate, revealing principles of regeneration through constant progenitor production, spatial specification, and guidepost-like cells.

results.title: Reconnecting Eye to Brain
results.author: M. Crair
results.takeaway: This paper summarizes our understanding of visual system regeneration and provides a roadmap for future progress in restoring visual function after injury or disease.

results.title: Visual Restoration after Cataract Surgery Promotes Functional and Structural Brain Recovery
results.author: Haotian Lin
results.takeaway: Cataract surgery can functionally and structurally reverse cataract-induced brain changes, improving both visual and cognitive brain function.

results.title: Allogeneic whole-eye transplantation: advancements, challenges, and future directions in vision restoration
results.author: Lingxi Wei
results.takeaway: Allogeneic whole-eye transplantation shows promise for vision restoration, but current challenges and ethical considerations require further research to advance it to clinical reality.

results.title: Retinal ganglion cell repopulation for vision restoration in optic neuropathy: a roadmap from the RReSTORe Consortium
results.author: Jonathan R. Soucy
results.takeaway: Retinal ganglion cell repopulation shows promise for restoring vision in optic neuropathies, but requires further research and development in five key areas to overcome challenges and advance the field.

results.title: Return of Vision and Other Observations in Replanted Amphibian Eyes.
results.author: L. Stone
results.journal: Proceedings of the Society for Experimental Biology and Medicine
results.takeaway: Replantation of amphibian eyes can lead to vision recovery, but resorption of the eye may occur, with some replanted eyes reverting to their original size.

results.title: Reimplantation of eyes in fishes (Bahtygobius soporator) with recovery of vision.
results.author: Sperry Rw
results.takeaway: Reimplantation of eyes in fishes (Bahtygobius soporator) can result in visual recovery, highlighting the potential for functional regeneration of the optic nerve in these species.

results.title: A model for investigating developmental eye repair in Xenopus laevis
results.author: Cindy X. Kha
results.takeaway: Frog embryos can successfully repair their eyes after considerable tissue loss, with apoptosis playing a crucial role in this process.

results.title: Neuro-Ophthalmologic Hurdles in Whole-Eye Transplantation
results.author: M. Mayorquín-Ruiz
results.takeaway: Whole-eye transplantation faces challenges in optic nerve repair and regeneration, necessitating a multidisciplinary approach for successful outcomes.

results.title: Cellular and Molecular Triggers of Retinal Regeneration in Amphibians
results.author: Yuliya V Markitantova
results.takeaway: Amphibian retinal regeneration is triggered by specific signaling pathways, transcription factors, and the epigenome, potentially offering potential treatments for human retina diseases.

results.title: Molecular and Cellular Aspects of Amphibian Lens Regeneration
results.author: J. J. Henry
results.journal: Progress in retinal and eye research
results.takeaway: Amphibian lens regeneration occurs in premetamorphic frogs and adult newts, with different mechanisms and molecular mechanisms, providing valuable insights into the process.

results.title: Tail and Spinal Cord Regeneration in Urodelean Amphibians
results.author: Eleonora N Grigoryan
results.takeaway: Urodelean amphibians can regenerate their tail and spinal cord throughout their life, highlighting the importance of cell dedifferentiation and mutual molecular regulation in tissue regeneration.

results.title: Unravelling the limb regeneration mechanisms of Polypedates maculatus, a sub-tropical frog, by transcriptomics
results.author: Cuckoo Mahapatra
results.takeaway: Polypedates maculatus frogs exhibit species-specific limb regeneration mechanisms, offering insights into alternative tactics for regenerative medicine and engineering.

results.title: Plasticity and reprogramming of differentiated cells in amphibian regeneration
results.author: J. Brockes
results.takeaway: Amphibian regeneration is primarily driven by plasticity and reprogramming of differentiated cells, rather than a'reserve-cell' mechanism.

results.title: Amphibian Limb Regeneration: Rebuilding a Complex Structure
results.author: J. Brockes
results.journal: American Association for the Advancement of Science
results.takeaway: Urodele amphibians can regenerate their limbs by local formation of a mesenchymal growth zone or blastema, potentially respecifying proximodistal identity in newt blastemal cells through retinoic acid receptor signaling.

results.title: Positional Memory in Vertebrate Regeneration: A Century's Insights from the Salamander Limb.
results.author: L. Otsuki
results.journal: Cold Spring Harbor perspectives in biology
results.takeaway: Positional memory in vertebrate regeneration, as demonstrated in the salamander limb model, could lead to improved tissue repair and tissue engineering for therapeutic purposes.

results.title: Amphibian regeneration and stem cells.
results.author: D. Stocum
results.journal: Current topics in microbiology and immunology
results.takeaway: Amphibian limb regeneration relies on growth and trophic factors from the apical epidermal cap and nerves, offering insights into regenerative medicine for mammalian tissues.

results.title: Cellular and Molecular Mechanisms in Amphibian Appendage Regeneration
results.author: Yang Li
results.takeaway: Amphibians can fully regenerate lost tissues, such as appendages, providing new strategies for stimulating organ regeneration in regenerative medicine.

results.title: A Comparative Perspective on Brain Regeneration in Amphibians and Teleost Fish
results.author: Katharina Lust
results.takeaway: Brain regeneration in amphibians and fish is similar, but distinct, with frogs losing regenerative abilities after metamorphosis and teleost fish and salamanders maintaining regenerative competence throughout adulthood.

results.title: Study of Natural Longlife Juvenility and Tissue Regeneration in Caudate Amphibians and Potential Application of Resulting Data in Biomedicine
results.author: E. Grigoryan
results.takeaway: Caudate amphibians exhibit the highest regenerative abilities among tetrapods, with pedomorphosis and juvenile properties being the main explanation for their high regenerative abilities.

results.title: Hierarchical pattern formation during amphibian limb regeneration
results.author: Warren A. Vieira
results.takeaway: Hierarchical pattern formation in amphibian limb regeneration involves four basic steps: cell memory, communication, induction of molecular signaling centers, and specialized cell types interpreting signals to restore the limb.

results.title: Advances in signaling in vertebrate regeneration as a prelude to regenerative medicine.
results.author: Cristi L. Stoick-Cooper
results.takeaway: Understanding shared signaling pathways in vertebrate regeneration can accelerate the development of regenerative medicine therapies for organ and appendage regeneration in humans.

results.title: Nerve-mediated FGF-signaling in the early phase of various organ regeneration.
results.author: Sakiya Yamamoto
results.journal: Journal of experimental zoology. Part B, Molecular and developmental evolution
results.takeaway: Nerve-mediated FGF-signaling plays a crucial role in the early phase of organ regeneration in amphibians, contributing to their high regeneration capacity.

results.title: The molecular basis of amphibian limb regeneration: integrating the old with the new.
results.author: D. Gardiner
results.takeaway: Advances in technology and genomics may enable humans to encourage regeneration and enhanced repair processes through understanding the molecular basis of amphibian limb regeneration.

results.title: Cellular and molecular bases of arm regeneration in Brittlestars
results.author: M. Thorndyke
results.takeaway: Brittlestars can rapidly regenerate lost arms, with functional recovery occurring within a week after ablation.

results.title: MARCKS-Like Protein Immunolocalization in Healing Appendages of Amphibians Suggests Its Involvement in Regeneration.
results.author: L. Alibardi
results.journal: Journal of experimental zoology. Part B, Molecular and developmental evolution
results.takeaway: The presence of MARCKS-like protein in amphibians' healing appendages suggests its involvement in regeneration, potentially also in other vertebrates.

results.title: More Than Just a Bandage: Closing the Gap Between Injury and Appendage Regeneration
results.author: A. Kakebeen
results.takeaway: Amphibian regenerative healing processes involve early embryonic signaling pathways and physiological injury responses, which could be applied to human therapeutic interventions.

results.title: Amphibian regeneration and mammalian cancer: Similarities and contrasts from an evolutionary biology perspective
results.author: B. Corradetti
results.takeaway: Adult mammals' susceptibility to cancer may be determined by the loss of advanced regenerative capability during evolution, potentially offering a new treatment route.

results.title: Regeneration inducers in limb regeneration
results.author: A. Satoh
results.takeaway: The accessory limb model identified molecules (BMP7 (or2) + FGF2 + FGF8) that can initiate limb regeneration responses in amphibians, potentially revealing universal regeneration mechanisms among species.

results.title: The inbred newt genome unveils molecular mechanisms of behavior, development, and regeneration in urodele amphibians
results.author: Yuki Kimura
results.takeaway: The inbred newt genome provides insights into amphibian evolution, behavior, development, and regeneration, offering a valuable model organism for studying vertebrate development and regeneration.

results.title: Appendage‐restricted gene induction using a heated agarose gel for studying regeneration in metamorphosed Xenopus laevis and Pleurodeles waltl
results.author: Haruka Matsubara
results.takeaway: The "agarose-embedded heat shock" method allows for precise and reproducible gene induction in amphibian appendages, aiding in understanding molecular mechanisms underlying regeneration.

results.title: Repatterning in amphibian limb regeneration: A model for study of genetic and epigenetic control of organ regeneration.
results.author: Nayuta Yakushiji
results.takeaway: Epigenetic mechanisms may play a crucial role in maintaining positional information and regulating gene re-expression during amphibian limb regeneration.

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: salamanders
results.author: A. Joven
results.takeaway: Salamanders are key models for regeneration, demonstrating remarkable abilities to regrow tissues, organs, and even whole body parts, providing insights into cell, tissue, and organ regeneration mechanisms.

results.title: Appendage regeneration in anamniotes utilizes genes active during larval‐metamorphic stages that have been lost or altered in amniotes: The case for studying lizard tail regeneration
results.author: L. Alibardi
results.takeaway: Organ regeneration in anamniotes is influenced by specific evolutionary histories, with aquatic vertebrates having regenerative ability due to metamorphic stages, while terrestrial vertebrates lack regeneration.

results.title: Skin regeneration of amphibians: A novel model for skin regeneration as adults
results.author: H. Yokoyama
results.takeaway: Amphibian skin regeneration models provide valuable insights into adult skin regeneration, potentially leading to skin regeneration in adult mammals and limb regeneration in the future.

results.title: Beyond early development: Xenopus as an emerging model for the study of regenerative mechanisms
results.author: C. Beck
results.takeaway: Xenopus laevis is a leading model for studying regeneration mechanisms, enabling the identification of genes and cellular processes that enable successful regeneration.

results.title: Using Ambystoma mexicanum (Mexican Axolotl) Embryos, Chemical Genetics, and Microarray Analysis to Identify Signaling Pathways Associated with Tissue Regeneration
results.author: L. Ponomareva
results.journal: Comparative biochemistry and physiology. Toxicology & pharmacology : CBP
results.takeaway: Mexican axolotl embryos can efficiently regenerate amputated tails in 7 days, making them a useful model for studying signaling pathways associated with tissue regeneration.

results.title: Heat‐Shock‐Inducible Gene Expression Systems in Amphibians: Utility in Regeneration and Metamorphosis Studies
results.author: Ayumi Yamato
results.takeaway: Heat-shock-inducible systems in amphibians enable precise gene activation and lineage tracing, enabling molecular studies of regeneration and metamorphosis processes.

results.title: Study of regeneration in amphibians in age of molecular-genetic approaches and methods
results.author: E. Grigoryan
results.takeaway: Molecular-genetic approaches have improved our understanding of amphibian regeneration, leading to a new definition of regeneration as repeated development.

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: Xenopus
results.author: Lauren S. Phipps
results.takeaway: Xenopus is a key model organism for regeneration research, as it can achieve scar-free healing and tissue regeneration during larval stages, offering insights into the mechanisms governing regeneration.

results.title: Amphioxus regeneration: evolutionary and biomedical implications.
results.author: Ildikó M. L. Somorjai
results.journal: The International journal of developmental biology
results.takeaway: Amphioxus regeneration provides a valuable model for understanding regeneration evolution and its potential biomedical applications.

results.title: Tales of regeneration in zebrafish
results.author: K. Poss
results.takeaway: Zebrafish model system offers a promising approach to understanding molecular mechanisms of regeneration, with recent studies revealing their remarkable ability to regenerate fins.

results.title: It Cuts Both Ways: An Annelid Model System for the Study of Regeneration in the Laboratory and in the Classroom
results.author: Veronica G. Martinez Acosta
results.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
results.takeaway: An annelid model system can effectively study regeneration, providing insights for regenerative medicine and providing a primer for biology for researchers and educators.

results.title: Regeneration in anamniotes was replaced by regengrow and scarring in amniotes after land colonization and the evolution of terrestrial biological cycles
results.author: L. Alibardi
results.takeaway: Vertebrates evolved terrestrial lifecycles, limiting regeneration, and regenerative medicine should consider diverse developmental pathways before introducing "anamniote regenerative genes" in amniotes.

results.title: Ontogeny of homeothermy in the immature rat: metabolic and thermal responses.
results.author: D. Spiers
results.takeaway: Immature rats show significant improvements in homeothermic ability from 5 to 19 days of age, with thermal insulation being the primary factor responsible for these increases.

results.title: Effects of hypoxia on the respiratory and metabolic responses to progressive cooling in newborn rodents that range in heterothermic expression
results.author: Yvonne A. Dzal
results.takeaway: Newborn rodents show differences in how they regulate oxygen supply and demand when exposed to cold and hypoxia, reflecting their degree of heterothermic expression and tolerance.

results.title: Body temperature and oxygen consumption of newborn rats at various ambient temperatures.
results.author: N. Takano
results.takeaway: Newborn rats maintain body temperature at 36-37 degrees C and achieve homeothermy at subneutral temperatures after the weaning period, with higher thermogenic responses prior to weaning.

results.title: Development of Heat Production in Altricial and Precocial Rodents: Implications for the Energy Allocation Hypothesis
results.author: D. Webb
results.takeaway: Cotton rats have a higher metabolic heat production capacity per unit body mass than wood rats, and their rapid growth violates subtractive theories of energy allocation.

results.title: Development of Thermoregulatory Abilities in the Neonatal Hispid Cotton Rat, Sigmodon Hispidus Texianus, from Northern Kansas and South-Central Texas
results.author: S. Scheck
results.takeaway: Neonatal hispid cotton rats from northern Kansas and south-central Texas show similar thermoregulatory abilities, with age being more closely related to thermoregulation than body mass.

results.title: Development of Thermoregulation in Merriam's Kangaroo Rat, Dipodomys merriami
results.author: L. Soholt
results.takeaway: Young kangaroo rats develop 90% of their thermoregulatory ability within 2 weeks of birth, with endothermy developing early and homeothermy developing later.

results.title: Effects of temperature on ultrasound production by infant albino rats.
results.author: J. Allin
results.takeaway: Low ambient temperatures elicit high rates of ultrasonic distress calls in infant albino rats, while high ambient temperatures and nonthermal stimuli are ineffective in eliciting this response.

results.title: Neither rats nor mice have a broad thermoneutral zone: implications for physiological studies
results.author: J. Jacobsen
results.takeaway: Rats and mice both have thermoneutral points, but study them at 28-29°C to minimize cold-induced thermogenesis and reduce heat stress risks.

results.title: Ambient Temperature as a Strong Zeitgeber of Circadian Rhythms in Response to Temperature Sensitivity and Poor Heat Dissipation Abilities in Subterranean African Mole-Rats
results.author: D. W. Hart
results.takeaway: Ambient temperature strongly entrains circadian rhythms of locomotor activity in subterranean African mole-rats due to their sensitivity to temperature changes and poor heat dissipation abilities.

results.title: Thermal environment affects hair coat development of Norway rats
results.author: Jill A. Villarreal
results.takeaway: Cool-housed rats develop greater body and coat mass and a higher coat mass to body mass ratio than warm-housed rats.

results.title: Locomotor Activity and Body Temperature Patterns over a Temperature Gradient in the Highveld Mole-Rat (Cryptomys hottentotus pretoriae)
results.author: M. Haupt
results.takeaway: Highveld mole-rats exhibit nocturnal activity at all temperatures, with their endogenous locomotor activity rhythm being more robust than their body temperature rhythm, suggesting they rely more on behavioral thermoregulation for energy efficiency in their challenging environment.

results.title: Effect of ambient temperature on dexmedetomidine-induced metabolic and cardiorespiratory suppression in spontaneously breathing newborn rats.
results.author: Eishi Nakamura
results.takeaway: Dexmedetomidine can preserve ventilation-metabolism coupling in newborn rats at cold ambient temperatures, but not at hot temperatures.

results.title: The mouse: An “average” homeotherm
results.author: C. Gordon
results.takeaway: The mouse is considered a homeotherm when core temperature is averaged over a long period, but its core temperature varies significantly from hour to hour, potentially impacting research conclusions.

results.title: Development of behavioral responses to thermal challenges
results.author: Delia S. Shelton
results.takeaway: Young mammals develop abilities to combat heat loss earlier than protections against hyperthermia, making them particularly vulnerable to environmental warming.

results.title: Age-dependent differences in the thermoregulatory response of the immature rat to ethanol.
results.author: D. Spiers
results.takeaway: The thermoregulatory responsiveness to ethanol increases with age in immature rats, with greater effects in older animals.

results.title: Oxygen consumption in new‐born rats
results.author: P. Taylor
results.takeaway: New-born rats can increase oxygen consumption in the cold, unlike most mammalian species, by the age of 3-4 days, indicating a metabolic response to cold shortly after birth.

results.title: Unexplored aspects of African mole-rat thermal biology: Daily energy expenditure and development of thermoregulation in Fukomys darlingi (Rodentia: Bathyergidae)
results.author: J. Okrouhlík
results.takeaway: African mole-rats' thermoregulation development is slow, with fully developed abilities in three-month-olds, and the presence of adults helps increase core body temperature and decrease resting metabolic rate.

results.title: Body Temperature Patterns and Rhythmicity in Free-Ranging Subterranean Damaraland Mole-Rats, Fukomys damarensis
results.author: Sonja Streicher
results.takeaway: Damaraland mole-rats exhibit greater variation in body temperature during winter, with males showing greater variation than females, and no consistent relationship with ambient temperature.

results.title: Locomotor activity and body temperature rhythms in the Mahali mole-rat (C. h. mahali): The effect of light and ambient temperature variations.
results.author: Barry van Jaarsveld
results.takeaway: Mahali mole-rats possess a functional circadian clock that can integrate external light and temperature cues into their circadian rhythms of locomotor activity and core body temperature.

results.title: Body temperature rhythms, cold tolerance, and fever in young and old rats of both genders.
results.author: R. Refinetti
results.takeaway: Aging does not have a generalized debilitating effect on temperature regulation in rats, but rather affects individual components of the thermoregulatory system differently.

results.title: Morphological and Molecular Responses of Lateolabrax maculatus Skeletal Muscle Cells to Different Temperatures
results.author: Jingru Zhang
results.takeaway: Higher temperatures accelerate muscle cell proliferation, differentiation, and migration in Lateolabrax maculatus fish, while lower temperatures promote DNA damage and apoptosis.

results.title: Insights into molecular pathways and fatty acid membrane composition during the temperature stress response in the murine C2C12 cell model.
results.author: Marua Abu Risha
results.journal: The Science of the total environment
results.takeaway: Temperature stress alters skeletal muscle cell membrane composition and alters molecular pathways, affecting muscle cell differentiation and growth under heat or cold stress.

results.title: Heat stress inhibits the proliferation and differentiation of myoblasts and is associated with damage to mitochondria
results.author: Jiawei Lu
results.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
results.takeaway: Heat stress inhibits myoblast proliferation and differentiation, accelerates apoptosis, and impairs mitochondrial function, impacting skeletal muscle development.

results.title: Transcriptomic Response of Differentiating Porcine Myotubes to Thermal Stress and Donor Piglet Age
results.author: F. Sarais
results.takeaway: Different thermoregulatory capacities of donor piglets determine the ability of primary muscle cell culture to differentiate into myotubes at different temperatures, which can be leveraged to develop effective thermal management strategies for skeletal muscle growth.

results.title: Season-dependent effects of elevated temperature on stress biomarkers, energy metabolism and gamete development in mussels.
results.author: M. Mugica
results.takeaway: Elevated temperatures negatively impact mussel health and gamete development, making them vulnerable to global climate change.

results.title: Thermal stress affects proliferation and differentiation of turkey satellite cells through the mTOR/S6K pathway in a growth-dependent manner
results.author: Jiahui Xu
results.takeaway: Thermal stress affects turkey satellite cell proliferation and differentiation through the mTOR/S6K pathway, potentially impacting muscle growth and development in the turkey pectoralis major muscle.

results.title: Differential effects of temperature and mTOR and Wnt-planar cell polarity pathways on syndecan-4 and CD44 expression in growth-selected turkey satellite cell populations
results.author: Jiahui Xu
results.takeaway: Thermal stress alters SDC4 and CD44 expression in growth-selected turkey satellite cells, potentially impacting muscle development and growth.

results.title: The effects of temperature and donor piglet age on the transcriptomic profile and energy metabolism of myoblasts
results.author: Katharina Metzger
results.takeaway: Temperature stress in porcine myoblasts leads to diverse gene expression changes, with the most pronounced changes observed at 37°C, where muscle cells can develop to their full capacity.

results.title: Controlled Heat Stress Promotes Myofibrillogenesis during Myogenesis
results.author: Qiongyu Guo
results.takeaway: Moderate hyperthermia at 39°C promotes myofibrillogenesis during muscle regeneration, with strictly controlled heat stress needed to minimize atrophy and enhance mitochondrial biogenesis.

results.title: Temperature Effects on Force and Actin–Myosin Interaction in Muscle: A Look Back on Some Experimental Findings
results.author: K. Ranatunga
results.takeaway: Warming active muscle significantly increases force, with a half-maximum at 10°C, and the sigmoidal temperature dependence of force is due to the endothermic nature of crossbridge force generation in different muscle types.

results.title: The independent effects of heat application on muscle growth program associated mRNA and protein phosphorylation
results.author: M. McGlynn
results.takeaway: Local heat application at rest does not significantly influence gene expression or protein phosphorylation associated with muscle growth program-related markers.

results.title: Thermal conditions experienced during differentiation affect metabolic and contractile phenotypes of mouse myotubes.
results.author: A. Little
results.journal: American journal of physiology. Regulatory, integrative and comparative physiology
results.takeaway: Developing muscle can compensate for cold exposure by increasing metabolic rates, ATP production, and glycolytic flux, complementing central thermoregulation and allowing animals to maintain function in cold environments.

results.title: Comparative Transcriptome Profiles of the Response of Mycelia of the Genus Morchella to Temperature Stress: An Examination of Potential Resistance Mechanisms
results.author: Yihong Yue
results.takeaway: High temperatures accelerate oxidative stress response and energy metabolism in edible mushroom mycelia, while low temperatures improve low-temperature tolerance and upregulation of purine nucleotide catabolism and ribosomal protein-related genes.

results.title: A Molecular Mechanism of Temperature Sensitivity for Mutations Affecting the Drosophila Muscle Regulator Myocyte Enhancer Factor-2
results.author: TyAnna L. Lovato
results.takeaway: Temperature-sensitive mutations in the Drosophila muscle regulator Myocyte enhancer factor-2 (MEF2) can be generated by combining one weakened DNA binding MEF2 isoform with a second truncated MEF2 mutant, resulting in temperature-dependent intragenic complementation.

results.title: Temperature and muscle.
results.author: A. F. Bennett
results.takeaway: Temperature-dependent muscle rates of force development, contraction, and relaxation are influenced by evolutionary adaptations, with cold-adapted species maintaining better mechanical performance at low temperatures than warm-adapted animals.

results.title: Transcriptional dynamic changes in energy metabolism, protein synthesis and cell cycle regulation reveal the biological adaptation mechanisms of juvenile Acrossocheilus wenchowensis under acute temperature changes.
results.author: Jinghong He
results.takeaway: Acrossocheilus wenchowensis fish adapt by maintaining cell stability and reducing cell damage, regulating energy metabolism and protein synthesis under high-temperature stress and low-temperature stress.

results.title: Transcriptome Analysis Revealed Potential Genes of Skeletal Muscle Thermogenesis in Mashen Pigs and Large White Pigs under Cold Stress
results.author: Wenxi Li
results.takeaway: Mashen pigs show some cold adaptability, while Large White pigs regulate heat production and glycolipid energy metabolism, offering insights into molecular mechanisms of cold adaptation in pigs.

results.title: The temperature sensitivity of motor units in rat soleus
results.author: Bartosz Malak
results.takeaway: Slow-twitch motor units in soleus muscles are more thermally sensitive than their counterparts in medial gastrocnemius, with hypothermia causing more profound changes and hyperthermia having no effect on force or twitch time parameters.

results.title: Temperature sensitivity of Notch signaling underlies species-specific developmental plasticity and robustness in amniote brains
results.author: T. Nomura
results.takeaway: Temperature sensitivity of Notch signaling in amniote brains contributes to developmental plasticity and robustness, allowing adaptations to various ambient temperatures.

results.title: Both brown adipose tissue and skeletal muscle thermogenesis processes are activated during mild to severe cold adaptation in mice
results.author: N. Bal
results.takeaway: Both brown adipose tissue and skeletal muscle thermogenesis processes are activated during mild and severe cold adaptation in mice, with loss of heat production from one pathway leading to increased recruitment of the other.

results.title: Transcriptome data reveal conserved patterns of fruiting body development and response to heat stress in the mushroom-forming fungus Flammulina filiformis
results.author: Xiao-Bin Liu
results.takeaway: Conserved genes in the winter mushroom (Flammulina filiformis) help adjust to heat stress, aiding in the development of improved productivity and heat tolerance in the mushroom-forming fungus.

results.title: A single-cell time-lapse of mouse prenatal development from gastrula to birth
results.author: Chengxiang Qiu
results.takeaway: This study provides a comprehensive single-cell time-lapse of mouse prenatal development, revealing major cell-type relationships and physiological adaptations within one hour of birth.

results.title: Quantitative Genetic Analysis of Temperature Regulation in MUS MUSCULUS. I. Partitioning of Variance.
results.author: R. Lacy
results.takeaway: Temperature regulation in mice is influenced by physiological, morphological, and behavioral adjustments, with metabolic heat-production mechanisms reaching their genetic limits and behavioral heat conservation mechanisms showing considerable genetic variability.

results.title: A timecourse analysis of systemic and gonadal effects of temperature on sexual development of the red-eared slider turtle Trachemys scripta elegans.
results.author: M. Czerwinski
results.takeaway: Temperature influences sexual development in red-eared slider turtles, with multiple factors influencing early gonadogenesis and aromatase regulation playing a key role in sex determination.

results.title: QUANTITATIVE GENETIC ANALYSIS OF TEMPERATURE REGULATION IN MUS MUSCULUS. II. DIALLEL ANALYSIS OF INDIVIDUAL TRAITS
results.author: C. B. Lynch
results.takeaway: Heritabilities in traits closely associated with fitness are expected to be low, reflecting their importance to individual fitness in small mammals.

results.title: Comparative genomics reveals divergent thermal selection in warm‐ and cold‐tolerant marine mussels
results.author: I. Popović
results.takeaway: Temperature-dependent selection contributes to molecular divergence in warm- and cold-adapted marine mussels, affecting functions related to heat stress defense and cytoskeletal stabilization.

results.title: Unraveling the genotype by environment interaction in a thermosensitive fish with a polygenic sex determination system
results.author: B. Geffroy
results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
results.takeaway: Temperature-induced masculinization in European sea bass is influenced by genetic and environmental factors, with energetic pathways playing a role in sex determination.

results.title: The genomic basis of environmental adaptation in house mice
results.author: M. Phifer‐Rixey
results.takeaway: House mice from different latitudes show differences in fitness traits and blood chemistry, with specific genes underlying adaptive variation.

results.title: Two transcriptionally distinct pathways drive female development in a reptile with both genetic and temperature dependent sex determination
results.author: S. Whiteley
results.takeaway: Temperature determines sex in Pogona vitticeps reptiles, with early developmental cascades differing between genetically driven and thermally driven females, and genes playing a role in temperature sex reversal.

results.title: Analyzing the coordinated gene network underlying temperature-dependent sex determination in reptiles.
results.author: C. Shoemaker
results.takeaway: Temperature-dependent sex determination in reptiles involves a conserved to novel molecular network, with key players playing conserved to novel roles in gonad development.

results.title: QUANTITATIVE GENETIC ANALYSIS OF TEMPERATURE REGULATION IN MUS MUSCULUS. III. DIALLEL ANALYSIS OF CORRELATIONS BETWEEN TRAITS
results.author: D. S. Sulzbachi
results.takeaway: Wright, 1980).

results.title: Molecular and genetic control of plant thermomorphogenesis

results.author: P. Pottier

results.author: Alexandre Fellous

results.author: G.M. Worth

results.author: Jingru Zhang

results.author: Jiawei Lu
results.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology

results.title: Transcriptomic Response of Differentiating Porcine Myotubes to Thermal Stress and Donor Piglet Age

results.title: Season-dependent effects of elevated temperature on stress biomarkers, energy metabolism and gamete development in mussels.

results.title: Thermal stress affects proliferation and differentiation of turkey satellite cells through the mTOR/S6K pathway in a growth-dependent manner
results.author: Jiahui Xu

results.author: Jiahui Xu
results.takeaway: Thermal stress alters SDC4 and CD44 expression in growth-selected turkey satellite cells, potentially impacting muscle development and growth.

results.author: Katharina Metzger

results.author: Qiongyu Guo

results.author: K. Ranatunga

results.author: M. McGlynn
results.takeaway: Local heat application at rest does not significantly influence gene expression or protein phosphorylation associated with muscle growth program-related markers.

results.author: Yihong Yue

results.title: A Molecular Mechanism of Temperature Sensitivity for Mutations Affecting the Drosophila Muscle Regulator Myocyte Enhancer Factor-2
results.author: TyAnna L. Lovato

results.title: Temperature and muscle.

results.author: Jinghong He

results.author: Wenxi Li

results.author: T. Nomura

results.author: N. Bal

results.author: Xiao-Bin Liu

results.author: Chengxiang Qiu

results.author: I. Popović
results.takeaway: Temperature-dependent selection contributes to molecular divergence in warm- and cold-adapted marine mussels, affecting functions related to heat stress defense and cytoskeletal stabilization.

results.takeaway: A systematic review of complete blood count parameters has provided updated global estimates of biological variation, which will be included in the newly published European Federation of Clinical Chemistry and Laboratory Medicine BV Database.

results.title: Biological variation: recent development and future challenges
results.author: S. Sandberg
results.takeaway: Recent developments in biological variation data collection and reporting standards have improved laboratory medicine applications, including personalized reference intervals and measurement uncertainty.

results.title: The European Biological Variation Study (EuBIVAS): a summary report
results.author: A. Carobene
results.takeaway: The EuBIVAS study provides high-quality biological variation data for 80 different measurands, providing lower estimates than previously reported, impacting analytical performance specifications and reference change values.

results.title: Harmonization initiatives in the generation, reporting and application of biological variation data
results.author: A. Aarsand
results.takeaway: Harmonization initiatives in biological variation data generation, reporting, and application will improve patient care by providing high-quality data for clinical laboratory results.

results.title: A standard to report biological variation data studies – based on an expert opinion
results.author: William A. Bartlett
results.takeaway: The STARBIV mind map, developed by international experts, serves as a guideline for researchers to ensure data quality, consistency, and comparability in biological variation studies, improving clinical applications.

results.title: Disadvantages in preparing and publishing scientific papers caused by the dominance of the English language in science: The case of Colombian researchers in biological sciences
results.author: Valeria Ramírez-Castañeda

results.title: The global state, trajectory and trends of bacterial extracellular vesicles: a bibliometric and visualized analysis
results.author: Haokai Chen
results.takeaway: Bacterial extracellular vesicles (BEVs) show promising potential as immunotherapeutic agents, drug delivery systems, and nano-vaccines, with cancer immunotherapy, tumor microenvironment, and drug delivery as promising research directions.

results.title: Within-subject biological variation estimated using real-world data strategies (RWD): a systematic review
results.author: F. Marques-García
results.journal: Critical Reviews in Clinical Laboratory Sciences
results.takeaway: Real-World Data (RWD) strategies can improve biological variation estimates in clinical laboratories by using large amounts of data and allowing subgrouping.

results.title: Generation of data on within-subject biological variation in laboratory medicine: An update
results.author: F. Braga
results.journal: Critical Reviews in Clinical Laboratory Sciences
results.takeaway: This update of the guideline for biological variation data production in laboratory medicine emphasizes the importance of considering data distribution for accurate estimates of biological variation in laboratory tests.

results.title: Computer programming in quantitative biology
results.author: J. Jeffers

results.title: Special rebranding issue: "Quantitative cell and developmental biology".
results.author: C. Heisenberg

results.title: Variation in Citational Practice in a Corpus of Student Biology Papers
results.author: J. Swales
results.takeaway: Citation practices in biology papers show little difference between undergraduate and graduate students, with some variation in citing systems and richer intertextuality in evolutionary biology papers.

results.title: Biological variation database: structure and criteria used for generation and update
results.author: C. Perich
results.takeaway: The database on biological variation components has been updated every 2 years, providing valuable information for laboratory medicine and evaluating the reliability of included data.

results.title: Current Utility and Reliability of Biological Variability.
results.author: Khushbu K. Patel
results.takeaway: Biological variation estimates derived from carefully designed and well-described studies are reliable, paving the way for new and far-reaching applications in laboratory medicine.

results.title: Systematic Review of Over A Century of Global Bioscience Research
results.author: O. K. Iroha

results.title: Biological variation estimates obtained from Chinese subjects for 32 biochemical measurands in serum
results.author: Liming Ma
results.takeaway: This study provides biological variation data for Chinese subjects, highlighting population differences that may impact the applications of BV data.

results.title: Trends and gaps in the use of citizen science derived data as input for species distribution models: A quantitative review
results.author: Mariano J. Feldman
results.takeaway: Citizen science data has increased in species distribution models, but disparities in taxonomic and geographic coverage remain, with Western Europe and North America being the most covered regions.

results.title: On the molecular mechanisms regulating animal cell size homeostasis
results.author: E. Zatulovskiy
results.takeaway: Animal cell size homeostasis is regulated through two distinct mechanisms: size-dependent cell cycle progression and size-dependent cell growth.

results.title: Genetic compensation: A phenomenon in search of mechanisms
results.author: Mohamed A. El-Brolosy
results.takeaway: Genetic compensation in higher eukaryotes may involve both transcriptional and posttranscriptional processes, but our understanding of its molecular mechanisms remains limited.

results.title: Molecular and cellular mechanisms of myocardial stunning.
results.author: R. Bolli
results.takeaway: Myocardial stunning may be caused by oxygen-derived free radicals and calcium overload, with contractile dysfunction occurring after reperfusion and potentially contributing to chronic postischemic dysfunction.

results.title: Molecular mechanisms of adaptive evolution in wild animals and plants
results.author: Yibo Hu
results.takeaway: Recent advances in molecular biology have greatly increased our understanding of adaptive traits, convergent evolution, and coevolution in wild animals and plants, benefiting species survival and persistence.

results.title: Mitochondrial dynamics: overview of molecular mechanisms
results.author: Lisa Tilokani
results.takeaway: Mitochondrial dynamics, a crucial cellular process, is regulated by large GTPases belonging to the Dynamin family, which play crucial roles in maintaining shape, distribution, and size, and are linked to various human diseases.

results.title: Mechanisms and consequences of oxygen- and carbon dioxide-sensing in mammals.
results.author: E. Cummins
results.takeaway: Mammals have evolved mechanisms to sense changes in oxygen and carbon dioxide levels and elicit adaptive responses to maintain homeostasis, potentially serving as targets for therapeutic intervention in various pathological states.
