results.takeaway: Syllids show high posterior regeneration abilities, but anterior regeneration varies across species, with gene expression changes in both processes.

results.title: The people behind the papers - Alicia Boyd and Elaine Seaver.
results.takeaway: Capitella teleta, an annelid worm, gains regenerative ability with age, suggesting metamorphosis serves as a switch in annelid regenerative potential.

facets.q: Can environmental conditions such as the gastropod shell induce body asymmetry in hermit crabs (developmental plasticity)?
How does shell occupation shape abdominal morphology in hermit crabs?

104.state: Shell-induced body asymmetry in hermit crabs is confirmed developmental plasticity: crabs reared in symmetrical or non-dextral shells develop more symmetrical or reversed abdomens, and the asymmetry is readily overridden by environment. The de-shelling result is an early demonstration, occasionally re-cited.

results.title: Environmentally induced subsymmetry in the hermit crab, Calcinus dapsiles Morgan (Decapoda, Diogenidae).
results.author: G. J. Morgan
results.takeaway: The hermit crab Calcinus dapsiles Morgan exhibits more symmetrical body shape and uropods than usual when living in a non-coiled shelter, suggesting environmental factors may influence their symmetry.

results.title: Genes for asymmetry easily overruled
results.author: A. Harvey
results.takeaway: Hermit crab Clibanarius vittatus's asymmetry can be easily overridden by environmental factors, potentially aiding in the evolution of symmetrical king crabs and coconut crabs from hermit crab ancestors.

results.title: Asymmetrical chela growth patterns and correlation of chela shape to inhabited gastropod shells in Pagurus bernhardus (Linnaeus, 1758) (Decapoda, Anomura, Paguridae)
results.author: Yannic C. Ege
results.takeaway: Pagurus bernhardus hermit crabs exhibit sexually dimorphic growth patterns, with males showing larger right chelae and females showing smaller left chelae, suggesting sexual selection for display and agonistic behavior.

results.title: Asymmetrical morphology and growth of the hermit crab Pagurus filholi (Decapoda, Anomura, Paguridae) reared in non-dextral shell conditions
results.author: M. Imafuku
results.takeaway: Hermit crab Pagurus filholi shows asymmetrical morphology when reared in non-dextral shell conditions, with the right uropod becoming extended and the right major cheliped becoming enlarged.

results.title: CENTRAL AND PERIPHERAL ORIGINS OF ASYMMETRY IN THE ABDOMINAL MOTOR SYSTEM OF THE HERMIT CRAB *
results.author: W. Chapple
results.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
results.takeaway: Hermit crabs' abdominal nervous system shows asymmetries in different directions, highlighting the complexity of laterality and the adaptation of their body to their environment.

results.title: Hermit crabs perceive the extent of their virtual bodies
results.author: Kohei Sonoda
results.takeaway: Hermit crabs can modify walking behavior based on the shape of their shell, indicating an awareness of environmental obstacles and a flexible body image.

results.title: The Behavioral Ecology of Hermit Crabs
results.author: B. Hazlett
results.journal: Annual Review of Ecology, Evolution, and Systematics
results.takeaway: Hermit crabs' strong association with their adopted shelters has greatly influenced their biology, with most species adapting to inhabiting gastropod shells and exhibiting behavioral changes as they become benthic, shell-seeking crabs.

results.title: Choosing a bigger opponent: the path to victory and greater gains for the small contestant
results.author: Luis M. Burciaga
results.takeaway: Hermit crabs choose opponents larger than themselves for contests over gastropod shells, with fighting success higher when they choose opponents with better shell species or fit.

results.title: The molding hypothesis: linking shell use with hermit crab growth, morphology, and shell-species selection
results.author: A. Turra
results.takeaway: Hermit crab growth and morphology are influenced by shell use, with males reaching larger sizes and intermolt periods than females, and shell-species selection influenced by past experience and shell type.

results.title: Adaptive divergence in response to shared environmental pressures: examining gastropod shell exploitation by intertidal hermit crabs.
results.author: G. Alcaraz
results.takeaway: Hermit crabs adapt to snail shell shape based on the intertidal zone they inhabit, with shell shape similarities and contrasts depending on the species and pressures faced.

results.title: THE EFFECTS OF SHELL SIZE AND SHAPE ON GROWTH AND FORM IN THE HERMIT CRAB PAGURUS LONGICARPUS
results.author: N. Blackstone
results.takeaway: Shell shape and size significantly influence the growth and form of Pagurus longicarpus hermit crabs, potentially explaining geographic variation in their appearance.

results.title: Pattern and Plasticity in Tropical Hermit Crab Growth and Reproduction
results.author: M. Bertness
results.takeaway: Tropical hermit crab species trade-off growth and reproduction based on their supply of shells, allowing them to adapt to resource limitations and competition.

results.title: Early-life environment shapes claw bilateral asymmetry in the European lobster (Homarus gammarus)
results.author: Lorenzo Latini
results.takeaway: Exposure to substrate alone promotes claw asymmetry in juvenile European lobsters, with the 6th developmental stage being the critical period for claw differentiation.

results.title: Performance Implications of Divergent Shell Size Preferences and Exoskeleton Mass of Two Closely Related Hermit Crabs
results.author: Chloe B. MacLean
results.takeaway: Hermit crabs with larger shells have better protection but reduced motility and energetic cost, while those with smaller shells have greater mobility but increased vulnerability to stressors.

results.title: Hermit crabs, shells, and sentience
results.author: R. W. Elwood
results.takeaway: Hermit crabs exhibit complex perceptual and cognitive abilities in locating, selecting, and changing shells, suggesting potential sentience and awareness.

results.title: Mechanism of a plastic phenotypic response: predator‐induced shell thickening in the intertidal gastropod Littorina obtusata
results.author: J. Brookes
results.takeaway: Predation-induced shell thickening in intertidal snail Littorina obtusata is an active physiological response, involving energetic and developmental costs, potentially enhancing its evolutionary potential.

results.title: The colour of combat: How subtleties of resource value alter the effects of fighting ability in hermit crab contests
results.author: Thomas M. Chatfield
results.takeaway: Hermit crab contests over empty shells are more intense and aggressive when both shells are of high contrast, influenced by resource value and potential predation risk.

results.title: The physical basis of mollusk shell chiral coiling
results.author: R. Chirat
results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
results.takeaway: The development of chiral shells in mollusks is influenced by the interaction between the soft body and hard shell, with mechanical forces balanced by body twists.

results.title: The plastic homes of hermit crabs in the Anthropocene.
results.author: Zuzanna A. Jagiello
results.journal: The Science of the total environment
results.takeaway: Hermit crabs are increasingly using artificial shells made from plastic, mainly caps, due to sexual signaling, lightness, odor cues, and camouflage in polluted environments.

results.title: Asymmetric effects of contaminant exposure during asymmetric contests in the hermit crab Pagurus bernhardus
results.author: S. J. White
results.takeaway: Copper exposure in hermit crabs reduces the number of fights initiated and the likelihood of evicting defenders, but has no effect on defenders' chances of resisting eviction.

results.title: Strawberry hermit crab (Coenobita perlatus, H. Milne Edwards, 1837) gastropod shell utilization pattern according to the type and size
results.author: Y. Jeremy
results.takeaway: Strawberry hermit crabs (Coenobita perlatus) consistently select shells based on their architecture and size, affecting their fitness, but often overlook slight differences in size due to availability issues.

results.title: Shell occupation by the hermit crab Dardanus insignis (Decapoda, Diogenidae) from the north Coast of São Paulo state, Brazil.
results.author: I. F. Frameschi
results.journal: Brazilian journal of biology = Revista brasleira de biologia
results.takeaway: The hermit crab Dardanus insignis primarily occupies adequate shells, with Olivancillaria urceus being the most commonly used shell, and shell availability influencing occupation patterns for smaller individuals.

results.title: Social conquest of land: Sea-to-land changes in shell architecture and body morphology, with consequences for social evolution.
results.author: M. E. Laidre
results.takeaway: Changes in shell architecture and body morphology in land hermit crabs have led to increased social dependence and easier eviction, potentially impacting social evolution on land.

results.title: Associations between Crab Morphology and Gastropod Shell Species in the Hermit Crab Pagurus Longicarpus
results.author: T. Wilber
results.takeaway: Crab morphology and shell species occupancy change ontogenetically, suggesting a relationship between shell species and cheliped shape in Pagurus longicarpus.

results.title: The Behavioral Mechanisms Underlying Shell Selection By Hermit Crabs1)
results.author: E. S. Reese
results.takeaway: Hermit crabs select shells based on their properties, primarily using visual orientation and tactile and proprioceptor-based sensory input.

results.title: Comparative analysis of shell occupation by two southern populations of the hermit crab Loxopagurus loxochelis (Decapoda, Diogenidae)
results.author: Luciane Ayres-Peres
results.takeaway: Hermit crabs' shell choice is influenced by factors such as morphometry, shell availability, environmental conditions, and competition, leading to a diverse shell occupancy pattern in southern Brazil.

results.title: Morphometric traits as drivers for module structures and species specialization: a study about the hermit crab–gastropod networks from three different regions on the Brazilian coast
results.author: A. D. Silva
results.takeaway: Hermit crabs with different sizes need different types of shells, influencing their modularity and species specialization in their interaction with gastropod shells.

results.title: Role of the abdomen in the regulation of shell position in the hermit crabPagurus pollicarus
results.author: W. Chapple
results.takeaway: The abdomen plays a key role in maintaining shell position in Pagurus pollicarus hermit crabs, with its role being one-tenth of total lift and influenced by the fourth and fifth pereiopods.

results.title: Shell use by sympatric hermit crab species in a seasonally open coastal lagoon in Northeastern Brazil
results.author: V. Vale
results.takeaway: Hermit crab species in a Brazilian coastal lagoon predominantly use Neritina virginea shells, with shell weight being the most important determinant of shell occupancy, highlighting the need for conservation of these species.

results.title: Study on Shell Utilization Pattern of Two Sympatric Hermit Crab Species on the Rocky Intertidal Region of Veraval, Gujarat, India
results.author: K. Patel
results.journal: Thalassas: An International Journal of Marine Sciences
results.takeaway: Shell occupation patterns of C. rhabdodactylus and C. ransoni hermit crabs are highly influenced by the diversity, morphology, and availability of gastropod shells in the study area.

results.title: Shell occupation by the South Atlantic endemic hermit crab Loxopagurus loxochelis (Moreira, 1901) (Anomura: Diogenidae)
results.author: I. F. Frameschi
results.takeaway: The South Atlantic endemic hermit crab Loxopagurus loxochelis primarily occupies Olivancillaria urceus shells in Brazil's southwestern coast, suggesting stable environments for population perpetuation and new individuals.

results.title: Postural control of shell position by the abdomen of the hermit crab, Pagurus pollicarus. III. Analysis of movements and calculations of forces exerted by the muscles
results.author: W. Chapple
results.takeaway: Hermit crabs maintain shell position by bending their abdomens, with the columella in the crook of its bent abdomen, and the muscles exerting forces and bending moments consistent with behavioral measurements.

facets.q: Can crustaceans regenerate specialized mouthpart appendages such as the maxilliped?
What governs serial homology and identity in regenerated crustacean appendages?

45.state: Serial homology and identity of regenerated crustacean appendages is active evo-devo: Hox genes (Ubx, abd-A, Abd-B) specify and transform thoracic legs into feeding maxillipeds, and BMP signalling drives early appendage regeneration. The maxilliped-regeneration result fits directly.

results.title: Autotomy and Regeneration of Appendages in Crustaceans: A Review
results.author: Lei Liu
results.journal: Journal of Ocean University of China
results.takeaway: Autotomy in crustaceans is a self-protection mechanism that can affect foraging efficiency, growth, and reproduction, with chelicerae removal reducing cannibalism in commercial production.

results.title: Functional Study of the BMP Signaling Pathway in Appendage Regeneration of Exopalaemon carinicauda
results.author: Chaofan Xing
results.takeaway: The BMP signaling pathway plays a critical role in the early stages of appendage regeneration in Exopalaemon carinicauda, affecting wound healing and blastema regeneration time.

results.title: Crustacean appendage evolution associated with changes in Hox gene expression
results.author: M. Averof
results.takeaway: Changes in Hox gene expression in crustaceans correlate with the modification of anterior thoracic limbs into feeding appendages, suggesting homeotic changes play a role in adaptive evolutionary change.

results.title: CRISPR/Cas9 Mutagenesis Reveals Versatile Roles of Hox Genes in Crustacean Limb Specification and Evolution.
results.author: Arnaud Martin
results.takeaway: Hox genes play diverse roles in crustacean limb specification and evolution, with abdominal-A and Abdominal-B essential for proper posterior patterning and Ubx affecting gill development.

results.title: Probing the evolution of appendage specialization by Hox gene misexpression in an emerging model crustacean
results.author: A. Pavlopoulos
results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
results.takeaway: Hox gene misexpression in crustaceans can lead to gradual evolutionary transitions from thoracic legs to maxillipeds, revealing the role of Hox genes in morphological and functional transformations.

results.title: Novel regulation of the homeotic gene Scr associated with a crustacean leg-to-maxilliped appendage transformation.
results.author: Arkhat Abzhanov
results.takeaway: The homeotic gene Scr plays a novel role in the transformation of crustacean leg-to-maxilliped appendages, suggesting a novel regulatory mechanism for this process in this group of arthropods.

results.title: Knockdown of Parhyale Ultrabithorax recapitulates evolutionary changes in crustacean appendage morphology
results.author: Danielle M. Liubicich
results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
results.takeaway: Reducing Ultrabithorax expression in Parhyale hawaiensis crustaceans leads to additional maxillipeds, supporting the idea that changes in Ubx expression contribute to crustacean appendage diversity.

results.title: Morphological and Molecular Changes during Limb Regeneration of the Exopalaemon carinicauda
results.author: Chaofan Xing
results.journal: Animals : an Open Access Journal from MDPI
results.takeaway: Limb regeneration in the Exopalaemon carinicauda crustacean occurs rapidly and involves a complex network of cells and genes, contributing to our understanding of regeneration mechanisms in crustaceans.

results.title: Wound healing and regeneration in the crab Paratelphusa hydrodromous.
results.author: R. G. Adiyodi
results.takeaway: Crab Paratelphusa hydrodromous can amputate appendages and regenerate them, with regeneration linked to molting and reproduction, governed by the same controlling mechanisms.

results.title: Naturally occurring abnormalities (Bruchdreifachbildungen) in the chelae of three species of Crustacea (Decapoda) and a possible explanation.
results.author: P. M. Shelton
results.journal: Journal of embryology and experimental morphology
results.takeaway: Crustacean appendage abnormalities result from failure of wounds to heal, resulting in a range of structures similar to those observed in insect legs.

results.title: Embryonic expression patterns of the Hox genes of the crayfish Procambarus clarkii (Crustacea, Decapoda)
results.author: A. Abzhanov
results.takeaway: Trunk Hox genes in crayfish Procambarus clarkii play an essential role in the development of the complex decapod bodyplan, with more complex expression patterns compared to woodlouse Porcellio scaber.

results.title: Appendage Regeneration in Vertebrates: What Makes This Possible?
results.author: Valentina Daponte
results.takeaway: Understanding the similarities and differences in appendage regeneration in lizards, salamanders, and zebrafish can guide effective regenerative strategies in mammals.

results.title: Crustacean Limb Morphogenesis during Normal Development and Regeneration
results.author: A. Pavlopoulos
results.takeaway: Crustacean models with improved genomic and transcriptomic resources reveal the molecular and cellular basis of embryonic limb development and postembryonic limb regeneration, shedding light on appendage specialization mechanisms across arthropods and bilaterians.

results.title: Crustaceans.
results.author: Annalisa M. VanHook
results.takeaway: Crustaceans exhibit diverse limb adaptations for various functions, with mantis shrimps having highly specialized raptorial appendages capable of striking prey with incredible force.

results.title: Regenerated claws of the virile crayfish Faxonius virilis (Hagen, 1870) (Decapoda: Astacidea: Cambaridae) generate weaker pinching forces compared to original claws
results.author: Z. Graham
results.takeaway: Regenerated claws in virile crayfish Faxonius virilis generate weaker pinching forces (36% and 40% weaker in males and females) and have less muscle mass compared to original claws, potentially causing dishonest claws in crayfish.

results.title: Parhyale hawaiensis, Crustacea
results.author: John Rallis
results.journal: Handbook of Marine Model Organisms in Experimental Biology
results.takeaway: Parhyale hawaiensis has emerged as a valuable model organism for comparative developmental, genetic, and genomic research, contributing to understanding molecular mechanisms in body patterning and appendage diversification during arthropod development and evolution.

results.title: Unexpected UBX expression in the maxilliped of the mystacocarid crustacean Derocheilocharis remanei—evidence for a different way of making a maxilliped?
results.author: M. Fritsch
results.takeaway: The mystacocarid crustacean Derocheilocaris remanei shows unexpected UBX/ABD-A expression in the developing maxilliped, suggesting a shift in Hox gene function in arthropods.

results.title: Crustacean leg regeneration restores complex microanatomy and cell diversity
results.author: Alba Almazán
results.takeaway: Crustacean leg regeneration accurately replicates complex microanatomy and restores sensory function, with regenerated and uninjured legs having indistinguible cell-type composition and transcriptional profiles.

results.title: Burgess Shale fossils illustrate the origin of the mandibulate body plan
results.author: Cédric Aria
results.takeaway: Burgess Shale fossils reveal the origin of the mandibulate body plan, suggesting distinct ontogenetic niches among stem arthropods during the Cambrian period.

results.title: Deep evolutionary origin of limb and fin regeneration
results.author: Sylvain Darnet
results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
results.takeaway: A common origin of paired appendage regeneration exists among Osteichthyes, with a shared genetic program involving limb and fin regeneration in various species.

results.title: The Daphnia carapace and other novel structures evolved via the cryptic persistence of serial homologs.
results.author: Heather S. Bruce
results.takeaway: The Daphnia carapace evolved from a shared, ancestral tissue that persists in a cryptic state in other arthropod lineages, suggesting cryptic persistence of unrecognized serial homologs as a general solution for the origin of novel structures.

results.title: Homeotic transformation in a terrestrial isopod: insights into the appendage identity in crustaceans
results.author: Naoto Inui
results.takeaway: Homeotic transformation of a pleopod in the terrestrial isopod Porcellio scaber may cause a malformed appendage with three-segmented pereopod-like structures.

results.title: Genetic and developmental bases of serial homology in vertebrate limb evolution.
results.author: Ilya Ruvinsky
results.takeaway: This study proposes models for the evolution of paired appendages in vertebrates, emphasizing the importance of considering interactions among multiple genes from different gene families for understanding complex developmental systems.

results.title: A chromatin code for limb segment identity in axolotl limb regeneration.
results.author: Akane Kawaguchi
results.takeaway: Axolotl limb connective tissue cells use segment-specific levels of histone H3K27me3 as an intrinsic segment information code, supporting an ancient, conserved regeneration program.

results.title: Deconstructing the long‐standing a priori assumption that serial homology generally involves ancestral similarity followed by anatomical divergence
results.author: Natalia Siomava
results.takeaway: Serial homology may not always involve ancestral similarity and may display trends towards less similarity or more similarity in evolution, challenging the assumption that serial homology always involves anatomical divergence.

results.title: The hierarchical basis of serial homology and evolutionary novelty
results.author: J. DiFrisco
results.takeaway: Serial homology can be applied to repeated, individualized body parts, allowing a more fine-grained mapping of diverse trait-types and explaining why everything is not homologous with everything else in evolution.

results.title: Keeping at arm’s length during regeneration
results.author: Valerie A. Tornini
results.takeaway: Adult amphibians and fish can regenerate lost appendages, demonstrating remarkable developmental patterning, by maintaining positional identity and determining tissue completion.

results.title: Identification of Hox genes and their expression profiles during embryonic development of the emerging model organism, Macrobrachium olfersii.
results.author: M. Jaramillo
results.journal: Journal of experimental zoology. Part B, Molecular and developmental evolution
results.takeaway: Hox genes play a role in the development and evolution of body segments and appendages in crustaceans, with some isoforms previously unreported.

results.title: Evolution of Serial Patterns in the Vertebrate Pharyngeal Apparatus and Paired Appendages via Assimilation of Dissimilar Units
results.author: Tetsuto Miyashita
results.takeaway: Serial similarity in vertebrate pharyngeal apparatus and paired appendages is a derived state, acquired through the secondarily assimilation of distinctly patterned structures.

results.title: Genetic reprogramming of positional memory in a regenerating appendage
results.author: Ying-Ting Wang
results.takeaway: Positional information in regenerating tissues is malleable, with zebrafish tailfins retaining memory of their new size when disrupted during a 48-hour window of regeneration.

results.title: The Papilla Stage as a Critical Molecular Transition: Antp and Sex-Regulatory Network Orchestrate Cheliped Regeneration in Eriocheir sinensis
results.author: Benzhen Li
results.journal: Animals : an Open Access Journal from MDPI

results.title: Transitions in functional morphology from “large branchiopods” to Cladocera: Video and confocal microscopic studies of Cyclestheria hislopi (Cyclestherida) and Sida crystallina (Cladocera: Ctenopoda)
results.author: Zandra M. S. Sigvardt
results.takeaway: Cladocerans show a unique morphology and function, with a specialized swimming and feeding system that separates the anterior locomotory system and posterior feeding system, potentially explaining their omnipresence in various habitats.

results.title: Formation of body appendages during caudal regeneration in Platynereis dumerilii: adaptation of conserved molecular toolsets
results.author: Jan Grimmel
results.takeaway: Platynereis dumerilii's caudal regeneration shows conserved roles of genes involved in appendage formation, but the underlying mechanisms may not be identical across different clades.

results.title: Common themes in tetrapod appendage regeneration: a cellular perspective
results.author: Bess M. Miller
results.takeaway: Understanding commonalities between regenerative modes across diverse species can help integrate past observations and modern understanding of complex tissue regeneration.

results.title: Cellular diversity of the regenerating caudal fin
results.author: Yiran Hou
results.takeaway: Zebrafish regenerate their caudal fins after amputation, involving epithelial, mesenchymal, and hematopoietic cells, with molecular signatures aiding in cell type identification.

facets.q: Do muscle contractile proteins adapt their thermal stability to an animal's body temperature?
Is the thermal stability of muscle proteins fixed or thermally acclimated across species?

102.state: Whether muscle proteins adapt their thermal stability to body temperature is live thermal-adaptation physiology: fish adjust contractile-protein expression and force with temperature (though some, like trout, may not), and myofibrillar ATPase thermal stability varies. The 'fixed coagulation point' is the question, now answered with nuance.

results.title: Thermal Stability of Contractile Proteins in Bat Wing Muscles Explains Differences in Temperature Dependence of Whole-Muscle Shortening Velocity
results.author: A. Rummel
results.takeaway: Bat wing muscles' contractile properties are influenced by the thermal stability of myofibrillar ATPase, with forearm muscles having less thermal stability than pectoralis muscles, but no significant difference in acute temperature dependence of enzyme activity.

results.title: Adaptation of fish to different environmental temperature by qualitative and quantitative changes in gene expression
results.author: G. Goldspink
results.takeaway: Fish adapt to different environmental temperatures by changing gene expression, leading to increased force and power in muscles acclimated to low temperatures.

results.title: Temperature adaptation by the myotomal muscle of fish
results.author: R. Penney
results.takeaway: Fish can adapt their contractile proteins to suit a specific temperature, but trout may not have the ability to do so due to their relatively unchanging temperature environment.

results.title: Thermal conditions experienced during differentiation affect metabolic and contractile phenotypes of mouse myotubes.
results.author: A. Little
results.journal: American journal of physiology. Regulatory, integrative and comparative physiology
results.takeaway: Developing muscle can compensate for cold exposure by increasing metabolic rates, ATP production, and glycolytic flux, complementing central thermoregulation and allowing animals to maintain function in cold environments.

results.title: Muscle and Metabolic Genes Are Differentially Expressed During Thermal Acclimation by the Brook Trout Myotome.
results.author: D. Coughlin
results.journal: Journal of experimental zoology. Part A, Ecological and integrative physiology
results.takeaway: Brook trout show a robust response to elevated temperature, with more than 10,000 genes showing differential expression with temperature, potentially aiding their survival in climate change-related challenges.

results.title: TEMPERATURE ADAPTATION IN FISH MUSCLE
results.author: R. Penney
results.takeaway: Fish muscle adapts to low temperatures by having high specific nyofibrillar ATPase activity, but some species can acclimate to a wide range of temperatures, with similar calcium transport composition and temperature dependence.

results.title: Switches in fish myosin genes induced by environment temperature in muscle of the carp.
results.author: G. Goldspink
results.journal: Symposia of the Society for Experimental Biology
results.takeaway: Carp can adapt to seasonal temperature changes by expressing different myosin heavy chain isoform genes, allowing them to swim at warm or cold temperatures.

results.title: Regulatory proteins and thermostability of myofibrillar ATPase in acclimated goldfish
results.author: R. Penney
results.takeaway: Goldfish adapt to different temperatures by altering their contractile proteins, with regulatory proteins playing a more involved role in muscle contraction than a simple on/off switch.

results.title: Effects of thermal acclimation on ventricle size, protein composition, and contractile properties of crucian carp heart
results.author: V. Pelouch
results.takeaway: Thermal acclimation to cold temperatures increases extracellular matrix protein concentration but reduces myocyte protein concentration in crucian carp hearts.

results.title: Biochemical responses to temperature in the contractile protein complex of striped bass Morone saxatilis.
results.author: T. Moerland
results.takeaway: Striped bass's red muscle, powered by ATPase, is more sensitive to cold temperatures than white muscle, potentially impairing their sustained swimming capacity at cold temperatures.

results.title: Physical and molecular bases of protein thermal stability and cold adaptation.
results.author: F. Pucci
results.takeaway: Protein thermal and cold stability and adaptation are complex and challenging, requiring further investigation for large-scale rational protein design.

results.title: Loss of α-actinin-3 during human evolution provides superior cold resilience and muscle heat generation
results.author: V. Wyckelsma
results.takeaway: Loss of -actinin-3 in humans leads to improved cold resilience and muscle heat generation during cold-water immersion due to changes in skeletal muscle thermogenesis.

results.title: Heat stability of fish muscle proteins
results.author: R. Poulter
results.journal: International Journal of Food Science and Technology
results.takeaway: Fish muscle proteins show varying heat stability, with more stable proteins found in fish found in higher ambient temperatures, while actins show similar thermal stability across all species.

results.title: Thermal acclimation in rainbow smelt, Osmerus mordax, leads to faster myotomal muscle contractile properties and improved swimming performance
results.author: J. Woytanowski
results.takeaway: Rainbow smelt can maintain activity at cold temperatures by adjusting muscle contractile properties and modifying muscle function to enable active locomotion in cold water.

results.title: Movements of vastly different performance have similar underlying muscle physiology
results.author: J. Olberding
results.takeaway: Elastic tongue projection in salamanders leads to higher performance and thermal robustness, while muscle contractile properties remain relatively unchanged.

results.title: Thermal denaturation of proteins in post rigor muscle tissue as studied by differential scanning calorimetry
results.author: E. Stabursvik
results.journal: Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture
results.takeaway: Strict pH control is crucial for reproducible muscle thermograms, as myosin and actin denaturation peaks in post-rigor muscle tissue are pH-dependent and actin denaturation is salt-dependent.

results.title: Changing face of contractile activation in striated muscle at physiological temperature
results.author: Alf Månsson
results.takeaway: Calcium binding to troponin and myosin binding to actin play a crucial role in contractile regulation of striated muscle at physiological temperature (35-40°C).

results.title: Adaptations in Mg2+‐activated myofibrillar ATPase activity induced by temperature acclimation
results.author: W. Davison
results.takeaway: Goldfish with a wide thermal tolerance range show increased Mg2+-activated myofibrillar ATPase activity at low temperatures, suggesting a strong correlation between thermostability and environmental temperature.

results.title: Dissecting the key residues crucial for the species-specific thermostability of muscle-type creatine kinase.
results.author: Y. Gao
results.takeaway: Two residues near the dimer interface of muscle-type creatine kinase, the 46th and 146th residue, are crucial for species-specific thermal stability.

results.title: A comparison of thermal sensitivities of wing muscle contractile properties from a temperate and tropical bat species.
results.author: A. Rummel
results.takeaway: Temperature sensitivities in bat muscles are generally similar, but the pectoralis muscle in Eptesicus fuscus is less sensitive to temperature changes than in Carollia perspicillata, suggesting better function at low temperatures.

results.title: Meltome atlas—thermal proteome stability across the tree of life
results.author: A. Jarząb
results.takeaway: This study reveals that evolutionary conservation of protein complexes is reflected by similar thermal stability of their proteins, with protein sequence, composition, and size affecting thermal stability in prokaryotes and eukaryotes.

results.title: Adaptation of protein stability to thermally heterogeneous environments
results.author: Tadeas Priklopil
results.takeaway: Protein stability adaptation in complex thermal environments involves both mean temperature and thermal fluctuations, with local adaptation more likely for proteins with stability profiles limited to narrow temperature ranges.

results.title: Fish fast skeletal muscle tropomyosins show species-specific thermal stability.
results.author: Ming-Chih Huang
results.journal: Comparative biochemistry and physiology. Part B, Biochemistry & molecular biology
results.takeaway: Fish fast skeletal muscle tropomyosins show species-specific thermal stability, with only a few amino acid substitutions and post-translational modifications potentially affecting their stability.

results.title: Species dependence of fish myosin stability to heat and frozen storage
results.author: J. Davies
results.journal: International Journal of Food Science and Technology
results.takeaway: Fish myosin stability varies between habitat temperatures, with red snapper showing significant changes in whole muscle after frozen storage, while cod shows similar changes in whole muscle and isolated myosin.

results.title: Phylogenetic history and temperature adaptation contribute to structural and functional stability of proteins in marine mollusks
results.author: Xin-lei Zhang

results.title: Regeneration in Annelids: Cell Sources, Tissue Remodeling, and Differential Gene Expression

results.title: Regeneration in the Segmented Annelid Capitella teleta

results.takeaway: Rhodnius prolixus, a blood-feeding hemipteran, evolved an unusual cuticle pigmentation strategy using a color erasing function of the aaNATpreto tyrosine pathway branch.

results.title: Sexually Dimorphic Body Color Is Regulated by Sex-Specific Expression of Yellow Gene in Ponerine Ant, Diacamma Sp
results.author: S. Miyazaki
results.takeaway: Sex-specific expression of the yellow gene is responsible for the sexual color dimorphism observed in Diacamma sp. ants, with worker females appearing bluish-black and winged males yellowish-brown.

results.title: Biochemistry and biosynthesis of insect pigments
results.author: Gulsaz
results.takeaway: Insect pigments play a crucial role in providing coloration, UV protection, and oxygen transport, while also providing functional benefits for insects and their host plants.

results.title: Re‐evaluation of insect melanogenesis research: Views from the dark side
results.author: M. Whitten
results.takeaway: Insect melanogenesis research reveals diverse, sophisticated interactions with microbes, highlighting the importance of innate immunity in beneficial insects like pollinators and the versatility of phenoloxidases.

results.title: The genetic control of aposematic black pigmentation in hemimetabolous insects: insights from Oncopeltus fasciatus
results.author: Jin Liu
results.takeaway: Oncopeltus fasciatus hemimetabolous insect reveals that black pigmentation in wings is primarily derived from the melanin pathway, with Dopamine melanin being the predominant component, and follows a two-step model for pigment production and patterning.

results.title: Pigments in Insects
results.author: Ryo Futahashi
results.journal: Pigments, Pigment Cells and Pigment Patterns
results.takeaway: Insect pigments, mainly melanins, ommochromes, and pteridines, play a crucial role in their diverse colors and patterns, with genes involved in pigment synthesis, transport, and patterning.

results.title: Three Melanin Pathway Genes, TH, yellow, and aaNAT, Regulate Pigmentation in the Twin-Spotted Assassin Bug, Platymeris biguttatus (Linnaeus)
results.author: Yinqiao Zhang
results.takeaway: The melanin pathway plays a crucial role in regulating pigmentation in the twin-spotted assassin bug, with TH, yellow, and aaNAT genes playing key roles in black pigmentation and yellow pigmentation.

results.title: Tyrosine Metabolism for Insect Cuticle Pigmentation and Sclerotization
results.author: Y. Arakane
results.takeaway: The tyrosine-mediated cuticle tanning pathway plays a crucial role in insect body coloration, playing crucial roles in species recognition, communication, and resistance to temperature and ultraviolet radiation.

results.title: Pigmentation and color pattern diversity in Odonata.
results.author: Genta Okude
results.takeaway: Ommochrome and pteridine pigments are essential for light-blue coloration in Odonata, with gene-functional analysis warranting future studies.

results.title: Two MYB proteins in a self-organizing activator-inhibitor system produce spotted pigmentation patterns
results.author: Baoqing Ding
results.takeaway: Two MYB proteins in a self-organizing activator-inhibitor system in monkeyflower petals produce spotted pigmentation patterns, which impact pollinator visitation.

results.title: Insect pupil mechanisms
results.author: D. Stavenga
results.takeaway: The pupil mechanism of Hymenoptera is controlled by pigment granules in the retinula cells, with a broad absorbance spectrum peaking at about 520 nm, making it a useful part of the visual system.

results.title: The BTB-ZF gene Bm-mamo regulates pigmentation in silkworm caterpillars
results.author: Songyuan Wu
results.takeaway: The Bm-mamo gene plays a crucial role in regulating silkworm caterpillar color patterns by repressing dark melanin patterns and coordinating the expression of related pigment synthesis and cuticular protein genes.

results.title: Gene functions in adult cuticle pigmentation of the yellow mealworm, Tenebrio molitor.
results.author: Seulgi Mun
results.takeaway: Knocking down specific enzymes in the tyrosine metabolic pathway leads to abnormal pigmentation in individual layers and substructure of the rigid adult exoskeleton of the yellow mealworm, Tenebrio molitor.

results.title: From genes to color: Evolutionary insights and mechanistic pathways of the yellow gene in insect pigmentation
results.author: Blessie Pradeeka Gudelly
results.journal: International Journal of Biological and Pharmaceutical Sciences Archive

results.title: Chromatophores and color revelation in the blue variant of the Siamese fighting fish (Betta splendens).
results.author: M. H. Amiri

results.title: Hormonal regulation of colour change in eyes of a cryptic fish

results.title: Control of chromatophore movements in the blue-green damselfish, Chromis viridis
results.author: N. Oshima
results.journal: Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology Part C: Comparative Pharmacology
results.takeaway: The movements of chromatophores in the blue-green damselfish, Chromis viridis, are regulated by nervous and endocrine systems, contributing to its characteristic greenish hue and subtle color changes.

results.title: The physiology of flatfish chromatophores
results.author: D. Burton

results.title: The physical and cellular mechanism of structural color change in zebrafish

results.author: H. Kasukawa

results.title: Rapid integumental color changes due to novel iridophores in the chameleon sand tilefish Hoplolatilus chlupatyi

results.title: Ultrastructure and regulation of color change in blue spots of leopard coral trout Plectropomus leopardus

results.title: Biochemical regulation of pigment motility in vertebrate chromatophores: a review of physiological color change mechanisms
results.author: Russell A. Ligon

results.author: J. J. Henry

results.title: The power of amphibians to elucidate mechanisms of size control and scaling

results.author: L. M. Ochoa-Ochoa

results.author: A. Brunetti

results.author: Jennifer Y. Lamb

results.title: The Terrestrial Isopod Microbiome: An All-in-One Toolbox for Animal–Microbe Interactions of Ecological Relevance

results.title: Phylogenomics supports a single origin of terrestriality in isopods

results.title: Lignocellulose degradation in isopods: new insights into the adaptation to terrestrial life
results.author: M. Bredon
results.takeaway: Isopods exhibit different strategies for lignocellulose degradation, with terrestrial species showing expanded CAZy families and aquatic species showing contracted families, likely due to adaptation during terrestrial colonization.

results.title: Pleopodal-Lung Formation in a Terrestrial Isopod, Porcellio Scaber

results.title: Nutrition in terrestrial isopods (Isopoda: Oniscidea): an evolutionary‐ecological approach
results.author: M. Zimmer

results.title: Regeneration of swimming antennae after partial amputation in long- and short-lived Daphnia

results.title: Habitat prevails over host sex in influencing mycobiome structure of terrestrial isopod, Armadillidium vulgare
results.author: Jiho Yang

results.title: Function of Vivid Coloration of Terrestrial Isopods from the Point of View of an Avian Predator
results.author: Barbora Ďurajková

results.title: The terrestrial isopod fauna of Cheharmahal-va-Bakhtiyari Province
results.author: قاسم محمدی کاشانی
results.takeaway: The biodiversity of terrestrial isopods is relatively high in Cheharmahal-va-Bakhtiyari Province, with 10 identified species, but further research is needed for precise estimation of their number.

results.title: Preface – 11thISTIB: Facets of terrestrial isopod biology
results.author: P. De Smedt

results.title: Transition from marine to terrestrial ecologies: changes in olfactory and tritocerebral neuropils in land-living isopods.

results.title: A bibliometric analysis of research on terrestrial isopods
results.author: Miloš Vittori
results.takeaway: Basic research on terrestrial isopods flourishes, with smaller and developing economies making significant contributions if research organizations can achieve continuity, and journal metrics may be misleading in assessing research impact.

results.title: Patterns of taxonomic diversity among terrestrial isopods

results.takeaway: Taxonomic diversity patterns among terrestrial isopods can provide insights into their evolutionary dynamics and help refine their systematics.

results.title: Plant regeneration: cellular origins and molecular mechanisms

results.author: Ruoqing Huang

results.title: The engine initiating tissue regeneration: does a common mechanism exist during evolution?
results.author: Yanmei Liu
results.takeaway: A common mechanism may exist during evolution for triggering tissue regeneration, involving complex coordination of molecular, cellular, and physiological events.

results.title: Cellular and molecular mechanisms of liver regeneration: Proliferation, growth, death and protection of hepatocytes.
results.author: M. Ozaki
results.takeaway: Liver regeneration depends on hepatocyte proliferation, growth, and programmed cell death, regulated by interleukin-6/Jak/STAT3 and PI3-K/PDK1/Akt pathways.

results.title: Molecular and cellular mechanisms of tooth development, homeostasis and repair
results.author: Tingsheng Yu
results.takeaway: Recent advances in tooth development and stem cell-based dental tissue regeneration reveal potential therapies to improve oral health.

results.title: Transdifferentiation and mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition during regeneration in Demospongiae (Porifera).

results.title: Plant regeneration in the new era: from molecular mechanisms to biotechnology applications

results.title: How Does Scaffold Porosity Conduct Bone Tissue Regeneration?

results.title: New Insights Into Tissue Culture Plant-Regeneration Mechanisms
results.author: Y. Long
results.takeaway: Tissue culture plant regeneration can be influenced by environmental factors, such as explant sources, basal culture medium, growth regulators, and light/dark treatment, enhancing plant micropropagation and genetic modification.

results.title: Deciphering the molecular mechanisms of stem cell dynamics in hair follicle regeneration
results.author: Jung Hyun Lee
results.takeaway: Molecular mechanisms of stem cell dynamics in hair follicle regeneration and disease conditions can provide new insights for understanding and treating hair and skin disorders.

results.title: Animal regeneration in the era of transcriptomics
results.author: Loïc Bideau
results.takeaway: Recent data on animal regeneration models has identified key shared mechanisms, shedding light on the evolution of regeneration and its control mechanisms.

results.title: The cellular and molecular basis for planarian regeneration
results.author: P. Reddien
results.takeaway: Planarian regeneration is facilitated by positional information and stem cells, which guide tissue turnover and regeneration through a combination of pluripotent stem cells and fate-specified cells.

results.title: Comparative regenerative mechanisms across different mammalian tissues
results.author: S. Iismaa
results.takeaway: Recent insights into molecular mechanisms of regeneration in various mammalian tissues show potential for future regenerative therapies, despite constraints like immune responses, extracellular matrix composition, age, injury type, and physiological adaptations.

results.title: Cellular and Molecular Basis of Liver Regeneration
results.author: Sushant Bangru
results.takeaway: Advances in genetics and genomics have revolutionized our understanding of liver regeneration, revealing mechanisms and cellular sources that guide its recovery from acute or chronic damage.

results.title: Adaptive Evolution for Freshwater Adaptation in Coilia nasus by Directional Selection on Osmoregulation Genes

results.title: Osmotic and Adaptive Challenges: Physiological and Biochemical Responses of Aquatic Species to Increased Salinity

results.title: The physiology of saltwater acclimation in large juvenile Atlantic salmon Salmo salar.
results.author: Morgan S Brown
results.takeaway: Large juvenile Atlantic salmon maintain a high level of saltwater tolerance, surviving 100%, unaffected growth performance, increased Na-K-ATPase activity, and regulating plasma chloride and osmolality for 28 days without photoperiod and thermal regimes.

results.title: A postlarval instar of Phoxichilidium femoratum (Pycnogonida, Phoxichilidiidae) with an exceptional malformation

results.takeaway: A postlarval instar of Phoxichilidium femoratum sea spider shows a remarkable malformation, possibly due to injury-induced partial fusion of developing limb buds or irregular leg regeneration after near complete loss of trunk segments 3 and 4.

results.title: The effect of leg autotomy on terrestrial and aquatic locomotion in the wolf spider Pardosa valens (Araneae: Lycosidae)
results.author: Christopher A. Brown
results.takeaway: Leg autotomy in the wolf spider Pardosa valens negatively impacts sprint speed in both terrestrial and aquatic locomotion, with the impact depending on spider sex and habitat factors.

results.title: Regeneration and autotomy exhibited by the Black Widow spider,Latrodectus variolus walckenaer
results.author: J. B. Randall
results.journal: Wilhelm Roux's archives of developmental biology
results.takeaway: Black Widow spiders exhibit regeneration and autotomy, with regeneration occurring at the femoral mid-point and autotomy occurring at the trochanter-coxa joint, confirming the developmental gradient model of regeneration.

results.title: Cellular, Molecular, and Physiological Aspects of In Vitro Plant Regeneration
results.author: S. S. Bidabadi
results.takeaway: In vitro plant regeneration involves factors such as medium components, phytohormones, explant type, and light, with molecular signals playing a role in organogenesis and embryogenesis responses.

results.title: Cellular and molecular mechanisms of development and regeneration.
results.author: Kalika Prasad
results.takeaway: Cellular and molecular mechanisms of development and regeneration play a crucial role in organism renewal and repair, offering insights into developmental biology, tissue engineering, and regenerative medicine.

results.title: Plant regeneration: cellular origins and molecular mechanisms
results.author: Momoko Ikeuchi
results.takeaway: Plants exhibit high developmental plasticity and various types of tissue or organ regeneration, influenced by hormone balance and developmental and environmental constraints.

results.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Plant Regeneration.
results.author: Momoko Ikeuchi
results.takeaway: Plants can regenerate damaged tissues or organs by reprogramming somatic cells, activating developmental programs, and utilizing hormones like auxin and cytokinin.

results.title: An insight into planarian regeneration
results.author: Xin-Yang Ge
results.takeaway: Planarian regeneration is regulated by diverse molecular factors and cellular signaling pathways, with neoblasts playing a crucial role in tissue regeneration and morphology maintenance.

results.title: Plant regeneration in the new era: from molecular mechanisms to biotechnology applications
results.author: Chunli Chen
results.takeaway: Plant regeneration relies on cell totipotency and pluripotency, with various species using distinct mechanisms and varying regenerative capacities.

results.title: The Molecular and Cellular Choreography of Appendage Regeneration.
results.author: E. Tanaka
results.takeaway: Limb regeneration reveals the molecular events that integrate growth control, cell fate programming, and positional information, providing insights for engineers to recreate complex multi-tissue structures.

results.title: New Insights Into Tissue Culture Plant-Regeneration Mechanisms
results.author: Y. Long
results.takeaway: Tissue culture plant regeneration can be influenced by environmental factors, such as explant sources, basal culture medium, growth regulators, and light/dark treatment, enhancing plant micropropagation and genetic modification.

results.title: Role of Agrin in tissue repair and regeneration: From mechanisms to therapeutic opportunities (Review)
results.author: Xiang Li
results.takeaway: Agrin plays a crucial role in tissue repair and regeneration, offering potential for future Agrin-based therapies as a feasible treatment option for patients requiring organ replacement or repair.

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: Arabidopsis
results.author: Mabel Maria Mathew
results.takeaway: Arabidopsis serves as a model plant for studying cellular and molecular mechanisms of regeneration, providing insights into plant multi-scale regenerative potential.

results.title: Liver regeneration: Cellular origin and molecular mechanisms
results.author: Ruoqing Huang
results.takeaway: Liver regeneration involves self-replication of hepatocytes for maintaining function and mass, and compensatory proliferation of remaining hepatocytes after acute and chronic liver injury.

results.title: Axonal Regeneration: Underlying Molecular Mechanisms and Potential Therapeutic Targets
results.takeaway: Axonal regeneration in the central nervous system is hindered by factors like glial scar development, myelin-associated inhibitor molecules, and inflammation, but intrinsic growth factors play a significant role in regrowth.

results.title: Nematostella vectensis, an Emerging Model for Deciphering the Molecular and Cellular Mechanisms Underlying Whole-Body Regeneration
results.author: E. Röttinger
results.takeaway: The sea anemone, Nematostella vectensis, is an emerging model for understanding the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying whole-body regeneration in aquatic invertebrates.

results.title: Animal regeneration in the era of transcriptomics
results.author: Loïc Bideau
results.takeaway: Recent data on animal regeneration models has identified key shared mechanisms, shedding light on the evolution of regeneration and its control mechanisms.

results.title: Ultrastructural and molecular analysis of the origin and differentiation of cells mediating brittle star skeletal regeneration
results.author: L. Piovani
results.takeaway: Brittle stars exhibit skeletal regeneration by originating undifferentiated cells in the epithelium of the regenerating aboral coelomic cavity, then migrating towards the epidermis and forming sclerocytes.

results.title: Regeneration in Stentor coeruleus
results.author: W. Marshall
results.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
results.takeaway: Single cells can regenerate missing structures, resembling animal development and regeneration processes, and may have evolved by exploiting pre-existing subcellular developmental strategies from unicellular ancestors.

results.title: Cell tip growth underlies injury response of marine macroalgae
results.author: Maki Shirae‐Kurabayashi
results.takeaway: Marine macroalgae show high potential for regeneration after damage, with cell tip growth being a common response and nuclear translocation following this growth.

results.title: Tissue Repair and Regeneration: Elucidating Cellular and Molecular Mechanisms with Therapeutic Implications
Physiological and molecular mechanisms of insect appendage regeneration
results.author: Jiru Zhong
results.takeaway: Insect appendage regeneration is influenced by physiological conditions and internal molecular mechanisms, with research progress focusing on the role of hormones and cytokines in this process.

results.title: Whole body regeneration deploys a rewired embryonic gene regulatory network logic
results.author: Rita Andreoni-Pham
results.takeaway: Regeneration in Nematostella vectensis sea anemones involves partial redeployment and extensive rewiring of embryonic gene regulatory networks, reactivating developmental modules through a regeneration-specific network logic.

facets.q: Links the newts' secondary sexual characters to gonadal control — an amphibian counterpart to Steinach's mammalian sex-gland work.
What is the molecular and cellular mechanism of sex determination in Triturus?

results.title: Current research in amphibians: studies integrating endocrinology, behavior, and neurobiology.
results.author: W. Wilczynski
results.takeaway: Amphibian behavioral endocrinology reveals that hormones and social behavior mutually reinforce each other, with complex interactions among gonadal steroids, adrenal steroids, and peptide hormones impacting natural social behavior.

results.title: Regulation of Reproductive Behaviors in Amphibians by LHRH
results.author: F. L. Moore
results.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
results.takeaway: LHRH enhances sexual behaviors in amphibians, particularly newts, by acting in neurons of the nervus terminalis, rather than in the hypothalamo-pituitary-gonad axis.

results.title: Hormonal control of response to and secretion of sex attractants in Japanese newts.
results.author: F. Toyoda
results.takeaway: Prolactin and human chorionic gonadotropin enhance the response of Japanese newts to sex attractants secreted by the opposite sex, with potential involvement in secretion by male abdominal gland and female oviduct.

results.title: The annual reproductive cycle of the Smooth newt (Triturus vulgaris) in England
results.author: P. Verrell
results.takeaway: Male newts conserve sperm during the breeding season, promoting reproductive success through adaptations in courtship behavior and sperm allocation.

results.title: Historical perspective: Hormonal regulation of behaviors in amphibians.
results.author: F. L. Moore
results.takeaway: Testicular androgens, gonadal steroid hormones, prolactin, vasotocin, and corticosterone play crucial roles in amphibian behavior regulation, with prolactin acting synergistically with androgens.

results.title: Basic sexual trends in the development of vertebrates.
results.author: A. Jost
results.takeaway: Sexual development in vertebrates involves genetic sex, gonadal sex, and body sex, with hormonal control in mammals and some birds, and sex behavior influenced by sex type.

results.title: Gonadectomy reduces the concentrations of putative receptors for arginine vasotocin in the brain of an amphibian.
results.author: S. Boyd
results.takeaway: Gonadectomy reduces arginine vasotocin receptors in the brain of newts, suggesting that gonadal steroids maintain sexual behaviors by maintaining these receptors in the amygdala.

results.title: The transcriptome of the newt Cynops orientalis provides new insights into evolution and function of sexual gene networks in sarcopterygians
results.author: M. A. Biscotti
results.takeaway: The transcriptome of Cynops orientalis reveals new insights into sexual gene networks in sarcopterygians, including the discovery of the gsdf gene in a tetrapod species and the high variability of sex-related genes in vertebrates.

results.title: Amphibians as a model for studying xenoestrogen‐dependent neuroedocrine disruption
results.author: A. Polzonetti-Magni
results.takeaway: 4nonylphenol disrupts amphibian reproduction by inducing changes in secondary sexual characteristics, increasing androgen plasma levels, and reducing ARO-LI containing neurons.

results.title: Neural and Hormonal Control of Sexual Behavior
results.author: K. Jennings
results.takeaway: Sexual behavior is strongly dependent on circulating gonadal hormones, with distinct neural circuits underlying motivation and behavior in males and females.

results.title: Freemartin in the amphibian Pleurodeles waltl: Parabiosis between individuals from opposite sex triggers both germ and somatic cells alterations during female gonad development
results.author: H. Dumond
results.takeaway: Parabiosis between opposite sex individuals in Pleurodeles waltl amphibians leads to alterations in female gonad development, inhibiting ovary differentiation but not in the case of exogenous estradiol treatment.

results.title: The inbred newt genome unveils molecular mechanisms of behavior, development, and regeneration in urodele amphibians
results.author: Yuki Kimura
results.takeaway: The inbred newt genome provides insights into amphibian evolution, behavior, development, and regeneration, offering a valuable model organism for studying vertebrate development and regeneration.

results.title: The Aromatase–Estrogen System in the Testes of Non-Mammalian Vertebrates
results.author: L. Rosati
results.journal: Animals : an Open Access Journal from MDPI
results.takeaway: The aromatase-estrogen system plays a crucial role in regulating testicular activity in non-mammalian vertebrates, with different roles in different classes and species.

results.title: Hormones, Sex Accessory Structures, and Secondary Sexual Characteristics in Amphibians
results.author: D. Sever
results.takeaway: Gonadal steroid hormones play a crucial role in the development and seasonal variation of amphibian sex accessory structures and secondary sexual characteristics.

results.title: A neuroscience-based approach to the assessment of sexual behavior in animals
results.author: S. Tekin
results.takeaway: Sexual behavior in animals is shaped by the reproductive system, with hormones, neurotransmitters, and genetic factors playing crucial roles in ensuring the continuity of generation.

results.title: Comparison of Sex Determination in Vertebrates (Nonmammals)
results.author: Aleksandr F. Smirnov
results.takeaway: Sex determination in nonmammals, such as fish, amphibians, reptiles, and birds, is initially controlled by sex hormones, but later involves various genes and external conditions, while in mammals, sex hormones play a limited role in primary sex determination.

results.title: Potential antagonistic relationship of fgf9 and rspo1 genes in WNT4 pathway to regulate the sex differentiation in Chinese giant salamander (Andrias davidianus)
results.author: Jiankang Zhang
results.takeaway: Fgf9 and rspo1 genes in the WNT4 pathway play an antagonistic role in regulating sex differentiation in Chinese giant salamanders, providing potential for genome editing breeding to improve the salamander farming industry.

results.title: A Y-linked duplication of anti-Mullerian hormone is the sex determination gene in threespine stickleback
results.author: Matthew J Treaster
results.takeaway: The Y-linked duplication of anti-Mullerian hormone (amhy) is the primary sex determination gene in threespine stickleback, contributing to differential germ cell proliferation and sex determination.

results.title: Sexual dimorphic effects of a keystone predator on prey communities
results.author: J. Davenport
results.takeaway: Sexual dimorphism within adult newts can have differential effects on larval amphibian communities, with female newts consuming more prey species and similar impacts on prey fitness (size at metamorphosis).

results.title: Photoperiod‐independent testicular development in the model newt Pleurodeles waltl
results.author: Mitsuki Kyakuno
results.takeaway: The model newt Pleurodeles waltl shows a suitable model for studying testicular development and spermatogenesis, with spermatogenesis proceeding irrespective of day length.

results.title: Sex determination without sex chromosomes
results.author: C. Weber
results.journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B
results.takeaway: Sex determination in reptiles, where no sex chromosomes have been identified, likely involves a combination of molecular events that shift the scales towards one fate over another until a threshold is reached.

results.title: Molecular and Cellular Mechanisms Underlying Temperature-Dependent Sex Determination in Turtles
results.author: H. Merchant-Larios
results.takeaway: Temperature-dependent sex determination in turtles is influenced by incubation temperature, with fetal testes playing a crucial role in developing the male phenotype.

results.title: Molecular mechanisms of sex determination and differentiation in decapod crustaceans for potential aquaculture applications: An overview
results.author: Tao Wang
results.takeaway: This review highlights the importance of genetic factors in sex differentiation in decapod crustaceans, aiding in the advancement of the crustacean aquaculture industry.

results.title: A candidate sex determination locus in amphibians which evolved by structural variation between X- and Y-chromosomes
results.author: Heiner Kuhl
results.takeaway: A candidate sex determination locus in amphibians, XX/XY, evolved through structural variation between X- and Y-chromosomes, triggering sex-specific differentiation in males.

results.title: Diversity and Convergence of Sex Determination Mechanisms in Teleost Fish.
results.author: J. Kitano
results.takeaway: Sex-determination mechanisms in fish are diverse and converge on temperature, with TGF- signaling pathway genes often used as master sex-determining genes.

results.title: Discovery of Sex-Determining Genes in Portunus trituberculatus: A Comparison of Male and Female Transcriptomes During Early Developmental Stages
results.author: W. Zhang
results.takeaway: PtDMY is a key gene involved in sex determination in Portunus trituberculatus crabs, with its expression in males during early developmental stages suggesting it may be a key regulator of the sex determination pathway.

results.title: Sex Determination in Insects: Variations on a Common Theme
results.author: D. Bopp
results.takeaway: Sex determination in insects is largely conserved, with variations in instructive and executive aspects, but the signal-relaying part remains less prone to changes.

results.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Sex Determination in Reptiles
results.author: T. Rhen
results.takeaway: Sex determination in reptiles is influenced by molecular, cellular, morphological, and physiological changes, and understanding these interactions can help understand the evolution of sexual differentiation mechanisms.

results.title: Cellular calcium and redox regulation: the mediator of vertebrate environmental sex determination?
results.author: M. Castelli
results.takeaway: Environmental cues in reptiles and fish are sensed by conserved calcium and redox elements, which then activate signal transduction pathways or influence epigenetic processes, driving differential expression of sex genes.

results.title: Plasticity of gene‐regulatory networks controlling sex determination: of masters, slaves, usual suspects, newcomers, and usurpators
results.author: A. Herpin
results.takeaway: The molecular mechanisms controlling sex determination vary among various organisms and can change rapidly during evolution, challenging the classical view of a simple linear developmental cascade.

results.title: Functions of the transcription factor myb-like in sex determination and differentiation in Portunus trituberculatus
results.author: Shaoting Jia
results.takeaway: The transcription factor myb-like gene influences sex differentiation in Portunus trituberculatus by regulating IAG expression, potentially paving the way for single-sex breeding technology.

results.title: Molecular mechanisms of temperature-dependent sex determination in the context of ecological developmental biology.
results.author: Y. Matsumoto
results.takeaway: Temperature-dependent sex determination in red-eared slider turtles is influenced by two genes, FoxL2 and Dmrt1, which transduce environmental temperature signals into biological signals determining gonadal sex.

results.title: Mammalian sex determination: a molecular drama.
results.author: A. Swain
results.takeaway: Mammalian sex determination is a complex, network-based system with multiple gene products playing key roles, avoiding intersex phenotypes and requiring coordination across cell lineages.

results.title: Sex Determination, Gonadal Sex Differentiation and Pl--asticity in Vertebrate Species.
results.author: Y. Nagahama
results.takeaway: Vertebrates exhibit diverse sex determination mechanisms, with some species maintaining some degree of sexual plasticity into adulthood, aiding in understanding evolutionary conundrums.

results.title: Female Sex Determination Factors in Ceratitis capitata: Molecular and Structural Basis of TRA and TRA2 Recognition
results.author: M. M. Perrotta
results.takeaway: In the Mediterranean fruitfly, Ceratitis capitata, female-specific Transformer (TRA) and non-sex-specific Transformer 2 (TRA2) splicing factors interact to promote female-specific splicing, with a conserved TRA2 recognition motif in the TRA sequence.

results.title: LncRNA gene ANTSR coordinates complementary sex determination in the Argentine ant
results.author: Qiaowei Pan
results.takeaway: The Argentine ant's complementary sex determination (CSD) system involves a long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) gene, ANTSR, which coordinates sex determination based on complementarity among noncoding alleles.

results.title: Molecular mechanisms of sex determination and gonadal sex differentiation in fish
results.author: Y. Nagahama
results.takeaway: Fish sex determination and gonadal sex differentiation are regulated by DMY in medaka, estrogens in tilapia, and DMRT1 in testicular differentiation.

results.title: Molecular parallelism in the evolution of a master sex‐determining role for the anti‐Mullerian hormone receptor 2 gene (amhr2) in Midas cichlids
results.author: C. Nacif
results.takeaway: The anti-Mullerian hormone receptor 2 gene (amhr2) plays a key role in sex determination in Midas cichlids, with molecular parallelism playing a role in the evolution of sex determination mechanisms.

results.title: Recognition of polymorphic Csd proteins determines sex in the honeybee
results.author: M. Otte
results.takeaway: Different versus identical variants of a single protein determine sex in honeybees, with amino acid differences activating the female pathway and absence of polymorphisms inactivating the male pathway.

results.title: A chromosome‐level genome assembly enables the identification of the follicule stimulating hormone receptor as the master sex‐determining gene in the flatfish Solea senegalensis
results.author: R. Herrán
results.takeaway: The follicle stimulating hormone receptor (fshr) is the master sex-determining gene in the flatfish Solea senegalensis, with a novel molecular sexing tool and differential expression between male and female gonads.

facets.q: Characterizes the prawn's colour-change reactions — an early analysis of crustacean chromatophore control.
What is the molecular and cellular mechanism of this phenomenon in Crustacea?
