results.title: Background colour induced modification in general body coloration of freshwater prawn Macrobrachium lamarrei (Crustacea-Decapoda)
results.author: S. Shukla
results.journal: International Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Studies
results.takeaway: Darker background colors significantly increase the number of chromatophores in freshwater prawns, with the order of darkness being white followed by black.

results.title: Cellular aspects of the control of physiological color changes in crustaceans.
results.author: M. Fingerman
results.takeaway: Red pigment-concentrating hormone stimulates sodium ion exchange, while red pigment-dispersing hormone stimulates calcium ion entry, affecting red coloration in prawns.

results.title: Mechanisms of colour adaptation in the prawn Penaeus monodon
results.author: N. Wade
results.takeaway: Prawns adapt to dark substrates by increasing CRCN protein and astaxanthin, while light substrates reduce CRCN protein but retain the carotenoid in an esterified form.

results.title: Insights into the mechanism of color formation of the freshwater prawn (Macrobrachium rosenbergii) revealed by de novo assembly transcriptome analysis.
results.author: Junhui Liu
results.journal: Comparative biochemistry and physiology. Part D, Genomics & proteomics
results.takeaway: The transcriptome analysis reveals that apolipoprotein D, crustacyanin, cytochrome P450, and tyrosinase may play a role in the color formation of freshwater prawns (Macrobrachium rosenbergii).

results.title: Microtubules, microfilaments, and pigment movement in the chromatophores of Palaemonetes vulgaris (Crustacea).
results.author: W. Robison
results.takeaway: The glass shrimp's rapid color change is mediated by translocations of pigments within stellate cells called chromatophores, while the slow color change is effected by selective increases in certain types of chromatophore pigments.

results.title: Crustacean Color-Change Hormone: Amino Acid Sequence and Chemical Synthesis
results.author: P. Fernlund
results.takeaway: The blanching hormone of Pandalus borealis prawns has a unique amino acid sequence and is active in picogram amounts when tested in shrimps.

results.title: Effects of the antidepressant fluoxetine on pigment dispersion in chromatophores of the common sand shrimp, Crangon crangon: repeated experiments paint an inconclusive picture
results.author: A. Ford
results.takeaway: Antidepressants' effects on color change in common sand shrimp remain inconclusive, with inconsistent results between trials and potential for improved repeatability in future experiments.

results.title: Effect of temperature on Chromatophores of freshwater prawn, Macrobrachium lamarrei (Crustacea-Decapoda)
results.author: S. Shukla
results.takeaway: Temperature affects the coloration and chromatophore structure of freshwater prawns, with dark colors at low temperatures and lighter colors at high temperatures, impacting their marketing value.

results.title: EFFECT OF EYE-STALK ABLATION ON COLORATION IN PRAWN
results.author: K. Kant
results.takeaway: Bilaterally ablated prawns (BEA) show better coloration than unablated and uni-laterally ablated prawns, due to the absence of both eye-stalks, leading to a concentration of pigments in the carapace and a dark appearance.

results.title: Molecular Characterisation of Colour Formation in the Prawn Fenneropenaeus merguiensis
results.author: N. Ertl
results.takeaway: This study identified genes involved in crustacean coloration, including crustacyanin, sarcoplasmic calcium-binding protein, and actin, and found differences in gene expression and astaxanthin levels between albino, light, and dark prawns.

results.title: Moulting and colour changes in the Prawn, Caridina weberi
results.author: R. Nagabhushanam
results.takeaway: Caridina weberi prawns undergo small but significant color changes during the moult cycle, with red and white pigments more dispersed at stage D.

results.title: Background selection for camouflage shifts in accordance with color change in an intertidal prawn
results.author: Samuel D. Green
results.takeaway: As chameleon prawns change color and improve camouflage, their behavioral background matching shifts to match the new color, reinforcing camouflage in their natural habitat.

results.title: Background color effect on the pigmentation of prawn Macrobrachium tenellum
results.author: M. Palomera
results.journal: Latin American Journal of Aquatic Research
results.takeaway: Prawn Macrobrachium tenellum modify their pigmentation according to the different background colors in experimental aquariums.

results.title: The Controlling Mechanism of Chromatophores in Palaemonetes.
results.author: F. Brown,
results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
results.takeaway: The common prawn's red and yellow chromatophores contract and white pigment expands, with hormones found in the eyestalks and central nervous organs controlling these responses.

results.title: Background matching in the brown shrimp Crangon crangon: adaptive camouflage and behavioural-plasticity
results.author: A. Siegenthaler
results.takeaway: Brown shrimp can effectively camouflage themselves in dynamic estuarine habitats by rapidly changing their color, influenced by illumination and sediment color.

results.title: Rapid expansion of pigmentation genes in penaeid shrimp with absolute preservation of function
results.author: Alyssa M Budd
results.takeaway: Penaeid shrimp have undergone significant expansion and diversification of their pigmentation genes, but their functional role in color production has remained strictly conserved.

results.title: Control of Chromatophores in Leander serratus
results.author: E. Stephenson
results.takeaway: Leander serratus prawns' color-change mechanism involves red and yellow chromatophores contracting and reflecting yellow chromatophores expanding, with the reverse effect occurring when light on a dark background.

results.title: Rate of production and release of chromatophorotropins in crustaceans
results.author: T. Aoto
results.takeaway: Chromatophorotropins in crustaceans play a role in diurnal variation of body color, with the brain-RPDH being released quickly and the tritocerebral commissure playing a lesser role.

results.title: Colour change and behavioural choice facilitate chameleon prawn camouflage against different seaweed backgrounds
results.author: Samuel D. Green
results.takeaway: Chameleon prawns effectively camouflage against different seaweed backgrounds by changing color and selecting color-matching substrates, enabling them to adapt to diverse environments.

results.title: Role of hypoxia in the behaviour, physiology, immunity and response mechanisms of crustaceans: A review
results.author: Cheng Zheng
results.takeaway: Hypoxic stress in aquaculture systems can negatively impact crustacean behavior, survival, antioxidant ability, metabolic processes, and innate immunity, requiring multiple measures to prevent and regulate adverse effects.

results.title: Insights on Molecular Mechanisms of Ovarian Development in Decapod Crustacea: Focus on Vitellogenesis-Stimulating Factors and Pathways
results.author: Vidya Jayasankar
results.takeaway: Ovarian maturation in crustaceans is regulated by antagonistic inhibitory and stimulating factors, with potential applications in aquaculture technology development.

results.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Reception and Perireception in Crustacean Chemoreception: A Comparative Review.
results.author: C. Derby
results.takeaway: Crustacean chemoreception relies on unique gene families and repurposing of existing proteins, with potential for further discovery of new chemoreceptors and perireceptor events.

results.title: Mechanisms of apoptosis in Crustacea: what conditions induce versus suppress cell death?
results.author: M. Menze
results.journal: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death
results.takeaway: Crustacean apoptosis mechanisms are more diverse than previously thought, potentially enabling some species to survive harsh environmental insults.

results.title: Recent insights into hematopoiesis in crustaceans
results.author: Man-jun Liu
results.takeaway: Crustaceans' hematopoiesis is regulated by transcriptional factors, humoral factors, and cellular homeostasis, ensuring cellular and humoral immunity and maintaining life.

results.title: The role of pattern recognition receptors in crustacean innate immunity
results.author: B. Patnaik
results.takeaway: Pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) play a crucial role in crustacean innate immunity, enabling effective control and management of infectious diseases, enhancing the global crustacean aquaculture industry.

results.title: Cell Death in Crustacean Immune Defense
results.author: Zeyan Chen
results.takeaway: Crustaceans use NETosis and ferroptosis for pathogen defense, offering potential for developing targeted immune modulators and enhancing disease resistance in economically important species.

results.title: The clotting system in decapod crustaceans: History, current knowledge and what we need to know beyond the models.
results.author: R. Perdomo-Morales
results.takeaway: The clotting system in decapod crustaceans relies on the polymerization of plasmatic clotting protein, which is promoted by calcium-dependent transglutaminase, but differences among species and their diverse ecology suggest potential evolutionary differences.

results.title: Genes encoding putative bicarbonate transporters as a missing molecular link between molt and mineralization in crustaceans
results.author: Shai Abehsera
results.takeaway: The SLC4 family of transporters plays a key role in the tight coupling between molt cycle events and mineral deposition in crustaceans, such as crayfish.

results.title: Immune responses and immunoprotection in crustaceans with special reference to shrimp
results.author: Amod Kulkarni
results.takeaway: Shrimp have an efficient innate immune system, which can be used to develop effective immunoprophylactic measures against various pathogens.

results.title: Transcriptomic analysis of adaptive mechanisms in response to sudden salinity drop in the mud crab, Scylla paramamosain
results.author: Huan Wang
results.takeaway: Scylla paramamosain mud crabs adapt to sudden salinity drops by enhancing intracellular metabolic activities and regulating ion transport and amino acid metabolism.

results.title: Deciphering Molecular Mechanisms Governing the Reproductive Molt of Macrobrachium nipponense: A Transcriptome Analysis of Ovaries across Various Molting Stages
results.author: Huwei Yuan
results.takeaway: The molecular mechanisms regulating the molting process of Macrobrachium nipponense crustaceans include mTOR, insect hormone biosynthesis, TGF-beta, and Wnt signaling pathways, which crosstalk to control ecdysone synthesis and degradation.

results.title: Neuroendocrine‐immune regulation mechanism in crustaceans: A review
results.author: Ruixue Tong
results.takeaway: The neuroendocrine-immune system plays a crucial role in maintaining homeostasis and enhancing environmental adaptability in crustaceans, which can help prevent and control shrimp diseases in aquaculture.

results.title: Glucose transporter GLUT1 expression is important for oriental river prawn (Macrobrachium nipponense) hemocyte adaptation to hypoxic conditions
results.author: Xichao Sun
results.takeaway: GLUT1 expression in hemocytes of oriental river prawns is crucial for adaptation to hypoxic conditions, with a close relationship between hypoxia-mediated glycolysis and GLUT1 in hemocytes.

results.title: Investigating Low‐Temperature Stress Responses in Crustacea Aquatic Species Through Comparative Transcriptomics
results.author: Ying Chen
results.takeaway: Crustacean species exhibit shared and species-specific responses to low-temperature stress, offering a foundation for breeding cold-tolerant strains to enhance aquaculture resilience.

results.title: Pattern recognition receptors in Crustacea: immunological roles under environmental stress
results.author: Jesús Luis Betancourt
results.takeaway: Crustacean immune responses can be enhanced by enhancing their ability to recognize pathogens under environmental stressors, potentially reducing economic losses in aquaculture.

results.title: Homeostatic responses of crustaceans to salinity changes
results.author: R. Thabet
results.takeaway: Crustaceans exhibit exceptional abilities in coping with salinity changes, with gills and antennal glands playing a key role in maintaining hydromineral homeostasis.

results.title: Crustacean molt-inhibiting hormone: structure, function, and cellular mode of action.
results.author: T. Nakatsuji
results.journal: Comparative biochemistry and physiology. Part A, Molecular & integrative physiology
results.takeaway: Molt-inhibiting hormone (MIH) in Crustaceans regulates ecdysteroidogenesis through cellular signaling pathways, with calcium potentially playing a role through activation of glandular PDE1.

results.title: Contrasting strategies of osmotic and ionic regulation in freshwater crabs and shrimps: gene expression of gill ion transporters
results.author: Milene Mantovani
results.takeaway: Freshwater crabs and shrimps exhibit distinct osmotic and ionic regulation strategies, with crabs showing a more robust hypo-osmotic ability and shrimps showing a more robust hyper-osmotic ability.

results.title: Live imaging reveals the progenitors and cell dynamics of limb regeneration
results.author: Frederike Alwes
results.takeaway: Live imaging of leg regeneration in crustaceans reveals that there are no specialized stem cells for epidermis, and most epidermal cells proliferate and contribute to new segments in the regenerating leg.

results.title: The inbred newt genome unveils molecular mechanisms of behavior, development, and regeneration in urodele amphibians
results.author: Yuki Kimura
results.takeaway: The inbred newt genome provides insights into amphibian evolution, behavior, development, and regeneration, offering a valuable model organism for studying vertebrate development and regeneration.

results.title: Development of a ZRS Reporter System for the Newt (Cynops pyrrhogaster) During Terrestrial Limb Regeneration
results.author: M. Casco-Robles
results.takeaway: This study developed a ZRS reporter system for newts, enabling monitoring of sonic hedgehog expression during terrestrial limb regeneration, providing valuable insights into regenerative medicine.

results.title: Altered metabolic state impedes limb regeneration in salamanders
results.author: Zhengrong Peng
results.takeaway: Under extreme physiological stress, salamanders can exploit alternative strategies to secure blastema formation for limb regeneration, but limb outgrowth and patterning are significantly attenuated.

results.title: The mRNA and microRNA Landscape of the Blastema Niche in Regenerating Newt Limbs
results.author: Qi Zhang
results.takeaway: Four key genes and seven human microRNAs are identified in the blastema niche of regenerating newt limbs, offering valuable insights for further exploration of tissue regeneration processes.

results.title: Reviewing the Effects of Skin Manipulations on Adult Newt Limb Regeneration: Implications for the Subcutaneous Origin of Axial Pattern Formation
results.author: M. Casco-Robles
results.takeaway: Adult newts can regenerate limbs with a normal axial pattern regardless of skin manipulation, suggesting that tissue under the skin plays a primary role in limb regeneration.

results.title: FGF8 and SHH substitute for anterior–posterior tissue interactions to induce limb regeneration
results.author: Eugen Nacu
results.takeaway: FGF8 and SHH signaling in axolotls drive limb regeneration by providing complementary cross-inductive signals, enabling complete limb regeneration with full skeletal element development.

results.title: Plasticity and reprogramming of differentiated cells in amphibian regeneration
results.author: J. Brockes
results.takeaway: Amphibian regeneration is primarily driven by plasticity and reprogramming of differentiated cells, rather than a'reserve-cell' mechanism.

results.title: NEUROTROPHIC CONTROL OF LIMB REGENERATION IN THE NEWT *
results.author: M. Singer
results.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
results.takeaway: Neurotrophic control of limb regeneration in amphibians, particularly newts and salamanders, is crucial for restoring structure and function after amputation.

results.title: Position dependent expression of a homeobox gene transcript in relation to amphibian limb regeneration.
results.author: Pierre Savard
results.takeaway: The homeobox gene transcript NvHbox 1 plays a role in amphibian limb regeneration, with higher expression in proximal blastemas and less in distal ones, potentially explaining the loss of regenerative ability with maturation in adult anurans.

results.title: A tissue-mapped axolotl de novo transcriptome enables identification of limb regeneration factors
results.author: D. M. Bryant
results.takeaway: Axolotls can replace entire limbs, and the de novo transcriptome identified cirbp as a cytoprotective factor during regeneration, while kazald1 expression disrupts regeneration.

results.title: Newt Hoxa13 has an essential and predominant role in digit formation during development and regeneration.
results.author: T. Takeuchi
results.takeaway: Hoxa13 plays a crucial role in digit formation during development and regeneration in newts, suggesting potential contributions to fin-to-limb transition.

results.title: Identification of Y-chromosome Turnover in Newts Fails to Support a Sex Chromosome Origin for the Triturus Balanced Lethal System
results.author: J. France
results.takeaway: The balanced lethal system in Triturus newts does not appear to have originated from an ancestral Y-chromosome, as its Y-chromosome is not homologous to its sister genus Lissotriton.

results.title: The Cytological Mechanism of the Triploidy-Inducing Effect of Heat on Eggs of the Newt, Triturus Viridescens.
results.author: G. Fankhauser
results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

results.title: Hybridization and introgression in deeply differentiated salamander species – molecular genetics and a reappraisal of Dr. Louis Vallée’s osteological data
results.author: J. Arntzen
results.takeaway: Introgression is low but asymmetric in the crested newt (Triturus cristatus) and marbled newt (T. marmoratus), with a partial breakdown of the species barrier and limited gene flow beyond F1 hybrid generation.

results.title: Observations on the mechanism of induction of supernumerary limbs in adult Triturus viridescens.
results.author: C. W. Bodemer

results.title: Cellular mechanotransduction in health and diseases: from molecular mechanism to therapeutic targets
results.author: Xingpeng Di
results.takeaway: Cellular mechanotransduction plays a crucial role in regulating biological processes, but excessive mechanical stimulation can lead to pathological processes like multi-organ fibrosis and cancer immunotherapy resistance.

results.title: Experiments on the phenomenon of paralysis produced by a toxin occurring in Triturus embryos
results.author: V. Twitty

results.title: Structures and gating mechanism of human TRPM2
results.author: Longfei Wang
results.takeaway: Human TRPM2's molecular mechanism of concerted gating by ADPR and calcium is explained in cryo-electron microscopy structures, providing insights into other TRP channels.

results.title: Microtubule-severing enzymes: From cellular functions to molecular mechanism
results.author: Francis J. McNally
results.takeaway: Microtubule-severing enzymes play a crucial role in diverse cellular processes, but their structure, biophysical mechanism, and regulation remain poorly understood.

results.title: A molecular mechanism for transthyretin amyloidogenesis
results.author: A. W. Yee
results.takeaway: Transthyretin amyloidogenesis occurs through a parallel equilibrium of partially unfolded species, with destabilizing mutations in the C-D loop of the protein enhancing the rate of fibrillation.

results.title: Molecular mechanisms of mitochondrial dynamics
results.author: Luis-Carlos Tábara
results.takeaway: Recent structural insights into core mitochondrial dynamics proteins reveal the complex interplay between proteins, lipids, and organelles during mitochondrial membrane fusion and fission.

results.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Plant Trichome Development
results.author: Guoliang Han
results.takeaway: Plant hormones, transcription factors, the cell cycle, and epigenetic modifications play crucial roles in trichome development, providing protection against various stresses and releasing valuable secondary metabolites.

results.title: Cellular and Molecular Mechanisms of Metformin Action
results.author: Traci E LaMoia
results.takeaway: Metformin's glucose-lowering effect in type 2 diabetes patients is mainly mediated through inhibition of hepatic gluconeogenesis, with a redox-dependent mechanism of action being proposed.

results.title: Phenomenon of aging liver. Part I: Molecular-genetic, cellular, and tissue mechanisms
results.author: Prikhodko A.M. Prikhodko

results.title: Cellular senescence: Molecular mechanisms and pathogenicity
results.author: Wenqiang Wei
results.takeaway: Cellular senescence is linked to aging-related diseases and can trigger chronic inflammation, necessitating strategies to control it.

results.title: The effect of ultrasonic vibrations on molting in triturus viridescens.
results.author: H. Clark
results.takeaway: Ultrasonic vibrations increase the frequency of molting in Triturus viridescens, with a seasonal variation in response and effects at different energy levels and exposure periods.

results.title: Molecular and Cellular Mechanisms of Atrial Fibrosis in Atrial Fibrillation.
results.author: S. Nattel
results.takeaway: Understanding the molecular and cellular mechanisms of atrial fibrosis may lead to new opportunities for preventing and managing atrial fibrillation.

results.title: Molecular Mimetism Phenomenon in SARS Cov-2
results.author: Juan Farak Gomez
results.journal: Medical Journal of Clinical Trials & Case Studies
results.takeaway: Molecular mimicry is a link between SARS Cov2 infection and autoimmunity induced by immune responses targeting both virus and human proteins.

results.title: Mitochondrial dynamics: overview of molecular mechanisms
results.author: Lisa Tilokani
results.takeaway: Mitochondrial dynamics, a crucial cellular process, is regulated by large GTPases belonging to the Dynamin family, which play crucial roles in maintaining shape, distribution, and size, and are linked to various human diseases.

results.title: Cellular and molecular mechanisms of muscle atrophy
results.author: P. Bonaldo
results.takeaway: Understanding the key mechanisms regulating muscle mass can provide new therapeutic targets for prevention and treatment of muscle atrophy in metabolic and neuromuscular diseases.

results.title: Molecular basis for cellular compartmentalization by an ancient membrane fission mechanism
results.author: Javier Espadas

facets.q: Growth proceeds in regular stepwise ratios per moult — the empirical basis of what became 'Przibram's Rule' (~2.09x mass, ~1.26x linear dimension per instar).
What is the molecular and cellular mechanism of growth and allometry in Sphodromantis?

135.state: The modern field is active — Consensus retrieves 40 related papers, the most recent from 2025. The BVA paper itself is cited 60 times in this literature.

results.title: The Progression Factor in Insect Growth
results.author: F. S. Bodenheimer
results.takeaway: The growth factor in insect growth is a general rule of 2 for weight and i.26 for length, with deviations in complex cases being only deviations from this principle.

results.title: Relationship of Size of Fecal Pellets to Larval Molts in Lepidoptera
results.author: J. B. Sardesai
results.journal: Annals of The Entomological Society of America
results.takeaway: The size of fecal pellets in Lepidoptera larvae can be used as an easy and reliable index for determining larval molt size, providing a more reliable method for entomologists than head-capsule size.

results.title: Instar sizes and growth in the Middle Permian monuran Dasyleptus brongniarti (Insecta: Machilida: Dasyleptidae)
results.author: A. Heckert
results.takeaway: Dasyleptus brongniarti, a Middle Permian wingless insect, shows body length increasing by a factor of 1.13 to 1.37 at each instar, with an average of 1.24 over six instars.

results.title: Towards a mechanistic understanding of insect life history evolution: oxygen‐dependent induction of moulting explains moulting sizes
results.author: S. M. Kivelä
results.journal: Biological Journal of The Linnean Society

results.title: THE DETERMINATION OF RELATIVE GROWTH IN CRUSTACEA
results.author: R. Hartnoll
results.takeaway: Relative growth in Crustacea generally follows the simple allometry rule, y = Bx, with growth progressing through a series of phases and transition changes often resulting in critical moults or metamorphosis.

results.title: Developmental variation in the forest tent caterpillar: life history consequences of a threshold size for pupation
results.author: E. Étilé
results.takeaway: Forest tent caterpillars have a higher threshold size for pupation, which requires more instars and longer development time, but does not necessarily lead to smaller adult size.

results.title: A Quantitative Analysis of Growth and Size Regulation in Manduca sexta: The Physiological Basis of Variation in Size and Age at Metamorphosis
results.author: L. Grunert
results.takeaway: Manduca sexta larvae grow progressively from instar to instar, with temperature-dependent declines in mass-specific growth rate, and different adult body sizes affect larval growth and development time.

results.title: The Hiatt growth diagram for crustacea
results.author: J. Mauchline
results.takeaway: The Hiatt growth diagram for crustaceans shows that growth factors decrease logarithmically at successive moults, and using these constants can help determine moulting and growth sequences throughout a crustacean's life.

results.title: Przibram's Rule and male body‐size dimorphism in Zygoballus rufipes (Araneae: Salticidae)
results.author: D. Faber
results.takeaway: Males of Zygoballus rufipes spider mature at two different instars, suggesting two size-based alternative life-history strategies.

results.title: Growth ratios in holometabolous and hemimetabolous insects.
results.author: B. Cole
results.journal: Annals of The Entomological Society of America

results.title: Growth ‘rules’ and the larvae of decapod crustaceans
results.author: A. L. Rice
results.takeaway: Decapod larvae generally follow Brooks's Law, but Przibram's Rule and Gurney's growth factor rule may not apply to the order as a whole.

results.title: QUANTITATIVE ANALYSIS OF LARVAL BODY GROWTH IN THE SILKWORM, BOMBYX MORI (LEPIDOPTERA: BOMBYCIDAE)
results.author: S. Prasad
results.takeaway: Bombyx mori silkworm larvae accumulate energy reserves and structures during growth, violating Dyar's constant rule, but show a progressive increase in body mass from third to fth instar.

results.title: Geometrics of growth in four species of Spodoptera
results.author: M. Ramaiah
results.takeaway: The linear growth ratio in Spodoptera species varies, with S. exigua showing the maximum progression factor between 2nd and 3rd instars.

results.title: Dyar's rule and multivariate allometric growth in nine species of waterstriders (Heteroptera: Gerridae)
results.author: C. Klingenberg
results.takeaway: Dyar's rule is inconsistent in waterstrider species, but growth ratios vary within a limited range, with head width growth ratios differing more between moults than multivariate size.

results.title: Allometric growth in two species of Ectobius (Dictyoptera: Blattidae)
results.author: V. Brown
results.takeaway: Allometric growth in Ectobius species shows significant variations, with few structures growing by simple allometry, and the choice of reference dimension and statistical model affects growth data estimates.

results.title: An equation for geometric progression in Brooks-Dyar growth ratios
results.author: T. Hawes
results.takeaway: A simple exponential equation can provide a more realistic representation of growth increments and quantify the degree of geometric progression in development, replacing transformations and providing a more precise method for evaluating agreement with the Brooks-Dyar rule.

results.title: Dyar's Rule and the Investment Principle: optimal moulting strategies if feeding rate is size-dependent and growth is discontinuous
results.author: J. Hutchinson
results.journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B
results.takeaway: The Investment Principle predicts optimal size increases and instar durations for animals with feeding rate dependent on moulting structures, offering a new adaptive explanation for Dyar's Rule and common deviations from it.

results.title: Growth of Insects with Reference to Progression Factors for Successive Growth Stages
results.author: F. Harries
results.journal: Annals of The Entomological Society of America
results.takeaway: This study demonstrates that Cicadellidae species show a consistent growth pattern, with a progression factor for each growth stage, supporting the Dyar rule and Przibram principle.

results.title: Biometrical analysis of growth in the larvae ofHeliothis armigera Hubner
results.author: G. G. Bilapate
results.journal: Proceedings of the Indian Academy of Sciences - Section B, Animal Sciences
results.takeaway: Heliothis armigera larvae show five distinct instars, but Przibram's rule cannot be applied to linear dimensions of larvae in successive stages.

results.title: A test of Przibram's Rule
results.author: A. Solow
results.takeaway: This test of Przibram's Rule avoids the problems of assigning individuals to instars and assuming the variance of logarithmic weight is equal.

results.title: Size and shape: the developmental regulation of static allometry in insects
results.author: A. Shingleton
results.takeaway: Recent advances in growth regulation and endocrinology suggest that insulin/IGF signaling may play a central role in regulating organismal shape and size in insects.

results.title: The developmental basis for allometry in insects.
results.author: David L. Stern
results.takeaway: Insects' organ sizes are determined based on total body size through autonomous growth, centralized measurement, and feedback between growing organs.

results.title: Growth and size control during development
results.author: Jannik Vollmer
results.takeaway: Organ size in organisms is controlled by their genotype, with related species able to produce organs of different sizes due to environmental factors.

results.title: Allometry of cell types in planarians by single-cell transcriptomics
results.author: Elena Emili
results.takeaway: Planarians of different sizes consist of the same basic cell types but in varying proportions, with gut basal cells being the most responsive to size changes, suggesting a role in energy storage.

results.title: Genetical Aspects of Metrical Growth and Form in Animals
results.author: A. Cock
results.takeaway: Longitudinal data is essential for studying genetic differences in growth and form in animals, and a new multivariate method is suggested for analyzing longitudinal data.

results.title: Elucidating roles of lipid remodeling and ion homeostasis in sustaining oyster allometric growth
results.author: G. He
results.takeaway: Allometric oysters exhibit rapid tissue growth through efficient energy metabolism and lipid remodeling, which can be used to improve meat yield in marine bivalves.

results.title: Allometry, Scaling and Ontogeny of Form-An Introduction to the Symposium.
results.author: H. Nijhout
results.takeaway: The study of allometry and scaling has become a diverse field, but progress is hindered by lack of coordination among diverse approaches.

results.title: Growth Models of Complex Allometries in Holometabolous Insects
results.author: H. Nijhout
results.takeaway: Allomeries among adult holometabolous insects result from normal developmental processes during metamorphosis, with imaginal disks competing for nutrients, potentially playing a role in the evolution of body proportions in ants and other insects.

results.title: Evolution of, and via, developmental plasticity: insights through the study of scaling relationships.
results.author: Sofia Casasa
results.takeaway: Developmental plasticity may play a role in the evolution of scaling relationships, facilitating adaptation and diversification in diverse traits.

results.title: A temporal allocation of amino acid resources ensures fitness and body allometry in Drosophila.
results.author: Luca Valzania
results.takeaway: Hexamerins, specific storage proteins in Drosophila, play a crucial role in tissue formation and adult fitness, with their absence altering body allometry.

results.title: Utilizing geometric morphometrics to investigate gene function during organ growth: Insights through the study of beetle horn shape allometry
results.author: P. Rohner
results.takeaway: Geometric morphometry can help distinguish between genes primarily affecting relative trait growth and those primarily affecting alternative developmental processes.

results.title: Structure and molecular basis of spermatid elongation in the Drosophila testis
results.author: Qiuru Huang
results.takeaway: Spermatid elongation in the testis involves microtubule-based axoneme assembly, individualization complex formation, and mitochondria maintenance, which are crucial for male fertility.

results.title: A muscle-epidermis-glia signaling axis sustains synaptic specificity during allometric growth in Caenorhabditis elegans
results.author: Jiale Fan
results.takeaway: A muscle-epidermis-glia signaling axis maintains synaptic specificity during allometric growth in Caenorhabditis elegans, preserving the synaptic pattern established during embryogenesis.

results.title: Developmental model of static allometry in holometabolous insects
results.author: A. Shingleton
results.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences
results.takeaway: The slope of nutritional static allometries in Drosophila melanogaster is controlled by the relative sensitivity of an organ's growth rate to changes in nutrition, and the relative duration of development when nutrition affects an organ's final size.

results.title: The worldwide allometric relationship in anatomical structures for plant roots
results.author: Yue Zhang
results.takeaway: Root allometry, where cortex thickness increases faster than stele radius with increasing root diameter, is common in plants and varies greatly across species, with implications for understanding plant ecology and physiology.

results.title: Single particle tracking-based reaction progress kinetic analysis reveals a series of molecular mechanisms of cetuximab-induced EGFR processes in a single living cell
results.author: Do-Hyeon Kim
results.takeaway: Using single particle tracking-based reaction progress kinetic analysis (sptRPKA), researchers identified a previously unknown intermediate state responsible for the selective targeting of cetuximab-induced EGFR endocytosis to cancer cells.

results.title: Streptomyces morphogenetics: dissecting differentiation in a filamentous bacterium
results.author: K. Flärdh
results.takeaway: Morphological differentiation in Streptomyces is closely integrated with growth, cell-cycle processes, and multicellular behavior, involving hormone-like extracellular signaling and diverse secondary metabolism.

results.title: Cellular Allometry of Mitochondrial Functionality Establishes the Optimal Cell Size
results.author: Teemu P. Miettinen
results.takeaway: Optimal cell size is determined by uncoupling mitochondrial content and functional scaling, resulting in maximized cellular fitness and proliferative capacity.

results.title: Growth polarity and cell division in Streptomyces.
results.author: K. Flärdh
results.takeaway: Streptomyces DivIVA protein and nucleoid migration contribute to bacterial growth polarity and cell division, leading to single-chromosome spores.

results.title: Bioelectric-calcineurin signaling module regulates allometric growth and size of the zebrafish fin
results.author: Jacob M. Daane
results.takeaway: The potassium channel kcnk5b plays a key role in regulating allometric growth and size of zebrafish fins, integrating calcineurin's growth effects and maintaining proper proportionality during development.

facets.q: Probes how far mammals regenerate the tail — testing the limited regenerative powers of warm-blooded vertebrates.
What is the molecular and cellular mechanism of regeneration in animals?

137.state: The modern field is active — Consensus retrieves 40 related papers, the most recent from 2025. The BVA paper itself is cited 1 times in this literature.

results.title: To regenerate or not to regenerate: Vertebrate model organisms of regeneration-competency and -incompetency
results.author: Can Aztekin
results.journal: Wound repair and regeneration : official publication of the Wound Healing Society [and] the European Tissue Repair Society
results.takeaway: Studying model organisms with varying regenerative abilities can help uncover factors contributing to regeneration-incompetency in mammals and test functional restoration strategies.

results.title: Thyroid hormone receptor knockout prevents the loss of Xenopus tail regeneration capacity at metamorphic climax
results.author: Shouhong Wang
results.takeaway: Thyroid hormone receptor knockout in Xenopus tadpoles preserves tail regeneration capacity at metamorphic climax, potentially offering new avenues for regenerative medicines in humans.

results.title: The myeloid lineage is required for the emergence of a regeneration-permissive environment following Xenopus tail amputation
results.author: T. Hiscock
results.takeaway: The myeloid lineage plays a crucial role in promoting tissue regeneration after tadpole tail amputation, with regeneration-competent tadpoles showing reparative myeloid cells and regeneration-incompetent tadpoles showing inflammatory myeloid cells.

results.title: Anatomical and histological analyses reveal that tail repair is coupled with regrowth in wild-caught, juvenile American alligators (Alligator mississippiensis)
results.author: Cindy Xu
results.takeaway: American alligators can regenerate tails, exhibiting a distinct wound repair pattern similar to lepidosaurs and amphibians.

results.title: Lizard Tail Regeneration As An Instructive Model of Enhanced Healing Capabilities In An Adult Amniote
results.author: Thomas P. Lozito
results.takeaway: Lizard tail regeneration serves as a valuable model for understanding and improving adult mammalian healing capabilities.

results.title: Tail Tales: What We Have Learned About Regeneration from Xenopus Laevis Tadpoles
results.author: Jessica Lara
results.takeaway: Tadpoles provide unique insights into regenerative biology, offering a model for understanding tissue repair constraints in higher organisms and shedding light on evolutionary loss of regenerative abilities.

results.title: Probe Sequencing Analysis of Regenerating Lizard Tails Indicates Crosstalk Among Osteoclasts, Epidermal Cells, and Fibroblasts
results.author: Darian J Gamble
results.takeaway: Crosstalk between osteoclasts and fibroblasts regulates blastema and epidermis formation during lizard tail regeneration.

results.title: Identification of a regeneration organizing cell in the Xenopus tail
results.author: Can Aztekin
results.takeaway: The regeneration-organizing cell (ROC) in tadpole tails ensures successful regeneration by forming the wound epidermis and signaling to progenitors to reconstitute lost tissue.

results.title: Tail Regeneration in Xenopus laevis as a Model for Understanding Tissue Repair
results.author: A. Tseng
results.takeaway: The tadpole tail of Xenopus laevis serves as a model system for understanding tissue regeneration, providing insights into regenerative therapies for human tissues and organs.

results.title: Neuronal activation in the axolotl brain promotes tail regeneration
results.author: S. Walker
results.takeaway: Activation of dpErk/etv1glutamatergic neurons in the axolotl brain is essential for successful tail regeneration after injury, shedding light on how neurons outside the injury site respond to damage.

results.title: The Secreted Protein Disulfide Isomerase Ag1 Lost by Ancestors of Poorly Regenerating Vertebrates Is Required for Xenopus laevis Tail Regeneration
results.author: A. S. Ivanova
results.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
results.takeaway: The loss of the secreted protein disulfide isomerase Ag1 in warm-blooded vertebrates may contribute to their poorer regenerative ability, as it is essential for frog tail regeneration.

results.title: Review: Biological and Molecular Differences between Tail Regeneration and Limb Scarring in Lizard An Inspiring Model Addressing Limb Regeneration in Amniotes
results.author: L. Alibardi
results.journal: Journal of Experimental Zoology Part B: Molecular and Developmental Evolution
results.takeaway: Lizards show a unique model for tissue regeneration and scarring in amniotes, with tail regeneration resulting from low inflammation and high cell proliferation, while limb scarring occurs due to intense inflammation and lack of FGFs.

results.title: A novel amniote model of epimorphic regeneration: the leopard gecko, Eublepharis macularius
results.author: K. McLean
results.takeaway: Leopard geckos exhibit a highly conserved pattern of epimorphic regeneration, with a latent period of scar-free healing and regeneration occurring through blastema-mediated cell proliferation.

results.title: Transcriptomic Analysis of Tail Regeneration in the Lizard Anolis carolinensis Reveals Activation of Conserved Vertebrate Developmental and Repair Mechanisms
results.author: Elizabeth D. Hutchins
results.takeaway: Lizard tail regeneration involves activation of conserved developmental and wound response pathways, offering potential targets for regenerative medical therapies.

results.title: Evolutionary divergence in tail regeneration between Xenopus laevis and Xenopus tropicalis
results.author: Shouhong Wang
results.takeaway: Xenopus tropicalis lacks the refractory period in tail regeneration, indicating a potential evolutionary divergence in tissue regeneration capacity.

results.title: Single Cell Sequencing Analysis of Lizard Phagocytic Cell Populations and Their Role in Tail Regeneration.
results.author: R. Londono
results.journal: Journal of immunology and regenerative medicine
results.takeaway: Lizard macrophages play a critical role in lizard tail regeneration, with high levels of MMPs and faster recruitment to tail amputation injuries compared to mouse populations.

results.title: Tail and Spinal Cord Regeneration in Urodelean Amphibians
results.author: Eleonora N Grigoryan
results.takeaway: Urodelean amphibians can regenerate their tail and spinal cord throughout their life, highlighting the importance of cell dedifferentiation and mutual molecular regulation in tissue regeneration.

results.title: Sall Genes and Proteins Activation during Early Tail and Limb Regeneration in the Lizard Podarcis muralis Suggests Dedifferentiation
results.author: Alibardi Lorenzo
results.takeaway: Cell dedifferentiation occurs during early stages of tail and limb amputation in lizards, contributing to their regeneration or scarring.

results.title: Tail regeneration in Lepidosauria as an exception to the generalized lack of organ regeneration in amniotes.
results.author: L. Alibardi
results.journal: Journal of experimental zoology. Part B, Molecular and developmental evolution
results.takeaway: Lepidosaurians, lizards, have evolved tail regeneration as an exception to the general lack of organ regeneration in amniotes, due to the loss of metamorphosis genes and an effective immune system.

results.title: Transcriptional dynamics of tail regeneration in Xenopus tropicalis
results.author: Jessica K. Chang
results.takeaway: Xenopus tropicalis tadpoles can rapidly regenerate complex tissues, including tails, using a complex network of biological signaling processes.

results.title: The cellular basis for animal regeneration
results.author: E. Tanaka
results.takeaway: Animal regeneration involves various cellular strategies, including pluripotent stem cells, tissue-specific stem cells, and dedifferentiation, using various cell types.

results.title: Animal regeneration in the era of transcriptomics
results.author: Loïc Bideau
results.takeaway: Recent data on animal regeneration models has identified key shared mechanisms, shedding light on the evolution of regeneration and its control mechanisms.

results.title: Hallmarks of Regeneration
results.author: K. Poss
results.takeaway: Regeneration in various animal species involves activation of a cell source, initiation of regenerative programs, interplay with supporting cells, and control of tissue size and function.

results.title: Evolution of Regeneration in Animals: A Tangled Story
results.author: A. Elchaninov
results.takeaway: The evolution of regenerative capacity in animals is complex and not always beneficial, driven by signaling pathways and adaptive immunity advances.

results.title: Regeneration in Echinoderms: Molecular Advancements
results.author: J. Medina-Feliciano
results.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
results.takeaway: This study identifies genes and signaling pathways involved in echinoderm regeneration, providing insights into the molecular basis of regeneration in other animal taxa.

results.title: Emerging roles of mitochondria in animal regeneration
results.author: Yun Zhao
results.takeaway: Mitochondria play a crucial role in animal regeneration, with defects and perturbations in mitochondria leading to regeneration failure, and future studies should focus on their regulation of aging in regeneration.

results.title: Cellular and Molecular Mechanism of Cardiac Regeneration: A Comparison of Newts, Zebrafish, and Mammals
results.author: L. de Wit
results.takeaway: Cardiac regeneration in lower vertebrates like newts and zebrafish is more effective than in adult mammals, suggesting potential for future interventions to promote regeneration in mammals.

results.title: The Molecular and Cellular Choreography of Appendage Regeneration.
results.author: E. Tanaka
results.takeaway: Limb regeneration reveals the molecular events that integrate growth control, cell fate programming, and positional information, providing insights for engineers to recreate complex multi-tissue structures.

results.title: Beyond Casual Resemblances: Rigorous Frameworks for Comparing Regeneration Across Species.
results.author: M. Srivastava
results.journal: Annual review of cell and developmental biology
results.takeaway: This review provides a framework for comparing regeneration across animals, focusing on gene regulatory networks, to identify unifying principles of regeneration biology across animals, benefiting evolutionary studies and human regenerative medicine.

results.title: Wound‐induced cell proliferation during animal regeneration
results.author: Lorenzo Ricci
results.takeaway: Shared wound-induced mechanisms regulate cell division during regeneration in various animal species, with similarities in signaling pathways across distantly related species.

results.title: Gene regulatory programs of tissue regeneration
results.author: J. A. Goldman
results.takeaway: Understanding gene regulatory networks in tissue regeneration pathways could potentially enable targeted reactivation for treating human injuries and degenerative diseases.

results.title: Cellular and molecular mechanisms of development and regeneration.
results.author: Kalika Prasad
results.takeaway: Cellular and molecular mechanisms of development and regeneration play a crucial role in organism renewal and repair, offering insights into developmental biology, tissue engineering, and regenerative medicine.

results.title: Regulation and phylogeny of skeletal muscle regeneration.
results.author: Meryem B. Baghdadi
results.takeaway: Skeletal muscle regeneration involves a complex interaction between stem cells, progeny, and stromal cells, which is crucial for successful repair and re-establishing homeostasis after injury.

results.title: Liver Regeneration
results.author: G. Michalopoulos
results.takeaway: Liver regeneration restores hepatic mass and preserves normal liver histology in adult animals, utilizing specific stimuli and feedback loops to maintain metabolic support.

results.title: Comparative regenerative mechanisms across different mammalian tissues
results.author: S. Iismaa
results.takeaway: Recent insights into molecular mechanisms of regeneration in various mammalian tissues show potential for future regenerative therapies, despite constraints like immune responses, extracellular matrix composition, age, injury type, and physiological adaptations.

results.title: PPARβ/δ: Linking Metabolism to Regeneration
results.author: Ajit Magadum
results.takeaway: PPAR/ plays a crucial role in wound healing and regeneration in mammals, including skin, bone, and liver, and may be a promising target for promoting human organ repair.

results.title: Regeneration in Stentor coeruleus
results.author: W. Marshall
results.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
results.takeaway: Single cells can regenerate missing structures, resembling animal development and regeneration processes, and may have evolved by exploiting pre-existing subcellular developmental strategies from unicellular ancestors.

results.title: Comparative aspects of animal regeneration.
results.author: J. Brockes
results.journal: Annual review of cell and developmental biology
results.takeaway: Animal regeneration involves wound epithelium formation, regenerative progenitor cells, and morphogenesis, with common mechanisms in both vertebrates and invertebrates, and potential evolutionary origins.

results.title: Advances in signaling in vertebrate regeneration as a prelude to regenerative medicine.
results.author: Cristi L. Stoick-Cooper
results.takeaway: Understanding shared signaling pathways in vertebrate regeneration can accelerate the development of regenerative medicine therapies for organ and appendage regeneration in humans.

results.title: The Diversity of Muscles and Their Regenerative Potential across Animals
results.author: L. Zullo
results.takeaway: Muscle regeneration in metazoans reveals conserved and divergent cellular and molecular mechanisms, highlighting the importance of using non-canonical animal models for molecular studies.

results.title: What frog gill resorption brings: loss of function, cell death, and metabolic reorganization
results.author: L. Chang
results.takeaway: Gill resorption in frogs during metamorphosis leads to loss of respiratory function, cell death, and metabolic reorganization, highlighting their crucial role in facilitating the transition from aquatic to terrestrial habitats.

results.title: Differential effects of 3,5-T2 and T3 on the gill regeneration and metamorphosis of the Ambystoma mexicanum (axolotl)
results.author: I. Lazcano
results.takeaway: 3,5-T2 promotes partial gill retraction in axolotls but induces full metamorphosis at higher concentrations, potentially due to different gene activation patterns.

results.title: Functional analysis of thyroid hormone receptor beta in Xenopus tropicalis founders using CRISPR-Cas
results.author: Yuto Sakane
results.takeaway: Thyroid hormone receptor beta (TR) is not required for metamorphosis but contributes to the timing of resorptive events in tadpoles.

results.title: Glucocorticoid receptor mediates corticosterone-thyroid hormone synergy essential for metamorphosis in Xenopus tropicalis tadpoles.
results.author: Zachary R Sterner
results.takeaway: The glucocorticoid receptor (GR) plays a crucial role in enhancing thyroid hormone signaling and completing metamorphosis in tadpoles.

results.title: Mechanisms of Caspases 3/7/8/9 in the Degeneration of External Gills of Chinese Giant Salamanders (Andrias davidianus)
results.author: Shijun Yang
results.takeaway: Caspases 3/7/8/9 play a key role in the loss of external gills in Chinese giant salamanders during metamorphosis, with thyroid hormone treatment accelerating this process.

results.title: Metamorphic competence in urodeles: observations on the induction of gill resorption and its relationship to acid phosphatase.
results.author: D. G. Benson
results.takeaway: Acid phosphatase activity in urodele larvae increases 13-fold by day 7 after treatment with 3,5,3-triiodothyronine, suggesting a role in gill resorption during metamorphic competence.

results.title: A comparative perspective on lung and gill regeneration
results.author: L. Cadiz
results.takeaway: Fish and amphibians' gill regeneration offers a unique opportunity to uncover common signaling mechanisms for lung regeneration in all vertebrates, potentially leading to new advances in tissue repair after lung disease.

results.title: Effects of structural remodelling on gill physiology
results.author: Kathleen M. Gilmour
results.takeaway: Gill remodelling in fishes enables them to adapt to changing conditions, affecting physiological function and identifying potential evolutionary pathways.

results.title: Identification of signalling pathways involved in gill regeneration in zebrafish
results.author: L. Cadiz
results.takeaway: BMP, FGF, Notch, and Shh signaling pathways play a crucial role in gill regeneration in zebrafish, suggesting potential applications in respiratory organ regeneration.

results.title: The GH/IGF axis in the sea lamprey during metamorphosis and seawater acclimation.
results.author: D. Ferreira-Martins
results.takeaway: Metamorphosis in sea lampreys stimulates the GH/IGF axis, which promotes metamorphosis and seawater tolerance.

results.title: Gill regeneration in the mayfly Cloeon uncovers new molecular pathways in insect regeneration
results.author: C. Martin-Blanco
results.takeaway: The mayfly Cloeon can regenerate lost abdominal gills faster than normal development, revealing new molecular pathways in insect regeneration.

results.title: Opposite T3 Response of ACTG1–FOS Subnetwork Differentiate Tailfin Fate in Xenopus Tadpole and Post-hatching Axolotl
results.author: Gwenneg Kerdivel
results.takeaway: The fate of tailfin in Xenopus tadpoles and post-hatching Axolotls is influenced by the alternative transcriptional states of an fos-actg1 subnetwork, which controls distinct thyroid hormone responses and alternative tailfin fate.

results.title: Gene Expression Program Underlying Tail Resorption During Thyroid Hormone-Dependent Metamorphosis of the Ornamented Pygmy Frog Microhyla fissipes
results.author: Shouhong Wang
results.takeaway: Tail resorption in ornamented pygmy frogs shares many programs with other amphibian species, offering a valuable model for studying postembryonic development in vertebrates.

results.title: Local Thyroid Hormone Activation or Inactivation by Deiodinases Regulates Intestinal Remodeling and Tail Resorption during Xenopus Metamorphosis
results.author: Yuki Shibata
results.takeaway: Local thyroid hormone activation and inactivation by deiodinases is crucial for the timing and progression of organ-specific metamorphic events during frog metamorphosis.

results.title: Gill and Liver Transcript Expression Changes Associated With Gill Damage in Atlantic Salmon (Salmo salar)
results.author: M. Emam
results.takeaway: Gill damage in Atlantic salmon leads to upregulation of wound healing and stress-related transcripts in both gills and livers, potentially aiding in developing therapeutic diets to improve welfare.

results.title: Proliferation, survival and cell death in fish gills remodeling: From injury to recovery
results.author: C. F. Sales
results.takeaway: Fish gills can recover from injury and pollution damage if maintained in good-quality water, emphasizing the importance of conserving aquatic environments.

results.title: 11-Deoxycortisol controls hydromineral balance in the most basal osmoregulating vertebrate, sea lamprey (Petromyzon marinus)
results.author: C. Shaughnessy
results.takeaway: 11-deoxycortisol (S) is an osmoregulatory hormone in sea lampreys, and receptor-mediated discriminative corticosteroid regulation of hydromineral balance is an evolutionary basal trait among vertebrates.

results.title: Insufficiency of Thyroid Hormone in Frog Metamorphosis and the Role of Glucocorticoids
results.author: L. Sachs
results.takeaway: Thyroid hormone is crucial for frog metamorphosis, but glucocorticoids play a crucial role in modulating the rate of development and completing metamorphic events.

results.title: Thyroid hormone receptor knockout prevents the loss of Xenopus tail regeneration capacity at metamorphic climax
results.author: Shouhong Wang
results.takeaway: Thyroid hormone receptor knockout in Xenopus tadpoles preserves tail regeneration capacity at metamorphic climax, potentially offering new avenues for regenerative medicines in humans.

results.title: Teleost Metamorphosis: The Role of Thyroid Hormone
results.author: Marco A Campinho
results.takeaway: Thyroid hormones drive metamorphosis in teleosts, leading to dramatic morphological changes and adaptations, but more fundamental questions remain unanswered.

results.title: The cellular and signaling dynamics of salamander limb regeneration.
results.author: Elad Bassat
results.takeaway: Salamanders can regenerate their limbs after limb amputation, involving multiple cell types and coordinated cell-cell communication and physical events.

results.title: Salamanders: The molecular basis of tissue regeneration and its relevance to human disease
results.author: C. M. Arenas Gómez
results.takeaway: Salamanders are a valuable model for studying tissue regeneration, which may lead to therapies for human diseases in the future.

results.title: Model systems for regeneration: salamanders
results.author: A. Joven
results.takeaway: Salamanders are key models for regeneration, demonstrating remarkable abilities to regrow tissues, organs, and even whole body parts, providing insights into cell, tissue, and organ regeneration mechanisms.

results.title: Identification of the Adult Hematopoietic Liver as the Primary Reservoir for the Recruitment of Pro-regenerative Macrophages Required for Salamander Limb Regeneration
results.author: R. Debuque
results.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
results.takeaway: The liver is the primary source of leukocytes recruited to regenerating limbs in adult salamanders, with splenic maturation being dispensable for macrophage education.

results.title: Understanding positional cues in salamander limb regeneration: implications for optimizing cell-based regenerative therapies
results.author: Catherine D. McCusker
results.takeaway: Understanding positional interactions in salamander limb regeneration can improve the integration of cell-based regenerative therapies in humans.

results.title: Putative epithelial–mesenchymal transitions during salamander limb regeneration: Current perspectives and future investigations
results.author: Ryan T. Kim
results.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
results.takeaway: Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) plays a crucial role in salamander limb regeneration, regulating keratinocyte migration, epithelial cell invasion, and non-epithelial blastemal progenitor cell escape.

results.title: Altered metabolic state impedes limb regeneration in salamanders
results.author: Zhengrong Peng
results.takeaway: Under extreme physiological stress, salamanders can exploit alternative strategies to secure blastema formation for limb regeneration, but limb outgrowth and patterning are significantly attenuated.

results.title: Fundamental differences in dedifferentiation and stem cell recruitment during skeletal muscle regeneration in two salamander species.
results.author: Tatiana Sandoval-Guzmán
results.takeaway: Different salamander species exhibit diverse limb muscle regeneration mechanisms, with myofiber dedifferentiation in newts and resident PAX7(+) cells in axolotls.

results.title: Cell-to-Cell Connection in Plant Grafting - Molecular Insights into Symplasmic Reconstruction.
results.author: Ken-ichi Kurotani
results.takeaway: This review focuses on plasmodesmata formation during grafting, which is crucial for sharing cellular information among newly proliferated cells and achieving tissue differentiation correctly.

results.title: Homeostatic and regenerative neurogenesis in salamanders
results.author: A. Joven
results.takeaway: Salamanders exhibit large-scale regeneration in the adult central nervous system, enabling functional recovery in retina, brain, and spinal cord, with recent technological advances aiding in understanding regenerative processes.

results.title: Lessons from the swamp: developing small molecules that confer salamander muscle cellularization in mammals
results.author: JungIn Um
results.takeaway: Small molecules that induce salamander muscle cellularization in mammals show promise for enhancing tissue regeneration and cellular processes regulating regeneration.

results.title: The salamander blastema within the broader context of metazoan regeneration
results.author: Benjamin Tajer
results.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
results.takeaway: The salamander limb blastema serves as a useful reference model for comparing regeneration processes across different animal species, aiding in our understanding of regeneration and aiding in the selection of regenerative model systems.

results.title: Germline Transgenic Methods for Tracking Cells and Testing Gene Function during Regeneration in the Axolotl
results.author: Shahryar Khattak
results.takeaway: This study developed germline transgenic strains in the axolotl salamander, enabling molecular analysis of regeneration processes and revealing tissue-specific gene expression.

results.title: Immunity in salamander regeneration: where are we standing and where are we headed?
results.author: L. Bolaños-Castro
results.journal: Developmental dynamics : an official publication of the American Association of Anatomists
results.takeaway: The immune system plays a critical role in salamander regeneration, but our understanding of its precise roles and functions remains limited.

results.title: Advances in understanding the graft healing mechanism: a review of factors and regulatory pathways
results.author: Lixian Wang
results.takeaway: Recent advances in plant grafting research focus on factors and regulatory pathways that influence graft healing, aiming to improve successful grafting and create desirable grafting chimeras.

results.title: The salamander limb: a perfect model to understand imperfect integration during skeletal regeneration
results.author: Camilo Riquelme-Guzmán
results.takeaway: The salamander limb serves as a perfect model to understand imperfect integration during skeletal regeneration, as early events like tissue histolysis and patterning influence faithful regeneration of the appendicular skeleton.

results.title: Salamanders aid research into mechanisms of non‐canonical organ regeneration for clinical applications
results.author: Binxu Yin
results.takeaway: Salamanders' remarkable regenerative capacities have expanded to include non-canonical organs, offering potential solutions to challenging clinical problems.

results.title: Tissue transplantation in planarians: A useful tool for molecular analysis of pattern formation.
results.author: J. I. Rojo‐Laguna
results.takeaway: Tissue transplantation in planarians allows for the study of regeneration and pattern formation, with blastema formation resolving positional identity conflicts.

results.title: Amphibian Transplantation Reactions: A Review
results.author: N. Cohen
results.takeaway: Amphibian transplantation reactions vary among species, with Ranidae showing the strongest acute immune response to skin and organ allografts.

results.title: Mitochondrial transfer/transplantation: an emerging therapeutic approach for multiple diseases
results.author: Zong-gang Liu
results.takeaway: Artificial mitochondrial transfer/transplantation (AMT/T) shows potential in maintaining body homeostasis and regulating pathological processes, offering a potential therapeutic approach for various diseases.

results.author: M. R. Maxwell

results.author: L. Grunert

results.takeaway: The Spottilian mantis shrimp Squilla mantis in the Algiers region shows major growth in total size but minor growth in weight, indicating under-exploitation.

results.title: An equation for geometric progression in Brooks-Dyar growth ratios
results.author: T. Hawes

results.author: S. Mili
results.takeaway: The Spot-tail Mantis Shrimp, Squilla mantis, grows faster in the Gulf of Gabes than in the Gulfs of Hammamet and Tunis, with female growth being lower than male growth.

results.title: An enriched prey diet increases survival and growth rate in the early instars of two mantises
results.author: A. Baranowski

results.title: Comparative morphology of the post-embryonic development reveals the existence of distinct nymphal semaphoronts for Mantodea (Dictyoptera)
results.author: Marcus V. Scherrer
results.journal: Annales de la Société entomologique de France (N.S.)
results.takeaway: This study identifies two distinct nymphal forms for praying mantises, revealing shared developmental patterns across diverse lineages, and provides a key for taxonomic identification.

results.title: Stage-specific predation and functional response of predatory mites to greenhouse thrips (Heliothrips haemorrhoidalis) on avocado
results.author: Junlin Cao
results.takeaway: A. limonicus shows the highest predation rates and preference for first-instar thrips, making it a potential biocontrol agent for avocado pests.

results.title: Determination of Larval Instars of Dastarcus helophoroides (Coleoptera: Bothrideridae) Using Head Capsule Width Frequency Distribution
results.author: Tayyab Shaheen
results.takeaway: Larval instar determination of Dastarcus helophoroides beetles can accurately be determined using head capsule width frequency distribution, aiding in developing effective control programs and predicting future population levels.

results.title: Larval growth strategies in the genus Erebia Dalman, 1816 as analyzed by the size increment of the head capsule: different strategies – same goal (Lepidoptera: Nymphalidae)
results.author: Peter H. Roos
results.takeaway: Larval growth strategies in Erebia species vary based on the number of moults and life history, with some showing developmental polymorphism and a single size in the last instar.

results.title: The cultivable gut bacteria Enterococcus mundtii promotes early-instar larval growth of Conogethes punctiferalis via enhancing digestive enzyme activity.
results.author: Jiayu Li
results.takeaway: Enterococcus mundtii, a cultivable gut bacteria, significantly boosts early-instar larval growth of yellow peach moth Conogethes punctiferalis by enhancing digestive enzyme activity and total protein levels.

results.title: Dynamic Analysis of Major Components in the Different Developmental Stages of Tenebrio molitor
results.author: Xiao Yu
results.takeaway: Early larval stages of yellow mealworms have higher protein, fat, and chitin content, making them ideal for farming and reducing farming costs.

results.title: Sizing up spotted lanternfly nymphs for instar determination and growth allometry
results.author: Theodore Bien
results.takeaway: Spotted lanternfly nymphs can be staged using body mass and length, with their growth allometry varying between isometry and growing faster than predicted, aiding in understanding their life history patterns.

results.title: Quadratic resource value assessment during mantis shrimp (Stomatopoda) contests
results.author: P. A. Green
results.takeaway: Mantis shrimp exhibit quadratic resource value assessment, choosing burrows larger than their predicted best fit size and being more aggressive in contests over burrows predicted to be best fit, with burrow residents showing little evidence of resource value assessment.

results.title: Population dynamics of mantis shrimp (Gonodactylus chiragra Fabricius, 1781) in Batukalasi waters, South Sulawesi, Indonesia
results.author: Mawaddatan Warahma
results.journal: IOP Conference Series: Earth and Environmental Science
results.takeaway: The mantis shrimp population in Batukalasi, South Sulawesi, Indonesia, has a higher natural mortality rate than fishing mortality, but the relative yield per recruit is below optimum values for both female and male species.

results.title: Biology, ecology, and biogeography of eremic praying mantis Blepharopsis mendica (Insecta: Mantodea)
results.author: Zohre Mirzaee
results.takeaway: The Egyptian Flower mantis is a large, overwintering mantid with a variety of adaptations to its extreme and unpredictable habitat, found from the Canary Islands to Pakistan.

results.title: Antennal Development in the Praying Mantis (Tenodera aridifolia) Highlights Multitudinous Processes in Hemimetabolous Insect Species
results.author: T. Carle
results.takeaway: Praying mantis antennae develop with the addition of new segments at two distinct sites, highlighting the multitudinous processes in hemimetabolous insect species.

results.title: The Developmental Characteristics for the Head Capsule Width of Monochamus alternatus (Coleoptera: Cerambycidae) Larvae and Determination of the Number of Instars
results.author: Myeong Su Go
results.takeaway: Monochamus alternatus larvae pass five instars, with more precise head capsule width measurements than previous studies, and their development halts at the 10th instar stage.

results.title: Variation in growth and instar number in field and laboratory Manduca sexta
results.author: J. Kingsolver
results.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences
results.takeaway: Manduca sexta shows variation in larval instar number and growth rate, with six instars exhibiting slower growth rates and a threshold body size predicting whether an individual will have five or six instars.

results.title: Size and shape: the developmental regulation of static allometry in insects
results.author: A. Shingleton
results.takeaway: Recent advances in growth regulation and endocrinology suggest that insulin/IGF signaling may play a central role in regulating organismal shape and size in insects.

results.title: The developmental basis for allometry in insects.
results.author: David L. Stern
results.takeaway: Insects' organ sizes are determined based on total body size through autonomous growth, centralized measurement, and feedback between growing organs.

results.title: Growth and size control during development
results.author: Jannik Vollmer
results.takeaway: Organ size in organisms is controlled by their genotype, with related species able to produce organs of different sizes due to environmental factors.

results.title: Allometry of cell types in planarians by single-cell transcriptomics
results.author: Elena Emili
results.takeaway: Planarians of different sizes consist of the same basic cell types but in varying proportions, with gut basal cells being the most responsive to size changes, suggesting a role in energy storage.

results.title: Genetical Aspects of Metrical Growth and Form in Animals
results.author: A. Cock
results.takeaway: Longitudinal data is essential for studying genetic differences in growth and form in animals, and a new multivariate method is suggested for analyzing longitudinal data.

results.title: Elucidating roles of lipid remodeling and ion homeostasis in sustaining oyster allometric growth
results.author: G. He
results.takeaway: Allometric oysters exhibit rapid tissue growth through efficient energy metabolism and lipid remodeling, which can be used to improve meat yield in marine bivalves.

results.title: Allometry, Scaling and Ontogeny of Form-An Introduction to the Symposium.
results.author: H. Nijhout
results.takeaway: The study of allometry and scaling has become a diverse field, but progress is hindered by lack of coordination among diverse approaches.

results.title: Growth Models of Complex Allometries in Holometabolous Insects
results.author: H. Nijhout
results.takeaway: Allomeries among adult holometabolous insects result from normal developmental processes during metamorphosis, with imaginal disks competing for nutrients, potentially playing a role in the evolution of body proportions in ants and other insects.

results.title: Evolution of, and via, developmental plasticity: insights through the study of scaling relationships.
results.author: Sofia Casasa
results.takeaway: Developmental plasticity may play a role in the evolution of scaling relationships, facilitating adaptation and diversification in diverse traits.

results.title: A temporal allocation of amino acid resources ensures fitness and body allometry in Drosophila.
results.author: Luca Valzania
results.takeaway: Hexamerins, specific storage proteins in Drosophila, play a crucial role in tissue formation and adult fitness, with their absence altering body allometry.

results.title: Utilizing geometric morphometrics to investigate gene function during organ growth: Insights through the study of beetle horn shape allometry
results.author: P. Rohner
results.takeaway: Geometric morphometry can help distinguish between genes primarily affecting relative trait growth and those primarily affecting alternative developmental processes.

results.title: Structure and molecular basis of spermatid elongation in the Drosophila testis
results.author: Qiuru Huang
results.takeaway: Spermatid elongation in the testis involves microtubule-based axoneme assembly, individualization complex formation, and mitochondria maintenance, which are crucial for male fertility.

results.title: A muscle-epidermis-glia signaling axis sustains synaptic specificity during allometric growth in Caenorhabditis elegans
results.author: Jiale Fan
results.takeaway: A muscle-epidermis-glia signaling axis maintains synaptic specificity during allometric growth in Caenorhabditis elegans, preserving the synaptic pattern established during embryogenesis.

results.title: Developmental model of static allometry in holometabolous insects
results.author: A. Shingleton
results.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences
results.takeaway: The slope of nutritional static allometries in Drosophila melanogaster is controlled by the relative sensitivity of an organ's growth rate to changes in nutrition, and the relative duration of development when nutrition affects an organ's final size.

results.title: The worldwide allometric relationship in anatomical structures for plant roots
results.author: Yue Zhang
results.takeaway: Root allometry, where cortex thickness increases faster than stele radius with increasing root diameter, is common in plants and varies greatly across species, with implications for understanding plant ecology and physiology.

results.title: Single particle tracking-based reaction progress kinetic analysis reveals a series of molecular mechanisms of cetuximab-induced EGFR processes in a single living cell
results.author: Do-Hyeon Kim
results.takeaway: Using single particle tracking-based reaction progress kinetic analysis (sptRPKA), researchers identified a previously unknown intermediate state responsible for the selective targeting of cetuximab-induced EGFR endocytosis to cancer cells.

results.title: Streptomyces morphogenetics: dissecting differentiation in a filamentous bacterium
results.author: K. Flärdh
results.takeaway: Morphological differentiation in Streptomyces is closely integrated with growth, cell-cycle processes, and multicellular behavior, involving hormone-like extracellular signaling and diverse secondary metabolism.

results.title: Cellular Allometry of Mitochondrial Functionality Establishes the Optimal Cell Size
results.author: Teemu P. Miettinen
results.takeaway: Optimal cell size is determined by uncoupling mitochondrial content and functional scaling, resulting in maximized cellular fitness and proliferative capacity.

results.title: Growth polarity and cell division in Streptomyces.
results.author: K. Flärdh
results.takeaway: Streptomyces DivIVA protein and nucleoid migration contribute to bacterial growth polarity and cell division, leading to single-chromosome spores.

results.title: Bioelectric-calcineurin signaling module regulates allometric growth and size of the zebrafish fin
results.author: Jacob M. Daane
results.takeaway: The potassium channel kcnk5b plays a key role in regulating allometric growth and size of zebrafish fins, integrating calcineurin's growth effects and maintaining proper proportionality during development.

results.author: D. Ilse

results.title: A long noncoding RNA at the cortex locus controls adaptive coloration in butterflies
results.author: L. Livraghi

results.takeaway: A long noncoding RNA, cortex, plays a key role in adaptive diversification of wing patterns in butterflies.

results.title: Response of White Cabbage (Brassica oleracea var. capitata) to Single and Repeated Short-Term Waterlogging

results.title: Generation of Lens Progenitor Cells and Lentoid Bodies from Pluripotent Stem Cells: Novel Tools for Human Lens Development and Ocular Disease Etiology
results.author: A. Cvekl
results.takeaway: Advances in in vitro differentiation methods enable the generation of lens progenitor cells and micro-lenses, offering potential for studying cataractogenesis and ocular disease etiology.

results.title: Lens regeneration: scientific discoveries and clinical possibilities
results.author: Yuzhou Gu
results.takeaway: Lens regeneration has great potential for cataract treatment, restoring vision and avoiding postoperative complications, with potential for both in situ and in vitro methods.

results.title: Three-dimensional data capture and analysis of intact eye lenses evidences emmetropia-associated changes in epithelial cell organization
results.author: A. Kalligeraki
