results.title: In Vivo Imaging of Newt Lens Regeneration: Novel Insights Into the Regeneration Process
results.author: Weihao Chen
results.takeaway: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) is a valuable in vivo imaging modality for tracking and analyzing newt lens regeneration, potentially aiding in developing new therapies for blinding disorders in higher vertebrates.

results.title: In vivo imaging reveals exosome-mediated intercellular communication in lens development
results.author: Jingyu Ma
results.takeaway: Exosomes play a crucial role in lens development and play a role in intercellular communication, with their biogenesis regulated by the Syntenin-a pathway.

results.title: Conservation of fibroblast growth factor function in lens regeneration.
results.author: K. Rio-Tsonis
results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
results.takeaway: FGF molecules play a key role in lens regeneration and development in urodele amphibians, suggesting their conservation in lens regeneration and development.

results.title: Secondary lens formation from the cornea following implantation of larval tissues between the inner and outer corneas of Xenopus laevis tadpoles.
results.author: J. G. Reeve
results.journal: Journal of embryology and experimental morphology
results.takeaway: Implantation of retina, pituitary, limb blastema, or limb bud in larval Xenopus laevis eyes leads to secondary lens formation, similar to stage-5 lens regenerates.

results.title: Intrinsic Lens Forming Potential of Mouse Lens Epithelial versus Newt Iris Pigment Epithelial Cells in Three-Dimensional Culture
results.author: Andrea Hoffmann
results.takeaway: Newt iris pigment epithelial cells show complete lens regeneration in three-dimensional culture, while mouse lens epithelial cells show incomplete lens formation, with bFGF supplementation beneficial for MLE aggregate-derived lens-like structures.

results.title: Teleost and elasmobranch eye lenses as a target for life-history stable isotope analyses
results.author: Katie Quaeck-Davies
results.takeaway: Fish eye lenses are potential biochemical data recorders for life-history stable isotope analyses, providing insights into diet and spatial ecology, but species-specific uncertainties in lens growth rates complicate interpretation.

results.title: Two is not necessarily better than one: a double lens in a pre-metamorphic adult axolotl (Ambystoma mexicanum)
results.author: Levi H Smith
results.takeaway: Advanced imaging in axolotl ophthalmology reveals two distinct lenses in an 8-year-old female, suggesting potential regenerative abnormalities in axolotls.

results.title: Experimental studies on the regeneration of the lens in the eye of anurans, urodeles and fishes†
results.author: L. Stone

results.title: Direct evidence for transformation of differentiated iris epithelial cells into lens cells.
results.author: T. Yamada
results.takeaway: In Wolffian lens regeneration, fully differentiated adult cells are transformed into another cell type, with lens-forming capacity extending to the ventral half of the iris epithelium.

results.title: In Vivo and in Vitro Experimental Analysis of Lens Regeneration in Larval Xenopus laevis
results.author: L. Bosco
results.takeaway: The interaction of corneal cells with the retina plays a crucial role in lens regeneration in larval Xenopus laevis, with no lens tissue formed when the cornea is cultured alone.

results.title: A Focus on the Optical Properties of the Regenerated Newt Lens
results.author: Sarah J. Wassmer
results.takeaway: Regenerated newt lenses have greater light transmission but reduced focal length and refractive index than their original lenses, but by 26 weeks, they have recovered enough optical parameters to allow functional vision.

results.title: Transformation of Iris into Lens in vitro and its Dependency on Neural Retina
results.author: T. Yamada
results.takeaway: In Wolffian lens regeneration, iris epithelial cells interact with the retina, facilitating lens formation, rather than instructing cells to produce lens.

results.title: Central role for the lens in cave fish eye degeneration.
results.author: Yoshiyuki Yamamoto
results.takeaway: Cave fish eye degeneration is linked to evolutionary changes in the lens' inductive signal, with surface fish lenses restoring optic tissues lost during cave fish evolution.

results.title: Deposited in DRO : 31 May 2018 Version of attached
results.author: Y. K.
results.takeaway: Our novel technique using SPIM imaging enables in vivo measurements of the eye lens refractive index, providing insights into the mechanisms involved in lens development and its associated optical properties.

results.title: Transcriptomic analysis of three annelid species: looking for markers of positional information
results.author: Sofia Platova
results.takeaway: Spatial gene expression in annelid species reveals conserved molecular systems involved in posterior growth and positional identity, with species-specific modifications affecting regeneration capacity.

results.title: Evolution and development of segmented body plan revealed by engrailed and wnt1 gene expression in the annelid Alitta virens
results.author: A. I. Kairov
results.takeaway: The gradual segment formation pattern in nereidids suggests that segmentation in bilaterians did not arise from a common ancestral mechanism.

results.title: Segment formation in Annelids: patterns, processes and evolution.
results.author: G. Balavoine
results.journal: The International journal of developmental biology
results.takeaway: Annelids exhibit remarkable evolvability in segmentation, with diverse mechanisms used to produce segments depending on species, developmental time, and life history processes.

results.title: Growth patterns during segmentation in the two polychaete annelids, Capitella sp. I and Hydroides elegans: comparisons at distinct life history stages
results.author: E. Seaver
results.takeaway: Larval segments in Capitella sp. I and Hydroides elegans originate from lateral regions of the body, while post-metamorphic segments in H. elegans originate from a classical posterior growth zone.

results.title: Developmental system drift in dorsoventral patterning is linked to transitions to autonomous development in Annelida
results.author: Allan M. Carrillo-Baltodano
results.takeaway: BMP plays an ancestral role in promoting dorsoventral development in Spiralia, but this signaling hierarchy is lost in annelids transitioning to autonomous development, potentially linking autonomous cell-fate specification to developmental system drift.

results.title: Segment number threshold determines juvenile onset of germline cluster expansion in Platynereis dumerilii
results.author: Emily Kuehn
results.journal: Journal of experimental zoology. Part B, Molecular and developmental evolution
results.takeaway: A segment number threshold determines the onset of germline cluster expansion in juvenile Platynereis dumerilii, with growth state playing a crucial role in this process.

results.title: Comparative transcriptomics in Syllidae (Annelida) indicates that posterior regeneration and regular growth are comparable, while anterior regeneration is a distinct process
results.author: R. P. Ribeiro
results.takeaway: Syllids show high posterior regeneration abilities, but anterior regeneration varies across species, with gene expression changes in both processes.

results.title: Cell Proliferation Indices in Regenerating Alitta virens (Annelida, Errantia)
results.author: A. Y. Shalaeva
results.takeaway: Regenerating annelids show a high cell cycle rate and large growth fraction, making this model valuable for studying coordinated cell cycle entry in response to injury.

results.title: The cellular 3D printer of a marine bristle worm—chaetogenesis in Platynereis dumerilii (Audouin & Milne Edwards, 1834) (Annelida)
results.author: Ekin Tilic
results.takeaway: Chaetogenesis in marine bristle worms, such as Platynereis dumerilii, serves as a cellular 3D-printer, shaping chaetae through modulating microvilli patterns and affecting their shape and pattern throughout their lifespan.

results.title: Size and shape: the developmental regulation of static allometry in insects
results.author: A. Shingleton
results.takeaway: Recent advances in growth regulation and endocrinology suggest that insulin/IGF signaling may play a central role in regulating organismal shape and size in insects.

results.title: Early embryogenesis and organogenesis in the annelid Owenia fusiformis
results.author: Allan M. Carrillo-Baltodano
results.takeaway: Owenia fusiformis embryogenesis reveals that equal spiral cleavage leads to a coeloblastula, gastrulation via invagination, and a feeding trochophore-like larva, similar to other equal spiral cleaving annelids.

results.title: Developmental and molecular biology of annelid regeneration: a comparative review of recent studies.
results.author: B. Özpolat
results.takeaway: Recent studies reveal conserved and variable features in annelid regeneration, offering insights into the developmental basis and evolution of this process.

results.title: Cellular and Molecular Mechanisms of Segmentation in Annelida An Open Question
results.author: E. Zattara
results.takeaway: This paper explores the cellular and molecular mechanisms of segmentation in annelids, highlighting the need for further research to fully understand this process.

results.title: Growth and size control during development
results.author: Jannik Vollmer
results.takeaway: Organ size in organisms is controlled by their genotype, with related species able to produce organs of different sizes due to environmental factors.

results.title: Segmentation in Annelids: Cellular and Molecular Basis for Metameric Body Plan
results.author: Takashi Shimizu
results.takeaway: Annelid segmentation involves autonomous cell-autonomous properties, cellular differentiation, and genealogical position, with clitellate segmentation involving two stages and polychaetes showing distinct segmentation mechanisms.

results.title: Game over: Conflict resolution through strategic growth in an invertebrate
results.author: P. Radhakrishnan
results.takeaway: Strategic growth in marine annelid worms can mitigate reproductive conflict and establish size hierarchies, with the onset of reproduction weakening or stabilizing these differences depending on the social environment.

results.title: The developmental basis for allometry in insects.
results.author: David L. Stern
results.takeaway: Insects' organ sizes are determined based on total body size through autonomous growth, centralized measurement, and feedback between growing organs.

results.title: Establishing a new methodology for annelid studies: a biometric study of the ragworm Hediste diversicolor (Müller, 1776)
results.author: João Almeida
results.takeaway: The study proposes a new biometric methodology for annelids, using the number of chaetiger segments as an indicator of growth, to better understand the growth and evolution of individual structures in the ragworm Hediste diversicolor.

results.title: Allometry of cell types in planarians by single-cell transcriptomics
results.author: Elena Emili
results.takeaway: Planarians of different sizes consist of the same basic cell types but in varying proportions, with gut basal cells being the most responsive to size changes, suggesting a role in energy storage.

results.title: Cell lineage and cell cycling analyses of the 4d micromere using live imaging in the marine annelid Platynereis dumerilii
results.author: Duygu Özpolat
results.takeaway: Live imaging of marine embryos reveals the intricate relationship between cell lineage, cell cycle, and cell fate, with implications for evolutionary studies and stem cell research.

results.author: R. Lindley
results.takeaway: Lamarckian inheritance of somatically acquired adaptations involves stable, DNA-integrated inheritance, requiring specific population dynamics and sustained environmental stimuli for consolidation.

results.title: Lamarckism and epigenetic inheritance: a clarification
results.author: Laurent Loison
results.takeaway: Lamarckism and epigenetic inheritance are distinct concepts, with epigenetic mechanisms evolving as products of natural selection, and inheritance of acquired characters being an emergent feature of evolution.

results.title: Weismann’s three critiques to the inheritance of the acquired characters
results.author: Íñigo Ongay de Felipe
results.takeaway: Weismann's critique of soft inheritance is complex and multifaceted, and while his arguments are not conclusive, they do not refute the Lamarckian theory of inheritance.

results.title: Evolution in four dimensions: Genetic, epigenetic, behavioral, and symbolic variation in the history of life
results.author: M. Benton

results.title: Heredity determined by the environment: Lamarckian ideas in modern molecular biology.
results.author: O. N. Tikhodeyev

Certain experiments demonstrate the transmission of acquired characters to offspring; and 3. The principle can be inferred from other facts, independent of experiment results.

results.title: Lamarck, Evolution, and the Inheritance of Acquired Characters
results.author: R. W. Burkhardt

results.takeaway: The debate over the inheritance of acquired characters, known as Lamarckism, has raged for over a century and a half, with new experiments rekindling the controversy.

results.title: The Inheritance of Acquired Characters
results.author: M. Hartog

results.author: Y.-S. Liu

results.title: Let's Stop the Sloppy Use of “Lamarckian”

results.author: Lisa Tilokani

results.title: Cellular and molecular mechanisms of coronary artery spasm: lessons from animal models.

results.title: Molecular control of animal cell cytokinesis

results.author: Xingpeng Di

results.title: Molecular mechanisms and consequences of mitochondrial permeability transition
results.author: M. Bonora

results.title: Evolution of cellular stress response mechanisms.

results.takeaway: Cellular stress response (CSR) mechanisms have evolved across various life domains, with core features preserved and core elements varying in various organisms.

results.author: Junqiang Liu

results.title: The molecular mechanisms mediating mammalian fertilization

results.title: Mammalian sex determination: a molecular drama.

results.title: Body size predicts the rate of contemporary morphological change in birds

results.takeaway: Smaller bird species experience faster declines in body size and faster increases in wing length, indicating that body size is an important predictor of morphological change rates in birds.

results.title: Genome Size Covaries More Positively with Propagule Size than Adult Size: New Insights into an Old Problem

results.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Persistence in Protozoan Parasites

results.title: ‘The glideosome’: a dynamic complex powering gliding motion and host cell invasion by Toxoplasma gondii
results.author: C. Opitz
results.takeaway: The glideosome complex, composed of motor proteins and F-actin, plays a crucial role in Toxoplasma gondii's gliding motility and host cell invasion.

results.title: Graviresponses of certain ciliates and flagellates
results.author: R. Hemmersbach
results.takeaway: Gravity perception in protists can be mediated by distinct stato-organelles or density differences between the cytoplasm and extracellular medium, with no visible adaptation phenomena during hypergravity or microgravity exposure.

results.title: Intracellular Ca2+ Signaling in Protozoan Parasites: An Overview with a Focus on Mitochondria
results.author: Pedro Scarpelli
results.takeaway: Protozoan parasites, like nematodes and worms, exhibit a Ca2+ signaling toolkit similar to higher eukaryotes, with mitochondria playing a key role in Ca-dependent signaling events.

results.title: Inhibition of apoptosis by intracellular protozoan parasites.
results.author: V. Heussler
results.takeaway: Intracellular protozoan parasites, such as Toxoplasma gondii and Trypanosoma cruzi, can inhibit host cell apoptosis through heat shock proteins and NF-kappaB activation.

results.title: Exogenous lipid vesicles induce endocytosis-mediated cellular aggregation in a close unicellular relative of animals
results.author: Ria Q. Kidner

results.title: Protozoan predation as a driver of diversity and virulence in bacterial biofilms.
results.author: M. Hoque
results.takeaway: Protozoan predation on bacterial biofilms drives diversity and virulence, with biofilm formation enhancing resistance and causing trade-offs in virulence in other eukaryotes.

results.title: Different Drugs, Same End: Ultrastructural Hallmarks of Autophagy in Pathogenic Protozoa
results.author: Yasmin Pedra-Rezende
results.takeaway: Ultrastructural analysis reveals that several antiparasitic compounds induce similar autophagic phenotypes in protozoan parasites, suggesting potential for successful chemotherapy.

results.title: Endocytosis in anaerobic parasitic protists
results.author: Marlene Benchimol
results.takeaway: Endocytosis is crucial for survival and reproduction in anaerobic protists, with PI-3 kinase, Rab, and Rho molecular complexes playing key roles in this process.

results.title: How to get away with murder: The multiple strategies employed by pathogenic protozoa to avoid complement killing.
results.author: Laura Valéria Rios-Barros
results.takeaway: Pathogenic protozoa develop various strategies to avoid complement activation, evading host immune defenses and causing diseases like malaria, toxoplasmosis, and Chagas disease.

results.title: Who Needs a Contractile Actomyosin Ring? The Plethora of Alternative Ways to Divide a Protozoan Parasite
results.author: T. Hammarton

results.takeaway: Parasites employ diverse cell division mechanisms, offering potential new treatment avenues for protozoal diseases.

results.title: Oxygen Sensing by Protozoans: How They Catch Their Breath
results.author: C. West
results.takeaway: Prolyl 4-hydroxylases (P4Hs) are emerging as universal oxygen sensors, affecting both animals and protozoa, contributing to the regulation of unicellular eukaryotes in diverse oxygen environments.

results.title: ATPe Dynamics in Protozoan Parasites. Adapt or Perish
results.author: N. Lauri
results.takeaway: Protozoan parasites alter ATPe dynamics in host cells, potentially promoting infection and systemic responses that benefit or harm the parasite.

results.title: Inhibition of Cell Apoptosis by Apicomplexan Protozoa–Host Interaction in the Early Stage of Infection
results.author: Liyin Lian
results.journal: Animals : an Open Access Journal from MDPI

results.title: Intestinal immune responses to commensal and pathogenic protozoa
results.author: Aline Sardinha-Silva
results.takeaway: Intestinal protozoa regulate intestinal immunity through various cell types and immune mediators, potentially impacting host tolerance, protection, and pathogenesis.

results.title: Protozoan predation enhances stress resistance and antibiotic tolerance in Burkholderia cenocepacia by triggering the SOS response
results.author: Álvaro Morón

results.title: Biogenesis of extracellular vesicles in protozoan parasites: The ESCRT complex in the trafficking fast lane?
results.author: Abel Cruz Camacho
results.takeaway: The ESCRT complex plays a key role in the biogenesis of extracellular vesicles in human parasitic protozoa, offering potential for medical insight and therapeutic intervention.

results.title: Invasion and egress cascade in intracellular protozoa: Part 1
results.takeaway: Intracellular protozoa use complex strategies for invasion and egress, which are key factors in infection, pathogenesis, and transmission, and could be potential drug targets.

results.title: Molecular and Cellular Mechanisms Involved in the Trypanosoma cruzi/Host Cell Interplay
results.author: P. S. Romano
results.takeaway: T. cruzi invasion in nonphagocytic cells is facilitated by the upregulation of autophagy during starvation, resulting in increased parasite colonization.

results.title: Unique Endomembrane Systems and Virulence in Pathogenic Protozoa
results.author: M. F. Wiser
results.takeaway: Pathogenic protozoa, particularly apicomplexans, exhibit unique endomembrane systems that contribute to their virulence through secretory processes and host cell modification.

results.author: T. Yamada

results.journal: Cell differentiation and development : the official journal of the International Society of Developmental Biologists

results.author: S. Karasaki
results.takeaway: The adult newt Triturus viridescens undergoes a complex regenerative tissue transformation from iris epithelium to lens, involving changes in cell morphology and cellular processes.

results.title: Diverse Evolutionary Origins and Mechanisms of Lens Regeneration.
results.author: J. J. Henry
results.takeaway: Different forms of vertebrate lens regeneration evolved independently and utilize diverse molecular mechanisms, suggesting no conserved or convergent mechanisms for regulation.

results.title: Direct evidence for transformation of differentiated iris epithelial cells into lens cells.
results.author: T. Yamada
results.takeaway: In Wolffian lens regeneration, fully differentiated adult cells are transformed into another cell type, with lens-forming capacity extending to the ventral half of the iris epithelium.

results.title: Activation of ribosomal RNA synthesis in initiation of Wolffian lens regeneration.
results.author: D. Reese
results.takeaway: Lens removal in adult newts activates ribosomal RNA synthesis, which is the earliest event in lens regeneration, preceding DNA replication, cell replication, and dedifferentiation.

results.title: A study of DNA synthesis during the transformation of the Iris into lens in the lentectomized newt
results.author: S. Eisenberg
results.takeaway: DNA synthesis is necessary but not sufficient for the transformation of iris cells into lens cells in adult newts.

results.title: Control of mitotic activity in Wolffian lens regenerration.
results.author: T. Yamada
results.takeaway: Lens regeneration in adult newts involves a wave of mitoses in the iris epithelium, which subsides after lens formation and is maintained in the regenerated lens epithelium.

results.title: Influence of the pituitary on Wolffian lens regeneration.
results.author: T. G. Connelly
results.takeaway: Removal of the pituitary 3 days before lentectomy retards Wolffian lens regeneration in adult newts, but hypophysectomy 5 or 10 days after lentectomy does not alter regeneration progress.

results.title: LENS ANTIGENS IN A LENS-REGENERATING SYSTEM STUDIED BY THE IMMUNOFLUORESCENT TECHNIQUE.
results.author: C. Takata
results.takeaway: Lens antigens are present in the cytoplasm of lens fiber cells during Wolffian lens regeneration in adult Triturus viridescens, with all lens epithelium cells showing positive cytoplasm at stage X.

results.title: The role of a normal lens in Wolffian lens regeneration.
results.author: L. Williams
results.takeaway: Contact between the normal lens and iris may prevent lens regeneration, with larval retina showing a greater response than adult retina.

results.title: L.S. stone: lens regeneration--contributions to the establishment of an in vivo model of transdifferentiation.
results.author: J. Papaconstantinou
results.journal: Journal of experimental zoology. Part A, Comparative experimental biology
results.takeaway: L.S. Stone's papers from the late 1930s to the late 1960s significantly contributed to our understanding of lens regeneration in amphibians, establishing an in vivo model of tissue transdifferentiation.

results.title: Alteration of nucleolar ultrastructure in iris epithelial cells during initiation of Wolffian lens regeneration.
results.author: J. Dumont

results.title: Activation of DNA replication in the iris epithelium by lens removal.
results.author: T. Yamada

results.title: Analysis of a unique molecule responsible for regeneration and stabilization of differentiated state of tissue cells.
results.author: Yutaka Imokawa

results.title: Macrophages modulate fibrosis during newt lens regeneration
results.author: Georgios Tsissios
results.takeaway: Macrophages play a crucial role in newt lens regeneration by regulating fibrosis, modulating inflammation, and maintaining a proper balance of early proliferation and late apoptosis in iris pigment epithelial cells.

results.title: Lens regeneration from the cornea requires suppression of Wnt/β-catenin signaling

results.title: The Development, Growth, and Regeneration of the Crystalline Lens: A Review

results.title: Cellular and Molecular Triggers of Retinal Regeneration in Amphibians

results.title: Unravelling the limb regeneration mechanisms of Polypedates maculatus, a sub-tropical frog, by transcriptomics

results.title: Plasticity and reprogramming of differentiated cells in amphibian regeneration

results.journal: American Association for the Advancement of Science

results.title: Advances in signaling in vertebrate regeneration as a prelude to regenerative medicine.
results.author: Cristi L. Stoick-Cooper

results.title: The control of cuticular melanin and lutein incorporation in the morphological colour adaptation of a nymphalid pupa, Inachis io L.
results.author: A. Maisch
results.takeaway: Inachis io pupae's pigmentation varies between yellow and black, with a factor from the anterior part of the body reducing melanization and enhancing lutein content in light-background conditions.

results.title: Integrated Analysis of Transcriptome and Proteome to Reveal Pupal Color Switch in Papilio xuthus Butterflies
results.author: Jinwu He
results.takeaway: Pupal color in swallowtail butterflies is regulated by genes involved in black, blue, and yellow pigments, with no clear hormone involved in pupal development.

results.title: Pigments in the pupal integuments of two colour types of cabbage white butterfly, Pieris rapae crucivora
results.author: T. Ohtaki
results.takeaway: Cabbage white butterfly pupae can be green or greyish brown depending on light conditions, with green color due to yellow cuticle and bluish green epidermis, and brown color due to black spots and reddish-brown pigment in the epidermis.

results.title: Tyrosine Hydroxylase and DOPA Decarboxylase Are Associated With Pupal Melanization During Larval–Pupal Transformation in Antheraea pernyi
results.author: Qi Wang
results.takeaway: Tyrosine hydroxylase and DOPA decarboxylase are key genes associated with pupal melanization during larval-pupal transformation in Antheraea pernyi silkworms, setting the molecular basis for artificial control of pupal melanization.

results.title: Die rolle der Carotinoide und des Gallenfarbstoffs bei der Farbmodifikation der Puppen von Pieris brassicae
results.author: H. Kayser
results.takeaway: Pieris brassicae pupae's bile pigment content is related to melanization, with blue light enhancing it, but the negative correlation between melanization and bile pigment remains.

results.title: Pupal colour plasticity in the butterfly Catopsilia pomona (Lepidoptera: Pieridae)
results.author: Tarunkishwor Yumnam
results.journal: Biological Journal of the Linnean Society
results.takeaway: Pupal color plasticity in the butterfly Catopsilia pomona helps pupae match their substrate colors, with leaf-borne pupae tending to be greener and off-leaf pupae browner, influenced by leaf position, midrib thickness, and leaf length.

results.title: CRISPR/Cas9‐mediated ebony knockout results in puparium melanism in Spodoptera litura
results.author: Honglun Bi
results.takeaway: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated ebony knockout in Spodoptera litura leads to puparium melanism, demonstrating the crucial role of ebony in insect pigmentation and providing a useful marker gene for functional studies in lepidopteran pests.

results.title: Thermobiological effects of temperature‐induced color variations in Aglais urticae (Lepidoptera, Nymphalidae)
results.author: G. Markl
results.takeaway: Temperature-induced color variations in adult butterflies provide thermobiological benefits, with lower temperatures leading to darker coloration and higher temperatures leading to lighter individuals.

results.title: Induced Changes in the Pigmentation of the Pupoe of the Butterfly Pieris Napi L., and their Inheritance
results.author: J. Harrison
results.journal: Proceedings of The Royal Society B: Biological Sciences
results.takeaway: Exposure to orange light before pupation in Pieris Napi L. butterfly larvae leads to inherited green pupal pigmentation, affecting the appearance of the chrysalids.

results.title: Pigment composition in the pupal cuticles of two colour types of the swallowtails, Papilio xuthus L. and P. protenor demetrius Cramer
results.author: E. Ohnishi
results.takeaway: The pigment composition of swallowtail pupal cuticles reveals that environmental stimuli determine green and brown pupal colors, with papilioerythrins playing a role in determining these colors.

results.title: Aspartate Decarboxylase is Required for a Normal Pupa Pigmentation Pattern in the Silkworm, Bombyx mori
results.author: F. Dai
results.takeaway: Aspartate decarboxylase (BmADC) plays a crucial role in melanin metabolism and pupal pigmentation in silkworms, Bombyx mori.

results.title: Untangling the structural and molecular mechanisms underlying colour and rapid colour change in a lizard, Agama atra
results.author: M. Nicolaï
results.takeaway: Melanin, iridophores, and pteridines are the main color-producing mechanisms in Agama atra lizards, with rapid color change achieved through melanin dispersal and iridophore organization.

results.title: The Pupal Pigmentation Pattern and Pupal Development in the Species of Aphytis Howard (Hymenoptera: Aphelinidae)
results.author: Zhuhong Wang
results.takeaway: Pupal pigmentation can help identify species of Aphytis Howard, as it can show yellow, dark brown, or black pupae, with some cryptic species showing distinct pigmentation patterns.

results.title: The proximate control of pupal color in swallowtail butterflies: implications for the evolution of environmentally cued pupal color in butterflies (Lepidoptera: Papilionidae).
results.author: Mattia Jones
results.takeaway: The control of pupal color by PMRF has evolved independently in the swallowtail and nymphalid-pierid lineages, with green pupal color potentially evolving through facultative inhibition of PMRF release.

results.title: Color preference for pupation sites of the butterfly larvaeInachis io and the significance of the pupal melanization reducing factor
results.author: G. Starnecker
results.takeaway: Butterfly larvae Inachis io can adapt to various light and dark background colors, with a preference for certain colors, and the pupal melanization reducing factor plays a role in this adaptation process.

results.title: Involvement of Cyclic Adenosine Monophosphate in the Regulation of Pupal Color Adaptation of the Butterfly, Inachis io
results.author: G. Starnecker
results.takeaway: Increased intracellular cAMP levels mediate the PMRF effect in butterfly pupal color adaptation, resulting in yellow pupae on bright backgrounds.

results.title: The biology of color
results.author: I. Cuthill
results.takeaway: Advances in color biology are revolutionizing our understanding of animal coloration and its role in social signaling, defense, thermoregulation, and protection.

results.title: Different transcriptional responses to developmental versus short-term acclimation temperatures in Pieris rapae
results.author: Samantha L. Sturiale

results.title: Time- and temperature-dependent dynamics of prothoracicotropic hormone and ecdysone sensitivity co-regulate pupal diapause in the green-veined white butterfly Pieris napi.
results.author: Philip Süess
results.takeaway: In the green-veined white butterfly Pieris napi, pupal diapause is regulated by PTTH secretion and ecdysone sensitivity, with ecdysone sensitivity decreasing during diapause and returning during diapause termination at low temperatures.

results.title: Effects of the temperature on the development of Pieris brassicae L
results.author: O. Querci
results.journal: The Entomologist's Record and Journal of Variation

results.title: Exposure to elevated temperature during development affects eclosion and morphology in the temperate Pieris napi butterfly (Lepidoptera: Pieridae).
results.author: Z. Moradinour
results.takeaway: Exposure to 32°C during pupal stage increases mortality and decreases time to eclosion in the butterfly Pieris napi, leading to smaller and shorter body and sensory organs.

results.title: Degrees of freedom: temperature's influence on developmental rate.
results.author: Jess J Bourn
results.takeaway: Temperature influences developmental rate, affecting cell sensitivity and embryogenesis' robustness to environmental influences.

results.title: Thermal plasticity of growth and development varies adaptively among alternative developmental pathways
results.author: S. M. Kivelä
results.takeaway: In the butterfly Pieris napi, thermal reaction norms vary adaptively among alternative developmental pathways, driven by environmental factors, with direct development showing higher development and growth rates.

results.title: Molecular characterization of three Hsp90 from Pieris and expression patterns in response to cold and thermal stress in summer and winter diapause of Pieris melete
results.author: Yue-Kun Wu
results.takeaway: Hsp90 plays an important role in responding to heat/cold stress both in summer and winter diapause in Pieris melete pupae.

results.title: Thermal performance under constant temperatures can accurately predict insect development times across naturally variable microclimates.
results.author: Loke von Schmalensee
results.takeaway: Insect development rates can be accurately predicted across variable microclimates using constant laboratory temperatures, suggesting they are generally unaffected by thermal fluctuations.

results.title: Optimal Low Temperature and Chilling Period for Both Summer and Winter Diapause Development in Pieris melete: Based on a Similar Mechanism
results.author: Haijun Xiao
results.takeaway: Optimal chilling temperatures for diapause development in Pieris melete cabbage butterfly pupae are between 1 and 10°C, with a 50-60-day duration, resulting in shorter diapause durations.

results.title: Embryonic canalization and its limits-A view from temperature.
results.author: S. Irvine
results.journal: Journal of experimental zoology. Part B, Molecular and developmental evolution
results.takeaway: Embryonic canalization allows animals to produce stable offspring under varying conditions, but high temperatures can disrupt development, highlighting the need for targeted selection under climate change.

results.title: Timing of diapause termination in relation to variation in winter climate
results.author: Philipp Lehmann
results.takeaway: Diapause termination in the pupal diapausing butterfly Pieris napi occurs at a thermal optimum between 2 and 4°C, with trade-offs between time and temperature at the low and high ends of the thermal range.

results.title: Expression of alternative developmental pathways in the cabbage butterfly, Pieris melete and their differences in life history traits
results.author: Jian-Jun Tang
results.takeaway: The cabbage butterfly's developmental pathways are influenced by temperature, day length, and seasonality, allowing it to synchronize with host plant growth seasons and protect against unpredictable risks in a dynamic environment.

results.title: The Effects of Temperature on Cellular Physiology.
results.author: Benjamin D. Knapp
results.takeaway: Temperature impacts biological systems across all length and timescales, affecting protein folding, molecular composition, and volume expansion, with global warming potentially disrupting thermal homeostasis in microbes important for human and planetary health.

results.title: Two transcriptionally distinct pathways drive female development in a reptile with both genetic and temperature dependent sex determination
results.author: S. Whiteley
results.takeaway: Temperature determines sex in Pogona vitticeps reptiles, with early developmental cascades differing between genetically driven and thermally driven females, and genes playing a role in temperature sex reversal.

results.title: An autoregulatory negative feedback loop controls thermomorphogenesis in Arabidopsis
results.author: Sanghwa Lee
results.takeaway: PIF4-HEC forms an autoregulatory negative feedback loop that controls growth genes to modulate thermomorphogenesis in Arabidopsis plants.

results.title: A comparison of low temperature biology of Pieris rapae from Ontario, Canada, and Yakutia, Far Eastern Russia.
results.author: Natalia G. Li
results.journal: Comparative biochemistry and physiology. Part A, Molecular & integrative physiology
results.takeaway: Pieris rapae pupae can be freeze-tolerant or freeze-avoidant, with physiological plasticity playing a key role in surviving extreme low temperatures.

results.title: Integrative phenotyping analyses reveal the relevance of the phyB-PIF4 pathway in Arabidopsis thaliana reproductive organs at high ambient temperature
results.author: Shekoufeh Ebrahimi Naghani
results.takeaway: The phyB-PIF4 pathway plays a crucial role in relaying temperature signals throughout plant development, including reproductive stages, potentially impacting fertilization rates.

results.title: Morphological and Molecular Responses of Lateolabrax maculatus Skeletal Muscle Cells to Different Temperatures
results.author: Jingru Zhang
results.takeaway: Higher temperatures accelerate muscle cell proliferation, differentiation, and migration in Lateolabrax maculatus fish, while lower temperatures promote DNA damage and apoptosis.

results.title: Elevated temperature fatally disrupts nuclear divisions in the early Drosophila embryo
results.author: Girish R. Kale
results.takeaway: Elevated temperature disrupts early Drosophila embryo development, leading to developmental defects and increased lethality, and rescuing these defects could potentially improve insect survival in exposed populations.

results.title: Direct Control of SPEECHLESS by PIF4 in the High-Temperature Response of Stomatal Development
results.author: O. Lau
results.takeaway: Elevated temperatures suppress the expression of SPCH, the master regulator of stomatal development, mediated by the environmental signaling factor PIF4, limiting stomatal production in plants.

results.title: Tyrosinase and related proteins in mammalian pigmentation

results.title: MAMMALIAN TYROSINASE AND DOPA OXIDASE

results.author: M. Jiménez

results.author: V. Hearing

results.title: Mammalian tyrosinase; preparation and properties.

results.takeaway: Mammalian tyrosinase, an enzyme that catalyzes melanin production, has been confirmed to exist and is involved in the conversion of tyrosine to melanin in mammals.

results.title: Natural tyrosinase enzyme inhibitors: A path from melanin to melanoma and its reported pharmacological activities.
results.author: R. Logesh

results.title: Reactivities of Quinone Methides versus o-Quinones in Catecholamine Metabolism and Eumelanin Biosynthesis
results.author: M. Sugumaran
results.takeaway: Quinone methides play a key role in catecholamine metabolism and eumelanin biosynthesis, highlighting their importance during the melanogenic process.

results.title: Inhibition of Tyrosinase and Melanogenesis by Carboxylic Acids: Mechanistic Insights and Safety Evaluation
results.author: Yupei Chen

results.title: The role of peroxidase vs. the role of tyrosinase in enzymatic conversion of tyrosine to melanin in melanocytes, mast cells and eosinophils.

results.title: Tyrosinase autoactivation and the chemistry of ortho-quinone amines.

results.author: A. Hering

results.author: Senyue Liu

results.title: Fish pigmentation and coloration: Molecular mechanisms and aquaculture perspectives

results.title: Pigmentation and colour changing mechanism in fishes

results.takeaway: Fish color their skin through species-specific interactions among pigment cell types, influenced by direct cell contact and tissue environment cues.

results.title: Spectral tuning by opsin coexpression in retinal regions that view different parts of the visual field
results.author: Brian E. Dalton

results.title: Color opponency with a single kind of bistable opsin in the zebrafish pineal organ

results.title: Skin Colour in Salamanders Is Modulated by Both Epitranscriptomic Methylation and Gene Expression
results.author: Nicholas Strowbridge

results.title: Cellular and Molecular Basis of Environment-Induced Color Change in a Tree Frog
results.author: Runliang Zhai

results.takeaway: Morphological color change (MCC) driven by chromatophore proliferation is a key mechanism of background adaptation in tree frogs, offering insights into amphibian color adaptation and environmental adaptation in other vertebrates.

results.title: Xenopus as a model system for studying pigmentation and pigmentary disorders
results.author: Joudi El Mir
results.takeaway: Xenopus is a unique model system for studying pigmentation and pigmentary disorders, providing a more comprehensive understanding of the molecular basis of these disorders compared to mouse and zebrafish.

results.title: Leukocyte Tyrosine Kinase (Ltk) Is the Mendelian Determinant of the Axolotl Melanoid Color Variant
results.author: Mirindi Kabangu
results.takeaway: The melanoid color variation in axolotls is influenced by the Leukocyte Tyrosine Kinase (Ltk) gene, supporting the single-origin hypothesis of pigment cell development.

results.title: Albinism in the largest extant amphibian: A metabolic, endocrine, or immune problem?
results.author: L. Chang

results.title: Biochemical regulation of pigment motility in vertebrate chromatophores: a review of physiological color change mechanisms
results.author: Russell A. Ligon

results.title: On the Development of Pigment Patterns in Amphibians
results.author: J. T. Bagnara

results.title: The Embryology of Vertebrate Pigment Cells. Part I. Amphibia
results.author: G. Dushane
results.takeaway: The pigment cells in amphibians and birds are specialized highly-branched cells packed with pigment granules, and their migration and dependence on extrinsic factors contribute to their color patterns.

results.title: Expression patterns of melanin‐related genes are linked to crypsis and conspicuousness in a pumpkin toadlet
results.author: Juliane P. C. Monteiro
results.takeaway: Pumpkin toadlets' skin color varies from cryptic green to conspicuous orange, with melanin-related genes playing a key role in cryptic coloration and predator detection.

results.title: Pigment cell distribution in a rapid colour changing amphibian (Litoria wilcoxii)
results.author: Christina Kindermann
results.takeaway: Rapid color change in male stony creek frogs (Litoria wilcoxii) occurs through pigment aggregation and dispersion within melanophores, with significant variation in pigment cell distribution between color-changing and non-color-changing tissues.

results.title: Rapid color change in fish and amphibians – function, regulation, and emerging applications
results.author: Helen Nilsson Sköld
results.takeaway: Fish and amphibians exhibit rapid color change for background matching, thermoregulation, and signaling, with external factors playing a key role in regulating this process.

results.title: Intercellular Relations in the Development of Amphibian Pigmentation
results.author: V. Twitty
results.takeaway: Intercellular relations play a crucial role in the development of amphibian pigmentation, affecting migration and pigment synthesis.

results.title: Nerve stimulation and the movement of melanin granules in the pigment cells of the frog's web.
results.author: R. Snell
results.takeaway: The movement of melanin granules within amphibian pigment cells is influenced by hormones, skin moisture, and temperature, with pituitary secretions playing a significant role in regulation.

results.title: Blue, Black, and Stripes: Evolution and Development of Color Production and Pattern Formation in Lizards and Snakes
results.author: Takeo Kuriyama
results.takeaway: Lizards and snakes' color patterns are influenced by pigment cells and genetic factors during embryogenesis, improving our understanding of reptilian color pattern evolution.

results.title: Editorial: Evo-Devo of Color Pattern Formation
results.author: R. Mallarino
results.takeaway: Advances in genomic, molecular, and imaging approaches reveal the mechanistic basis of color pattern formation in animal species, providing insights into evolutionary developmental biology and phenotypic diversity.

results.title: Adaptive colouration in amphibians.
results.author: Andreas Rudh
results.takeaway: Adaptive coloration in amphibians plays a role in thermoregulation, UV protection, predator avoidance, and sexual signaling, but many functions remain unexplored and few genes influencing pigmentation or patterning have been identified.

results.title: Comparative Transcriptome analyses of the molecular mechanisms underlying skin color variations in ocellaris clownfish Amphiprion ocellaris (Cuvier, 1830)
results.author: Jing Hu
results.takeaway: This study reveals the molecular basis of skin color variations in clownfish, offering potential for breed improvement in aquaculture.

results.title: Colour Confusion: Reviewing Ambiguities in the Identification and Classification of Chromatophore Deficiencies Among Amphibians
results.author: John Gould
results.takeaway: This review clarifies terminology and establishes standards for identifying and classifying color abnormalities in amphibians, addressing ambiguity and confusion in the literature.

results.title:
Analysis of the correlation between phenotypic color differences and molecular regulation of
 Amphiprion percula
 and
 A. ocellaris
results.author: Jing Hu
results.takeaway: The genetic and cellular mechanisms underlying skin color variation in clownfish are revealed, providing valuable insights for ornamental fish breeding and genetic improvement.

results.title: Pigments, Chromatophore Structure, and Gene Expression Underlying Colour Polytypy of a Panamanian Poison Frog
results.author: Vasiliki Mantzana-Oikonomaki
results.takeaway: Red frogs show distinct pigments, chromatophore structure, and gene expression, while aquamarine, brown, and green frogs share overlapping pigment profiles and chromatophore organization, with transcriptional differences suggesting structural or regulatory mechanisms.

results.title: Evolution of viviparity in cold-climate lizards: testing the maternal manipulation hypothesis

results.title: Gestation temperature affects sexual phenotype, morphology, locomotor performance, and growth of neonatal brown forest skinks, Sphenomorphus indicus
results.author: X. Ji

results.author: G. Brusch

results.title: Sex‐specific variation in thermal sensitivity has multiple negative effects on reproductive trait performance

results.title: Influence of pregnancy on the thermal biology of the lizard, Sceloporus jarrovi: why do pregnant females exhibit low body temperatures?
results.author: T. Mathies
results.takeaway: Pregnant female lizards maintain relatively low body temperatures without compromising their physical condition, likely to avoid decrements in offspring fitness.

results.title: The cooler the better? Indirect effect of spring-summer temperature on fecundity in a capital breeder
results.author: L. Corlatti
results.takeaway: Higher spring-summer temperatures negatively impact female deer fecundity through decreased kidney fat index, suggesting a potential trade-off between reproduction and survival in ungulate populations.

results.title: Menstrual Cycle Temperature Dynamics and Their Association With Conception: A Within- and Between-Person Analysis
results.author: Orsolya Kiss
results.takeaway: Menstrual temperature rhythms, both in amplitude and timing, can predict conception likelihood, with higher amplitude and timing being more beneficial in shorter cycles and optimally aligning with the fertile window in typical length cycles.

results.title: Breeding phenology drives variation in reproductive output, reproductive costs and offspring fitness in a viviparous ectotherm.
results.author: Théo Bodineau
results.takeaway: Early parturition dates in reptiles positively impact offspring survival, growth, and recruitment, but may compromise gravid females' energetic condition.

results.title: Temperature effects during gestation in a viviparous lizard
results.author: C. Beuchat
results.takeaway: Pregnant females allowed to thermoregulate during gestation have larger offspring and better survival rates than those kept at constant temperatures, while adult lizards at higher temperatures lose weight.

results.title: Age-Dependent and Seasonal Changes in Menstrual Cycle Length and Body Temperature Based on Big Data
results.author: T. Tatsumi
results.takeaway: Age-dependent and seasonal changes in menstrual cycle length and basal body temperature contribute to a better understanding of female reproductive health in the modern world.

results.title: Assessing Pregnancy's Influence on Rectal and Corneal Temperature in Female Cats
results.author: Candemir Ozcan
results.takeaway: Pregnancy status significantly affects rectal temperature in female cats, but not corneal temperature, but rectal temperature may not be a reliable clinical indicator of pregnancy in cats.

results.title: Associations between high temperatures in pregnancy and risk of preterm birth, low birth weight, and stillbirths: systematic review and meta-analysis
results.author: M. Chersich
results.takeaway: High temperatures in pregnancy are associated with increased risks of preterm birth, low birth weight, and stillbirths, with larger risks in low and middle income countries.

results.title: Evolution of viviparity in warm‐climate lizards: an experimental test of the maternal manipulation hypothesis
results.author: X. Ji
results.takeaway: Gravid females in warm-climate lizards adjust thermoregulation during pregnancy to provide optimal thermal conditions for developing embryos, potentially enhancing offspring fitness.

results.title: Associations of ambient temperature exposure with embryonic and early fetal development
results.author: E. Essers

results.title: Skin temperature and reproductive condition in wild female chimpanzees
results.author: G. Dezecache

results.title: Using the product threshold model for estimating separately the effect of temperature on male and female fertility.
results.author: L. Tusell

results.author: Jingru Zhang

results.title: Insights into molecular pathways and fatty acid membrane composition during the temperature stress response in the murine C2C12 cell model.
results.author: Marua Abu Risha

results.title: Heat stress inhibits the proliferation and differentiation of myoblasts and is associated with damage to mitochondria
results.author: Jiawei Lu

results.title: Transcriptomic Response of Differentiating Porcine Myotubes to Thermal Stress and Donor Piglet Age
results.author: F. Sarais

results.title: Season-dependent effects of elevated temperature on stress biomarkers, energy metabolism and gamete development in mussels.
results.author: M. Mugica

results.title: Thermal stress affects proliferation and differentiation of turkey satellite cells through the mTOR/S6K pathway in a growth-dependent manner
results.author: Jiahui Xu

results.title: Differential effects of temperature and mTOR and Wnt-planar cell polarity pathways on syndecan-4 and CD44 expression in growth-selected turkey satellite cell populations
results.author: Jiahui Xu
results.takeaway: Thermal stress alters SDC4 and CD44 expression in growth-selected turkey satellite cells, potentially impacting muscle development and growth.

results.author: Katharina Metzger

results.title: Temperature Effects on Force and Actin–Myosin Interaction in Muscle: A Look Back on Some Experimental Findings

results.title: The independent effects of heat application on muscle growth program associated mRNA and protein phosphorylation
results.author: M. McGlynn
results.takeaway: Local heat application at rest does not significantly influence gene expression or protein phosphorylation associated with muscle growth program-related markers.

results.title: Thermal conditions experienced during differentiation affect metabolic and contractile phenotypes of mouse myotubes.
results.author: A. Little
results.journal: American journal of physiology. Regulatory, integrative and comparative physiology
results.takeaway: Developing muscle can compensate for cold exposure by increasing metabolic rates, ATP production, and glycolytic flux, complementing central thermoregulation and allowing animals to maintain function in cold environments.

results.author: Yihong Yue

results.journal: Comparative biochemistry and physiology. Part A, Molecular & integrative physiology
results.takeaway: Molt-inhibiting hormone (MIH) in Crustaceans regulates ecdysteroidogenesis through cellular signaling pathways, with calcium potentially playing a role through activation of glandular PDE1.

results.title: Contrasting strategies of osmotic and ionic regulation in freshwater crabs and shrimps: gene expression of gill ion transporters
results.author: Milene Mantovani
results.takeaway: Freshwater crabs and shrimps exhibit distinct osmotic and ionic regulation strategies, with crabs showing a more robust hypo-osmotic ability and shrimps showing a more robust hyper-osmotic ability.

results.title: Crustacean immunity.
results.author: L. Cerenius
results.journal: Advances in experimental medicine and biology
results.takeaway: Recent research on crustacean innate immune mechanisms reveals molecular characterisation of lectins, antiviral reactions, hemocyte formation, differentiation, and regulation of immune pathways.

results.title: The old and new faces of morphology: the legacy of D'Arcy Thompson's ‘theory of transformations' and ‘laws of growth'
results.author: A. Abzhanov
results.takeaway: D'Arcy Thompson's 'laws of growth' suggest that physical forces and internal growth parameters regulate biological forms, explaining the diversity of biological shapes through geometric transformations in morphological space.

results.title: A new framework for growth curve fitting based on the von Bertalanffy Growth Function
results.author: Laura Lee
results.takeaway: The new VBGF framework improves growth predictions and applies to a wider range of taxa, capturing variation in biosynthesis potential scaling and supra-exponential growth.

results.title: Influencing the morphological stability of MOVPE-grown β-Ga2O3 films by O2/Ga ratio
results.author: Ta‐Shun Chou
results.takeaway: MOVPE-grown -Ga2O3 films with low O2/Ga ratios (O2/Ga = 350) exhibit excellent electrical properties, while those with high O2/Ga ratios (O2/Ga = 1250) exhibit surface roughening.

results.title: Nonuniform growth and surface friction determine bacterial biofilm morphology on soft substrates
results.author: Chenyi Fei
results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
results.takeaway: Nonuniform growth and surface friction significantly determine bacterial biofilm morphology on soft substrates, with two distinct wrinkle patterns observed.

results.title: The metabolic interpretation of the von Bertalanffy growth rate
results.author: K. Lika
results.takeaway: The von Bertalanffy Growth Rate (vBGR) is proportional to the volume-specific somatic maintenance rate, linking high maintenance to fast growth in waste-to-hurry strategies.

results.title: A COORDINATE‐FREE APPROACH TO THE ANALYSIS OF GROWTH PATTERNS: MODELS AND THEORETICAL CONSIDERATIONS
results.author: J. Richtsmeier
results.takeaway: This study proposes a coordinate-free method for comparing and modeling growth trajectories in complex morphologies, potentially aiding in the study of morphological evolution and phylogenetic relationships.

results.title: Environment-specificity and universality of the microbial growth law
results.author: Qirun Wang
results.takeaway: The microbial growth law is generally environment-specific, but the growth law curve of Escherichia coli appears universal, with an upward bending in slow-growth conditions.

results.title: Foundations of Morphometrics
results.author: F. Bookstein
results.journal: Annual Review of Ecology, Evolution, and Systematics
results.takeaway: This paper proposes a framework for morphometric methods, aiming to address the lack of methodological introspection in the field and provide a basis for future research.

results.title: Energetic Implications of Morphological Changes between Fish Larval and Juvenile Stages Using Geometric Morphometrics of Body Shape
results.author: Lorena Martínez-Leiva
results.journal: Animals : an Open Access Journal from MDPI
results.takeaway: Larval morphological variability in fish influences metabolism, with smaller differences in respiration rate observed after 54 days post-hatching.

results.title: The universal dynamics of tumor growth.
results.author: A. Brú
results.takeaway: Molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) dynamics, characterized by linear growth, constraint to colony/tumor border, and surface diffusion, are universally observed in all cell colonies, suggesting tumor growth is a competition for space rather than nutrients.

results.title: Joint analysis of 6dFGS and SDSS peculiar velocities for the growth rate of cosmic structure and tests of gravity
results.author: K. Said
results.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
results.takeaway: The growth rate of cosmic structure at low redshift is 0.341  0.024, suggesting a growth index  > 6/11 or a Hubble constant H0 > 70 km s1 Mpc1 or a fluctuation amplitude 8  0.8.

results.title: Mathematical Morphology in Machine Learning
results.author: É. O. Rodrigues

results.title: Unique growth and morphology properties of Clade 5 Clostridioides difficile strains revealed by single-cell time-lapse microscopy
results.author: John W. Ribis

results.title: Part 1. Review and meta‐analysis of studies on modulation of longitudinal bone growth and growth plate activity: A macro‐scale perspective
results.author: Christian R. D’Andrea
results.takeaway: Longitudinal bone growth rate depends on load magnitude, anatomical location, and species, with alterations in growth plate morphology and viability influenced by loading parameters.

results.title: Nucleation-Limited Kinetics of GaAs Nanostructures Grown by Selective Area Epitaxy: Implications for Shape Engineering in Optoelectronics Devices
results.author: Michele Zendrini
results.takeaway: Selective area MOVPE on GaAs substrates allows for shape engineering of GaAs nanostructures, offering new possibilities for optoelectronics and photonic device design.

results.title: Morphology and growth of convective cold pools observed by a dense station network in Germany
results.author: Bastian Kirsch
results.journal: Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society
results.takeaway: Cold-air import by precipitation, through evaporative cooling and convective downdrafts, is the dominant driver of the growth of convective cold pools.

results.title: Association between the morphokinetics of in-vitro-derived bovine embryos and the transcriptomic profile of the derived blastocysts
results.author: S. Yaacobi-Artzi
results.takeaway: The morphokinetics of bovine embryos is associated with the transcriptome profile of derived blastocysts, potentially impacting embryo transfer programs.

results.title: Morphology and logical form
results.author: D. Pesetsky

results.title: Effect of growth velocity on microstructure evolution and properties in DS Ti–47.5Al–3Nb–1.5/3.5Cr
results.author: Chengyi He

results.title: The complexity of porphyrin-like pigments in a marine annelid sheds new light on haem metabolism in aquatic invertebrates
results.author: C. Martins
results.takeaway: Polychaeta marine annelids have two major types of porphyrin-like pigments, yellowish and greenish, that play a key role in UV protection, sensing, and chemical defense against foulants and predators.

results.title: Melanocytes Sense Blue Light and Regulate Pigmentation through Opsin-3.
results.author: Claire Regazzetti
results.takeaway: OPN3 is the key sensor in melanocytes responsible for regulating pigmentation in skin type III and higher, offering potential targets for regulating melanogenesis and protecting dark skins against blue light exposure.

results.title: Mechanism Underlying Light Intensity-Induced Melanin Synthesis of Auricularia heimuer Revealed by Transcriptome Analysis
results.author: Zhiheng Qiu
results.takeaway: High light intensity significantly affects the color of Auricularia heimuer fruiting bodies, with genes involved in light sensing, signal transduction, and melanin synthesis potentially regulating this process.

results.title: NNT mediates redox-dependent pigmentation via a UVB- and MITF-independent mechanism
results.author: J. Allouche
results.takeaway: NNT-modifying topical drugs can target a redox-dependent pigmentation mechanism in skin, potentially benefiting medical and cosmetic purposes.

results.title: Seeing the light to change colour: An evolutionary perspective on the role of melanopsin in neuroendocrine circuits regulating light‐mediated skin pigmentation
results.author: G. Bertolesi
results.takeaway: Melanopsins play a crucial role in regulating light-mediated skin pigmentation, with their evolutionary selection influenced by thermoregulation, ultraviolet protection, background adaptation, and the loss of a photosensitive pineal gland in mammals.

results.title: Interactions between colour-producing mechanisms and their effects on the integumentary colour palette
results.author: M. Shawkey
results.journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences
results.takeaway: Combining pigments and structural integumentary tissues can create colors and optical properties unachievable by either mechanism alone, expanding the animal color palette and highlighting the complexity of color classification.

results.title: Light Induced Changes in Pigment and Lipid Profiles of Bryopsidales Algae
results.author: Chiara E. Giossi
results.takeaway: High light exposure significantly alters pigment composition and lipid profiles in Bryopsidales algae, potentially reducing damage to their photosynthetic apparatus under increased irradiance.

results.title: Molecular delineation of a retina-dependent photoneuroendocrine pathway in zebrafish.
results.author: Krasimir Slanchev
results.takeaway: The retina-dependent photoneuroendocrine pathway in zebrafish allows for dynamic adjustment of body color to the perceived brightness of the ambient background, resulting in a pale or dark appearance.

results.title: Pharmacological induction of skin pigmentation unveils the neuroendocrine circuit regulated by light
results.author: G. Bertolesi
results.takeaway: Pharmacological induction of skin pigmentation and -MSH synthesis reveals a neuroendocrine circuit regulating light-regulated skin color change in invertebrates and lower vertebrates.

results.title: Skin Pigmentation and its Control: From Ultraviolet Radiation to Stem Cells
results.author: J. M. Yardman-Frank
results.takeaway: This review highlights the complex mechanisms of skin pigmentation, including the role of UV radiation, melanocyte stem cells, and potential interventions for pigmentation disorders.

results.title: Physiological and molecular insights into color variation and light intensity adaptation in Eucheuma perplexum with applications for selective cultivation
results.author: Ji-Long Liao
results.takeaway: Eucheuma perplexum red algae adapt to high light by restructuring phycobiliproteins, reducing phycoerythrin content and increasing phenolic compound production, potentially optimizing pigment yields for targeted applications.

results.title: Fish pigmentation and coloration: Molecular mechanisms and aquaculture perspectives
results.author: Mingkun Luo
results.takeaway: This review highlights the importance of understanding cellular and molecular mechanisms in fish coloration, which can be used to enhance body color in aquaculture through single-sex control and molecular marker-assisted breeding.

results.title: The Emerging Role of Visible Light in Melanocyte Biology and Skin Pigmentary Disorders: Friend or Foe?
results.author: Xuanxuan He
results.takeaway: Visible light has complex effects on melanocyte biology and skin pigmentary disorders, with different wavelengths potentially having positive or negative effects depending on interactions with specific chromophores, photoaging, and other photon-mediated reactions.

results.title: Two light‐activated neuroendocrine circuits arising in the eye trigger physiological and morphological pigmentation
results.author: G. Bertolesi
results.takeaway: Eye photoperception links physiological and morphological pigmentation by altering -MSH and melatonin production, respectively.

results.title: Transcriptomics reveals the molecular processes of light-induced rapid darkening of the non-obligate cave dweller Oreolalax rhodostigmatus (Megophryidae, Anura) and their genetic basis of pigmentation strategy
results.author: Wei Zhu
results.takeaway: Rapid morphological color change plays a key role in the light-induced rapid darkening of Oreolalax rhodostigmatus tadpoles, with genetic mutations in MC1R coordinating pigment regression and robust melanogenesis in darkness and light.

results.title: Revealing the synergistic effects of cells, pigments, and light spectra on light transfer during microalgae growth: A comprehensive light attenuation model.
results.author: Shiyan Ma
results.takeaway: The modified Cornet model better explains and predicts light transmission in microalgal suspensions, with blue light attenuation being the most severe, followed by red and green light.

results.title: Melanin’s Journey from Melanocytes to Keratinocytes: Uncovering the Molecular Mechanisms of Melanin Transfer and Processing
results.author: Liliana Bento-Lopes
results.takeaway: Understanding the molecular mechanisms regulating skin pigmentation can lead to novel therapeutic strategies for treating hypo- or hyper-pigmentation disorders and cosmetic applications.

results.title: Light and photosynthetic microalgae: A review of cellular- and molecular-scale optical processes
results.author: A. Lehmuskero
results.takeaway: This review explains the fundamental physical principles behind microalgae optical properties, impacting ocean color, underwater light distribution, and biomass accumulation, and suggests future research directions.

results.title: A transcriptome analysis revealing the molecular mechanism of light intensity-driven color variation in the skin of Chinese giant salamander (Andrias davidianus)
results.author: Zhizhi Jing

results.title: Synthesis and structural characteristics analysis of melanin pigments induced by blue light in Morchella sextelata
results.author: Zhiheng Qiu
results.takeaway: Blue light exposure promotes melanin synthesis and melanization in Morchella sextelata mushrooms, affecting their cap color and highlighting the role of light in color formation.
